Building on this chemical space, a generative strategy was developed in which ligand structures are iteratively mutated, recombined, and selected according to their predicted magnetic properties, while an elitememory mechanism preserves high-performing molecular motifs and guides subsequent generations toward increasingly favorable candidates. This enables targeted exploration of ligand combinations and coordination environments associated with large negative ZFS while simultaneously controlling rhombicity. The generated complexes were subjected to independent CASSCF calculations, including spin–orbit coupling, to directly validate their magnetic properties. Notably, the generative framework identified candidates with strongly enhanced axial anisotropy, including a representative complex exhibiting D ≈ −223 cm-1 after ab initio validation. The validated candidates reproduced the targeted ZFS with deviations of approximately 15–18 cm-1. These results establish a generative, memory-guided route from ligand design to electronically validated magnetic complexes, providing a practical strategy for discovering previously unexplored Co(II) molecular magnets and advancing molecular-magnet design from screening toward property-directed generation.
items.authors: Rajanikanta Rana, Aditya Choudhary, Abhijeet Biswas, Subodh Bhalchandra Rawool, Gopalan Rajaraman

items.title: Bio-derived ionic conductive Guar Gum hydrogels as distributed circuit elements for analogue signal processing: the case of Resistor-Capacitor filters
items.abstract: Developing functional electronic materials from renewable resources is a key challenge toward more sustainable electronics. Here, we report on a bio-derived ionic conductive hydrogel based on guar gum and demonstrate its direct integration as a functional circuit element for analogue signal processing. Ionic conductivity is introduced by incorporating sodium chloride into the polysaccharide matrix and systematically tuned through the glycerol and salt contents. Increasing glycerol loading enhances conductivity, while varying NaCl concentration produces a non-monotonic response, with maximum conductivities in the 10-2 S cm-1 range and an optimum salt-loading window. The conductive formulation is subsequently combined with pristine guar gum, used as a dielectric, to fabricate guar gum-based resistor-capacitor elements. Their integration into low-pass and high-pass filters demonstrates frequency-selective operation in the audio range, with cut-off frequencies of 658 and 576 Hz and transition slopes of −17 and +15 dB dec-1, respectively. These results demonstrate that guar gumbased ionic hydrogels can move beyond conventional roles as substrates or electrolytes and directly perform circuit-level functions, providing a simple materials platform for low-frequency analogue electronics.
items.authors: Yeeun Lee, Emilie Jéhanno, Emmanuel Jacques, Anne-Claire Salaün, Fabien Lucas

items.title: Group-aware validation sharply reduces the apparent accuracy of extraction-category classification in public cannabis laboratory data
items.abstract: Published models that classify cannabis products from cannabinoid and terpene profiles report near-perfect accuracy: above 95% for resin type, 100% for chemovar class. These figures come from random cross-validation or Kennard-Stone partitioning, which hold out no plant, producer or laboratory. We quantify the cost on a task with explicit group structure. On 33,229 public laboratory-result rows for cannabis concentrates that name a producer, nearly all from Nevada, each with a source-declared extraction category (non-solvent against solvent-based), a gradient-boosted classifier scores 78.5% balanced accuracy and a ROC AUC of 0.89 under random five-fold cross-validation. Holding out the producer leaves 54.0% and 0.62. A signal survives: the pooled held-out AUC is 0.61, with a producer-level bootstrap interval of 0.535 to 0.698. But the reported model's pooled balanced accuracy does not separate from chance (51.6%, interval 47.3 to 56.6); it keeps about 30% of its above-chance AUC, and an unweighted logistic regression 41 to 53%. A designed experiment shows the same direction: with the random split averaged over 200 seeds, 162 HPLC-assayed samples fall from 54.3% to 38.9% under leave-one-variety-out with gradient boosting and from 51.8% to 46.3% with logistic regression, against 33.3% chance. In the market data the same profiles identify the producer at 67.1% against a 14.4% baseline and the laboratory at 92.3% against 40.3%. We conclude that the declared extraction category is only weakly recoverable from these analyte panels for an unseen producer, and that a random split overstates it by 8 to 26 points of balanced accuracy depending on the model and subset. We did not rerun the published studies.
items.authors: Arthur Gonçalves Breguez

items.title: Metalsurfer: Fast Generation of Realistic Substrate-Adsorbate Interfaces
items.abstract: Realistic adsorbate–substrate geometries are essential for meaningful electronic-structure calculations at interfaces, yet constructing them remains slow and generally ad hoc for bulky molecules, high coverages, and irregular surfaces. This challenge limits systematic exploration of adsorption configurations across many problems in catalysis, surface chemistry, and materials design. We introduce metalsurfer, a Python package that generates density functional theory (DFT)-ready interface models from simplified molecular input line-entry system (SMILES) strings and a substrate. The workflow combines chemistry-aware, CPU-parallel placement enumeration with TorchSim GPU-batched relaxation under a machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP), molecular integrity filters, sequential coverage growth, and optional Bayesian acquisition. We demonstrate these capabilities on three chemically distinct systems. For camphor on Cu(111), a ∼1.2 h search recovers neighbors to all eight published weak-adsorption minima and provides a set of plausible basins for refinement. For bipyridine on defected Au(111), offline fixed-batch replays on saved saturation pools show that probability-of-improvement acquisition identifies the first committed motif much faster than random sampling. Transfer from earlier coverage steps also accelerates later searches, with a trust gate that can fall back to a cold model if the prior fails current-step validation. For CO/Pt(111), fixed-coverage n-tuplet searches locate all four ordered adlayers reported in the literature. In each case, a few hours of GPU screening produce a compact shortlist for DFT refinement. metalsurfer thus provides a practical route through the combinatorial problem of interface construction.
items.authors: Jorge Gonzalo, Jorge Felez, Julen Munarriz, Ruben Laplaza

items.title: First-principles analysis of the metal-free H2 dissociation mechanism by semiquinone radicals in mitochondrial Complex I and III
items.authors: Toru Ishibashi, Enjuro Harunari

items.title: Automated Extraction and FAIRification of Chemical Structures from Scientific Publications
items.abstract: Chemical structures are published predominantly as images, which makes them inaccessible for database indexing, structure-based search and computational reuse. While Optical Chemical Structure Recognition and PDF-extraction tools attempt post-publication recovery, they cannot restore the information lost during image rendering. To address this, we present BChemXtract, an open-source Java library that extracts chemical structures directly from the CDX and CDXML files that authors already submit with their manuscripts. BChemXtract parses the CDX object hierarchy to isolate chemical fragments from graphical annotations and expands abbreviations using a community-curated lookup table. The structures are then converted via the Chemistry Development Kit into standard machine-readable formats. BChemXtract is integrated into the production workflow of the Beilstein Journals, where extracted structures are manually validated before being embedded in article metadata as Schema.org JSON-LD, deposited in PubChem and offered for download. Applied to the 2993 ChemDraw figures and schemes of volume 20 of the Beilstein Journal of Organic Chemistry, it yielded 23,320 structures with InChIs in under two minutes. On a 225-file benchmark corpus, it generated valid InChIs for 98.2% of extracted unique substances, compared with 14.2% for Open Babel, at comparable per-file speed. BChemXtract makes published chemistry FAIR at the point of publication without altering author workflows. It is available under the MIT license together with a web application and the benchmark corpus.
items.authors: Felix Bänsch, Kohulan Rajan, Markus Nietfeld

items.title: MolSanitizer: An open-source pipeline to prepare small-molecule databases for large-scale virtual screening
items.abstract: Accurate preparation of small-molecule databases for virtual screening is crucial for the success of computer-aided drug discovery. Although numerous free software options are available, they often underperform compared to commercial alternatives. Here, we introduce MolSanitizer, an open-source molecular preparation pipeline built on RDKit and designed for large-scale virtual screening. MolSanitizer extends existing open-source functionality through curated, chemical-environment-aware rules for protonation and tautomerization, systematic stereoisomer enumeration, and a dedicated conformer generator that combines knowledge-based structural preferences with stochastic torsional sampling. Our benchmarking results show that MolSanitizer achieves better performance than several free software alternatives while achieving performance levels comparable to commercial software. MolSanitizer features a modular and open-source design, allowing users to easily customize the tool to meet their specific needs. MolSanitizer also generates output files compatible with several widely used molecular docking programs, thereby facilitating a streamlined workflow for users. MolSanitizer is available for free at https://github.com/carlssonlab/MolSanitizer and via a web server at https://carlssonlabtools.icm.uu.se/molsani.
items.authors: Thua-Phong Lam, Szymon Pach, Philip Ullmann, Hocine El Khaoudi Enyoury, Ruth Brenk, Flavio Ballante

items.title: Structural Convergence of MD simulations on RNA Motifs: A tRNA case study
items.abstract: A detailed understanding of the structural dynamics of diverse RNA architectures is critical for elucidating the chemical basis of cellular function and expanding the use of RNA in medicine and biotechnology. While classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can provide this much-needed atomic information, sampling requirements remain poorly characterized for RNA systems. In the present study, we compared the conformational ensemble sampled by five independent 5 μs trajectories and 60 independent 500 ns replicas for unmodified Escherichia coli tRNAPhe under three (monovalent, crystallographic-Mg2+, and 6 Mg2+) environmental conditions, yielding 165 μs of aggregate sampling. Although the global L-shaped tRNA fold was retained across all simulations, structural convergence was strongly motif-dependent. Mean base-pair and base-step descriptors of the rigid acceptor and anticodon stem-loop duplex regions were reproduced with modest replication across metal environments. In contrast, the dynamic anticodon loop exhibited substantial trajectory-to-trajectory heterogeneity. A stacking-based analysis identified diverse loop conformations with counterparts in experimentally determined tRNA structures, showing that ensembles of independent classical MD replicas can sample diverse experimentally observed conformations without enhanced sampling. While fewer long trajectories incompletely sampled the heterogeneous loop conformational space, ensembles of many shorter replicas are key to exploring the conformational dynamics of RNA motifs like hairpins. Inclusion of Mg2+ also shifted the sampled conformational ensemble, underscoring the importance of mimicking the experimentally-relevant ionic environment. Overall, our findings offer practical guidelines for MD simulation setup, including trajectory length, replica number, and divalent ion conditions, for studies of RNA systems featuring similar tertiary architectures.
items.authors: Austin Pounder, Mark J. Lea, Umer Yaqoob, Zaki Olvis, Cynthia Fonderson, Ute Kothe

items.title: Indium-Catalyzed Deaminative Coupling of Propargylamines with Terminal Alkynes: A Mild Approach to Conjugated 1,3-Dienones
items.abstract: A mild and efficient indium-catalyzed coupling of propargylamines with terminal alkynes has been developed, affording a diverse array of conjugated 1,3-dienones in good to excellent yields. The reaction proceeds via in situ hydrolysis of propargylamines to generate the corresponding enones, followed by an indium(III)-promoted syn-selective alkyne insertion. Using InCl3 as the catalyst and DBU as the base, the protocol features broad functional-group tolerance and operates under mild conditions. Mechanistic investigations indicate that indium activation is crucial for facilitating the addition of alkynes to enones, enabling selective construction of conjugated 1,3-dienones frameworks. This transformation represents a rare example of indium-catalyzed C–C bond formation and provides a practical and versatile approach to structurally diverse 1,3-dienones from readily available propargylamine precursors.
items.authors: Yujuan Xie, Liliang Huang, Huangdi Feng, Erik V. Van der Eycken

items.title: Depth-resolved operando grazing-incidence diffraction reveals non-equilibrium Cu-Pt alloy restructuring under glycerol electrooxidation
items.abstract: Alloying Pt with Cu enhances activity towards hydrogen generation and valueadded products during the electrooxidation of glycerol, but the most active alloys typically require electrochemical activation, during which their structure and composition evolve in poorly understood ways. Here we use synchrotron-based operando, angle-dependent grazing incidence X-ray diffraction in a custom dual-chamber electrochemical flow cell to follow, in real time, the depth-resolved structural evolution of Cu-Pt thin-film catalysts under glycerol electrooxidation in alkaline media. Our approach allows us to monitor the temporal evolution of lattice parameter, phase composition and microstrain during cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry while varying the X-ray penetration depth from the topmost tens of nanometres into the underlying alloy. For Cu-rich Cu92Pt8 catalysts, we observe substantial restructuring of the near-surface region, including the cyclic formation and reduction of Cu2O, pronounced Cu leaching from depths of several tens of nanometres, and the progressive emergence of a Pt-rich ≈Cu15Pt85 phase that stabilises the surface against further oxidation. These structural changes coincide with a ca. 5-fold increase in current density and a ca. 100 mV increase in onset potential during activation, after which the electrochemical response becomes stable. Pt-richer alloys exhibit markedly reduced restructuring, with compositional changes largely confined to the top ≈20-30 nm of the catalyst. Analysis of peak broadening via Williamson-Hall plots reveals that dealloying and surface oxidation are associated with increased microstrain, which subsequently relaxes as a Pt-rich surface configuration is established. Beyond revealing the non-equilibrium interplay of oxidation, segregation and realloying that governs the performance and durability of Cu-Pt catalysts for glycerol electrooxidation, our methodology and cell design provide a flexible, broadly applicable platform for operando, depth-resolved diffraction studies of electrochemical interfaces in energy and biomass-conversion reactions.
items.authors: Athira Anil, Martin Kapuscinski, Harish Gudla, Prabahar Kuppamuthu, Irina Terekhina, Priyanka Nehla

items.title: Development of A Modeling Framework for Characterizing Protein–Polymer Bioconjugates with Enhanced Sampling Molecular Dynamics Simulations
items.abstract: Protein–polymer bioconjugates represent a class of biomaterials that leverages the molecular specificity of proteins and the tunability of synthetic polymers. Strategic conjugation of polymers to protein surfaces can enhance key biomolecular properties such as structural stability and target affinity while preserving the biological functions of the native protein. The rational design of these hybrid biomolecules demands a detailed understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms governing protein–polymer interfacial behavior. Critically, strong interfacial interactions can impose substantial energetic barriers that hinder conformational sampling in molecular dynamics (MD) studies of this system. Enhanced sampling methods are highly effective for overcoming such limitations in the simulation of biomolecular interfaces. However, the opportunity to apply enhanced sampling methods toward navigating the complex interfacial landscapes of protein–polymer bioconjugates has yet to be realized by the field. In this study, we showcase the development of a molecular modeling framework that leverages enhanced sampling to extensively characterize protein–polymer bioconjugates. To validate this framework, we constructed two bioconjugate models of hen egg-white lysozyme grafted with activated methoxy polyethylene glycol (mPEG) chains of varying lengths at multiple surface-exposed lysine sites. We then performed all-atom MD simulations of these PEGylated constructs, augmented with well-tempered metadynamics (WTM) to fully explore their conformational landscapes under multi-site polymer conjugation. This approach yielded converged free energy surfaces (FES) characterizing the thermodynamic favorability of grafted mPEG chain conformations at each conjugation site. We also identified key protein contact residues and site-specific non-bonded interactions responsible for bioconjugate stabilization. This study demonstrates a novel application of enhanced sampling methodologies in bioconjugate systems for characterizing site-specific conjugation effects on protein–polymer interfacial energetics and structural dynamics in the context of protein surface chemistry. More broadly, applying this methodological framework across diverse polymer chemistries and protein variants can elucidate molecular design rules for engineering bioconjugates with precise properties and functions for applications spanning biotechnology, energy, and health.
items.authors: Ziyue Dong, Aidan B. Wegner, David Saeb, Matthew M. C. Kwan, Pedro E. Cintrón Baerga, C. Wyatt Shields

items.title: Quantitative Characterization of Pharmaceutical Powder Surface Interactions Using Inverse Gas Chromatography-Derived Surface Energy Profiles
items.abstract: Quantitative characterization of surface and interfacial properties is important for understanding the behavior of pharmaceutical powders, but conventional approaches to powder wettability and surface free energy can be influenced by measurement procedures and sample-specific factors. Inverse gas chromatography (IGC) provides a sensitive approach for characterizing powder surface energetics as a function of fractional surface coverage; however, the reproducibility and interpretation of IGC-derived surface energy profiles require careful evaluation. In this study, the reproducibility of IGC-derived surface energy profiles was examined using pharmaceutical excipients, and the resulting energetic characteristics were compared with wettability measurements obtained using sessile drop and Washburn methods. Surface-energy profiles were further used to calculate thermodynamic work-of-adhesion profiles for powder–water interactions and for drug–excipient systems. Distinct differences in surface-energy profiles were observed among pharmaceutical excipients, including materials with identical nominal chemical compositions but different grades. Drug–excipient work-of-adhesion profiles further demonstrated coverage-dependent differences in calculated interfacial interactions among pharmaceutical materials. The results demonstrate that IGC-derived surface-energy profiles can provide reproducible characterization of pharmaceutical powder surfaces and can be extended to quantitative evaluation of solid–liquid and solid–solid interfacial interactions. These findings support the use of surface-energy profiles as a quantitative framework for characterization of pharmaceutical powders and for comparison of potential interfacial interactions among formulation components.
items.authors: Ken Yoshioka, Kohei Tahara

items.title: VISION-BASED DRY-MATERIAL INVENTORY ESTIMATION IN AUTONOMOUS LABORATORIES: RGB SEGMENTATION VERSUS RGB-D SURFACE RECONSTRUCTION
items.abstract: Reliable dry-material inventory monitoring is needed for autonomous laboratory operation, but the suitability of a non-contact method depends on material behaviour, optical access, calibration requirements and the quantity to be estimated. We compared two vision-based approaches—material-specific RGB/YOLO level estimation and visible-surface reconstruction from an Intel RealSense D405—across three materials (black polypropylene pellets, wood powder, and microcrystalline cellulose fine powder) in small transparent laboratory tubes representative of common dosing instruments, with the aim of informing a practical, evidence-based framework for choosing between such methods in laboratory automation and similar industrial contexts. Software-coordinated records linked the two camera channels to a nominal mass-fraction inventory reference and a manual-height baseline. Across six runs and 133 paired, reference-eligible material states, D405 achieved lower error than YOLO in every run (mean absolute error of 3.26 vs. 7.14 percentage points), though YOLO offered higher valid-result coverage (97.2% vs. 95.1%). Both methods showed increased error under repeated surface disturbance, with YOLO degrading more sharply than D405. An exploratory correction fitted using the first observation at each mass level substantially improved YOLO but did not surpass D405’s uncorrected accuracy, while a single global correction worsened both methods—indicating that simple corrections do not transfer robustly across conditions. The results support a method-selection framework based on error, availability, viewing geometry, calibration-state representativeness and total resource requirements. Conclusions are limited to the tested materials and setups, and the mass-fraction reference is an operational inventory proxy rather than a direct measurement of true occupied volume.
items.authors: Mostafa Abd Al Kader, Miguel Hernández-del-Valle, Maciej Haranczyk

items.title: Chemically modified hydrogels to improve geothermal reservoir performance by enabling flow control via size-shifting microspheres
items.abstract: Thermal short circuits, where fluids preferentially connect injection and production wells, are a leading cause of premature enthalpy decline in geothermal reservoirs. These pathways accelerate cooling, reduce effective heat transfer area, and limit reservoir lifetime. We propose a temperature-responsive hydrogel microsphere suspension as an “active tracer” that dynamically redirects flow away from cooled short-circuit channels while also tracing fluid flow via fluorescence spectroscopy. Highly idealized reservoir simulations with field-informed permeability distributions indicate that a yieldstress fluid with temperature-responsive behaviors may improve reservoir thermal lifetime by a factor of at least 24 to 59x while maintaining acceptable hydraulic performance. To develop a candidate “active” tracer intended to satisfy the assumptions of the idealized simulations, we synthesized poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (pNIPA) microgels, characterized their swelling and rheological behavior, and conducted a large-scale laboratory experiment in an analog parallel-plate that demonstrates short-circuited flow behavior. These lab-scale results demonstrate that injected microgels clog cooled short circuits via swelling and diverted flow into hotter regions. This proof-of-concept establishes an attractive pathway for employing engineered materials to actively manage flow and extend geothermal reservoir lifetimes.
items.authors: Aaron M. Baxter, Danni Tang, Bryan H. Abdulaziz, Reeby J. Puthur, Patrick M. Fulton, Sarah Hormozi

items.title: Tyr10 Modifications and Peptide Context Rewire GLP-1 Modulation of Amyloid-β42 Assembly
items.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is best known as a receptor agonist, yet its peptide-level behavior in protein-rich environments remains poorly defined. Here, a GLP-1-directed photoaffinity probe recovered a predefined Aβ42 spike-in from cell lysates, while endogenous actin and α-synuclein were detected in the recovered fractions. This observation motivated chemically defined assembly studies with the actinlinked β-thymosin reference TMSB4Y. Thioflavin T (ThT) kinetics and endpoint electron microscopy (EM) revealed no single pro- or antiassembly response. GLP-1 advanced the ThT-positive transition of Tyr10-unmodified Aβ42, whereas TMSB4Y attenuated it. Phosphorylation or nitration at Tyr10 changed both the direction and timing of these effects, and GLP-1 added after assembly had begun redirected established trajectories in a Tyr10-modification-dependent manner. Ser18 O-GlcNAcylation of GLP-1 provided an orthogonal perturbation, suppressing the Tyr10-unmodified response while enhancing the nitrated trajectory and delaying the phosphorylated one. Together, capture in a complex protein background and assembly in defined mixtures identify GLP-1 as a context-sensitive modulator of Aβ42 assembly rather than a fixed promoter or inhibitor.
items.authors: Pritam Ghosh

items.title: First-principles data for solid-solution Nb–Zr, Ta–Zr, and V–Zr binary alloys with body-centered-cubic structures
items.abstract: We present three open-access datasets containing density functional theory (DFT) calculations for refractory solid-solution binary alloys niobium–zirconium (NbZr), tantalum–zirconium (TaZr), and vanadium–zirconium (VZr) in 128-atom body-centered-cubic (BCC) supercells. These datasets extend our previously published first-principles collections for NbTa, NbV, TaV, and NbTaV alloys and were generated with the same automated high-throughput workflow based on the Vienna Ab-Initio Simulation Package (VASP). For each of the three NbZr, TaZr, and VZr systems, we uniformly sample 31 chemical compositions across the full composition range in 4-atom increments. For every composition we construct 100 distinct disordered atomic configurations by randomizing the element assignments on the BCC lattice sites. All structures are fully relaxed, and the released data include complete input files, detailed VASP outputs for each relaxation stage, and derived physical quantities such as ground-state formation energy and root mean-squared displacement (RMSD) relative to an ideal BCC reference. These Zr-containing binaries are motivated by our earlier demonstration that graph neural networks (GNNs) trained on binary NbTa, NbV, and TaV data can interpolate formation enthalpies and structural descriptors in ternary NbTaV alloys while dramatically reducing the required number of ternary DFT calculations. The new NbZr, TaZr, and VZr datasets increase the diversity of available binary training data, in particular in systems with larger size mismatch and stronger lattice distortion due to Zr, and are intended to support the development of transferable machine learning (ML) interatomic models for accelerated exploration of high-dimensional multicomponent alloy spaces.
items.authors: Massimiliano Lupo Pasini, German Samolyuk, Jong Youl Choi, David Rogers, Ying Yang

items.title: Origin of the Difference between Kohn-Sham and ∆SCF Band gaps for Delocalized Electron–Hole Excitations in Hybrid-Functional Supercell Calculations
items.abstract: We examine the relationship between ground-state generalized Kohn–Sham (GKS) band gaps and self-consistent ∆SCF excitation energies for delocalized electron–hole excitations in finite periodic supercells. For a vertical excitation at the undistorted ground-state geometry, these two quantities are expected to coincide when the promoted electron and hole remain Bloch-like. This is mostly true with semilocal functionals, but not with hybrid functionals for which the difference increases linearly with the fraction of exact exchange. The origin of this difference is derived from two equivalent viewpoints: the total-energy change associated with the ∆SCF excitation and the occupation-dependent orbital gap shift arising from the self-consistent potential response. The residual energy arises from the orbital-dependent exact-exchange selfenergy associated with the electron-hole pair and decreases approximately as 1/N
items.authors: Mingxue Fu, Arghya Bhowmik, Juan Maŕıa Garćıa-Lastra

items.title: Earth-abundant 3d metal-catalyzed enantioselective catalysis towards the functionalization of E/Zalkenes mixtures.
items.abstract: Enantioselective catalysis transforming alkenes to chiral molecules have been a breakthrough in the field of organic synthesis. Though a major challenge persists. The “privileged” chiral catalyst capacities depend on the geometry of the olefin substrate which can be either E or Z. Enantioselective catalysis allowing to convert both alkene stereoisomers to a single chiral molecule promises sustainable synthetic routes and novel mechanistic strategies towards chiral molecule synthesis. Enantioselective methods towards the functionalization of E/Z-alkenes, which has largely taken advantages of the recent development of earth-abundant 3d metal catalysis, are covered in this revue. An emphasis on the mechanisms accounting for the observed stereoconvergence and enantioselectivity is proposed.
items.authors: Guillaume Delestras, John Henry Reed, Coralie Duchemin

items.title: Selective Ligand Replacement Leads to Carbene Complexes as Catalysts in Proteins
items.abstract: Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) that incorporate organometallic fragments through direct metal–protein coordination open the door to unlock the full evolutionary potential of the protein scaffold to modulate catalysis. This work builds on our previously published work, in which Ru(II) piano stool complexes bearing bipyridyl ligands were used to deliver [Ru(Arene)]2+ fragments into a naïve protein scaffold, generating a transfer-hydrogenase artificial metalloenzyme. Here we systematically explore Ru(II) piano stool complexes bearing pyridyl–N-heterocyclic carbene (Pyr–NHC) bidentate ligands as active-site precursors for metathases and transfer hydrogenases. In this work we describe the synthesis and characterisation of five novel Ru(II) piano stool complexes bearing a hexamethylbenzene (HMB) arene cap and Pyr–NHC bidentate ligands, in which systematic variation of the NHC wingtip substituent (R′ = Me, Et, iPr, Ph) and the pyridine ring substituent (R = H, F) tunes the steric and electronic properties of the complex. Single-crystal X-ray analysis and electrochemical studies show that the strong σ-donation from the carbene lowers the Ru(II/III) redox potential and elongates the Ru–HMB bond relative to their bipyridyl counterparts. This supports displacement of the arene as opposed to the bidentate ligand in the presence of protein. Systematic comparison between Pyr–NHC and bipyridyl complexes also provided an insight into the influence of the arene and the bidentate ligand on the structural and electrochemical properties of these complexes.
items.authors: Armando Albert Flores, Matthew G. Wheeler, Oskar James Klein, George S. Biggs, Jonathan Shaw, Jonathan Bostock

items.title: Hydrogenolysis of N-Cbz-Protected Amines Mediated by Spherical SiliaCat Pd(0)
items.abstract: The deprotection reaction of N-benzyloxycarbonyl (N-Cbz)-protected amino groups in organic compounds can be efficiently achieved by hydrogenolysis mediated by the sol-gel-entrapped spherical catalyst SiliaCat Pd(0). The heterogeneous catalyst combines high catalytic activity and chemoselectivity with low Pd loading, a nonpyrophoric nature, and excellent reusability. Investigation of the effects of solvent, substrate concentration, Pd loading, temperature, and catalyst particle size revealed that 100 µm spherical SiliaCat Pd(0) provides a favorable balance between rapid reaction kinetics and practical catalyst properties for batch applications. The catalyst was successfully reused over ten consecutive reaction runs, maintaining complete conversion and high isolated yields. A broad substrate scope was demonstrated, with tolerance toward methyl esters, Boc-protected amines, pinacol boronate esters, and an aliphatic bromide, while debromination of an aryl bromide revealed a limitation of the method. Comparison of the 100 µm spherical sol-gel catalyst with several commercial heterogeneous Pd catalysts demonstrates its high catalytic activity and selectivity under mild reaction conditions.
items.authors: Valerica Pandarus, Samuel Cashman-Kadri, Rosaria Ciriminna, François Béland, Mario Pagliaro

items.title: From Static Material Design to Predictive Open-Loop Control via Chemistry–Architecture Coupling in a Moving-Boundary Reaction–Diffusion Framework
items.authors: Andualem Belachew Workie

items.title: Pd-catalyzed Cycloadditions of 5-Vinyloxazolidine-2,4-diones: A Diastereo- and Enantioselective Access to Spirooxindoles
items.abstract: In this manuscript, we report a straightforward route to spirooxindoles by Pd-catalyzed cycloadditions of 5-vinyloxazolidine-2,4-diones with isatins. After a screening of chiral ligands, DTBM-SEGPHOS was selected to induce high diastereo- and enantiocontrol of the two newly created tetrasubstituted stereocenters. Our investigation demonstrated broad functional group tolerance under the reaction conditions. Overall, this work represents a rare example of Pd-catalyzed cycloadditions involving 5- vinyloxazolidine-2,4-diones and electrophilic C=O bonds.
items.authors: Xavier Xancho, Pinar Yildirim, Nicolas Casaretto, Alexis Archambeau

items.title: Designing organic photoredox catalysts as a fragment-based puzzle solved by reinforcement learning
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a promising strategy for identifying optimal solutions in vast search spaces. We have developed a framework in which the design of organic photoredox catalysts (OPCs) is deliberately formulated as a fragment-based puzzle that is well suited to RL. In this framework, an RL agent sequentially selects and orders molecular fragments and attempts to identify fragment combinations that afford high rewards, as calculated based on the similarity between the properties of the generated molecules and those of 4CzIPN, a well-known OPC. In addition to the rediscovery of a previously reported high-performance OPC, experimental validation of the proposed candidates revealed a TADF emitter with redox potentials similar to those of 4CzIPN, as well as an OPC with superior catalytic activity in several photoreactions.
items.authors: Naoki Noto, Mayu Hirakata, Mikito Fujinami, Yusuke Masuda, Ryosuke Kojima, Yasunori Matsui

items.title: QMzyme: A Python Package for Automated and Systematic QM-based Enzyme Modeling
items.abstract: We introduce QMzyme, a Python package to automate the generation of Quantum mechanics (QM)-based enzyme models. QM calculations on enzymes are computationally challenging because full enzyme systems typically contain thousands of atoms, placing accurate QM treatments beyond practical computational limits.Therefore, QM-based enzyme studies rely on identifying a subset of atoms that captures the essential chemistry of the reaction environment, enabling tractable yet chemically meaningful calculations. However, constructing these reduced models requires numerous user-defined decisions, including selection of the starting structure, identification of atoms to include in the QM region, and definition of truncation strategies for QM-only models, all of which can substantially influence the resulting calculations. QMzyme aims to provide the community with a flexible and extensible framework for automated, systematic generation of QM-based enzyme models, enabling researchers to more rigorously evaluate how model construction decisions influence computational outcomes while improving reproducibility and transparency across workflows. By facilitating high-throughput generation and analysis of QM enzyme models, QMzyme supports largescale, data-driven investigations of enzyme structure, function, and reactivity. This effort is especially crucial for the creation of large, chemically consistent datasets that can support emergent artificial intelligence and machine learning approaches for accelerated digital discovery in enzymology and biocatalysis.
items.authors: Arkanil Roy, Young Woo Kim, Heidi Klem

items.title: Birefringence Breaks Symmetry-Protected Fluorescence Trapping in Laser-Cooled Crystals
items.abstract: Total internal reflection traps light inside high-index emitters, and in laser-cooled crystals the trapped fluorescence limits how far purification lowers the parasitic heat load. The symmetry of the crystal shape is known to govern this trapping. Here we show that the dielectric tensor supplies a second, intrinsic symmetry, and we unify the geometric and dielectric symmetries in a single conservation law. A fluorescence photon stays trapped when every facet operation conserves a wave-vector component that keeps it inside total internal reflection. Mirror facets of a cuboid conserve three components and trap 17.2% of all directions. Brewster end facets, or mode conversion between ordinary and extraordinary waves at facets containing the optic axis of uniaxial Yb:YLF, leave one component and reduce the trapped set to a universal shell of 3.45% of directions. Sub-degree misorientation of the optic axis, subnanometer facet roughness or an asymmetric cut releases this shell, and the release rate determines how strongly purification lowers parasitic loss. Released Yb:YLF crystals keep nearly linear purity leverage at 77 K and tolerate about ten times more cold background and up to 240 times more facet absorption than the same crystals with mode-conserving reflection. Birefringence releases trapped light on the smoothest facets, where surface absorption is lowest. Crystal symmetry, set jointly by shape and dielectric tensor, thereby becomes a design parameter for optical refrigeration toward liquid-nitrogen temperature and for uniaxial scintillators, light-emitting diodes and other facet-bounded emitters that trap light by total internal reflection.
items.authors: Daqian Bian, Yuzhi Xu

items.title: Unveiling Photoluminescent N-Heterocyclic Silylene-Silver(I) Amides as Dual-Function Photosensitizers and Third-Harmonic Generators
items.abstract: N-Heterocyclic silylenes (NHSis) have evolved from laboratory curiosities to versatile ligands for small-molecule activation and homogeneous catalysis, yet their potential in photophysics and optical materials remains unexplored. Here, we report for the first time a series of luminescent NHSi-ligated Ag(I) amide complexes (2–4) exhibiting remarkable thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) and dual-emissive behavior. The NHSi→Ag–diphenylamine complex (2) displays pronounced TADF with an exceptionally small singlet–triplet energy gap (ΔES–T ≈ 0.006 eV) and a short delayed-fluorescence lifetime (τTADF ≈ 0.35 μs at 300 K), indicative of efficient reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) driven by NHSi-to-metal amide charge transfer. Complexes 3 and 4 exhibit dual emission and serve as efficient photosensitizers for singlet oxygen (1O2) generation. Remarkably, these complexes (2-4) demonstrate coherent photon up-conversion via third-harmonic generation (THG), representing the first such observation in main-group organometallic chemistry. These findings unveil a new class of main-group metal complexes as promising photosensitizers and third-order nonlinear optical materials.
items.authors: Moushakhi Ghosh, Abhijit Chatterjee, Prakash Panwaria, Riteeka Tanwar, K. S. Ananthram, Rishukumar Panday

items.title: Machine Learning of Methacrylated Dextran Phase Separation for Prediction, Transferability, and Adaptation
items.abstract: Thermoresponsive polymers are promising materials for separations, sensing, drug delivery, and other biomedical applications, but their phase behavior depends on numerous polymer and solution variables, which creates a formulation space that is impractical to explore exhaustively by experiments. Here, we develop machine-learning (ML) models for predicting the lower critical solution temperature (LCST) of methacrylated dextran (Dex-MA), a biocompatible polysaccharide-based polymer, using 403 unique experimentally measured formulations spanning polymer molecular weight, degree of methacrylation, concentration, salts, surfactants, and other additives. The dataset is nonuniformly sampled because of practical synthesis constraints and application priorities. Despite this nonuniformity, descriptor-and molecular-embedding-based XGBoost and multilayer perceptron (MLP) models achieved mean absolute errors of 3.6 o C to 3.7 o C and 5.4 o C to 5.7 o C, respectively, for within-domain LCST prediction and mean phase-behavior classification accuracies of 89.4–89.6% and 85.3–86.6%, respectively. However, strong within-domain performance did not uniformly transfer to unseen formulation domains. Systematically withholding entire polymer, surfactant, and salt domains produced domain-dependent losses in predictive accuracy; for example, withholding 86 and 250 kDa Dex-MA increased LCST prediction errors to 11.4 o C and 17.5 o C, respectively, whereas errors for held-out surfactants were 5.6–7.2 o C. Progressive incorporation of target-domain measurements recovered predictive accuracy, but the recovery rate varied substantially with additive and salt identity and polymer molecular weight. This work provides a framework not only for predicting thermoresponsive-polymer phase behavior but also for evaluating model transferability to new formulation domains and guiding experimental data collection for model adaptation.
items.authors: Jordan Carden, Erfan Moaseri, Elizabeth Roberge, Linqing Li, Yaxin An

items.title: A Redox-Non-Innocent Catecholate Shifts the Oxidation State Break in the Actinides
items.abstract: Realizing the full potential of actinide-based systems requires strategies to differentiate elements whose similar chemical properties complicate their selective use. Redox-active ligands offer a promising approach: their ability to participate in electron transfer provides a means to tune the oxidation states and electronic structures of both lanthanides and actinides. To explore this approach, we conducted a theory-guided study of (Tp*)2An(dtbsq) complexes (1-An; An = U, Np, Pu, Am, Bk; Tp* = [HB(C3N2Me2H)3]-; dtbsq•− = [C6O2 tBu2H2]-), which contain a redox-active semiquinone ligand. This study reveals a shift in the preferred actinide oxidation state from An(IV) to An(III) between the chemically similar elements Np and Pu. Such an effect is made possible due to differential stabilization of oxidation states by the ligated redox-active ligand. Structural and spectroscopic data are consistent with this trend, as exemplified by the experimentally characterized complexes 2-U ([(Tp*)(Bp*)UIV 2(dtbc)3], Bp* = [H2B(C3N2Me2H)2]-, dtbc = [C6O2 tBu2H2]2-) and 1-Pu [(Tp*)2PuIII(dtbsq)]. In these systems, the radical ligand is reduced to a catecholate only in the presence of UIII but it remains in its radical form with PuIII. Electronicstructure calculations for (Tp*)2An(dtbsq) (An = U, Np, Pu, Am, Bk) reveal tunable AnIII/IV oxidation states—supported by highly multiconfigurational ground states—and oxidation-statedependent covalency. This study advances our fundamental understanding of actinide bonding and highlights oxidation-state control as a promising strategy for tuning reactivity and selectivity across f-block chemistry.
items.authors: David J. Fiszbein, Maria J. Beltran-Leiva, Mikaela M. Pyrch, Enrique R. Batista, Polly L. Arnold, Ping Yang

items.title: Research Progress and Applications of the Fundamental Principles of Soft Ionization Mass Spectrometry
items.abstract: (1. Guangdong Huisheng Testing Technology Co., Ltd.) Abstract: Soft ionization mass spectrometry is widely applied in fields such as pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, environmental monitoring, and food safety; however, its fundamental principles remain subject to considerable debate, rendering it a "black-box" technology. This review summarizes the basic principles of electrospray ionization (ESI), matrix-assisted laser desorption (MALDI), and desorption electrospray ionization (DESI), and establishes "one theory, two equations, and three instruments" as the theoretical and practical foundation for soft ionization mass spectrometry. Furthermore, this study discusses the electromagnetic applications of soft ionization mass spectrometry, thereby expanding its scope of research and application.
items.authors: jiehong Luo, luo jiehong

items.title: Mixed Ionic–Electronic Memory in a Conjugated Polymer Composite for Retrospective Optical Event Reconstruction
items.abstract: Coupling a light-responsive conjugated polymer to an ionic matrix and oxide interfaces offers a materials strategy for retaining complementary information about completed optical events. A PEDOT:PSS/Nafion/TiO 2 composite implements this approach through an irradiance-dependent conductance amplitude and a wavelength-dependent fading trajectory. At matched nominal polymer loading, TiO 2 incorporation reduces the light-OFF amplitude by 70–77% while extending the half-decay time by 1.56–2.01-fold. Post-illumination optical spectra reveal persistent, composition-dependent changes consistent with electronic-state redistribution coupled to slower matrix and interfacial relaxation. The peak conductance change remains linear with irradiance over 10–40 mW cm −2 (R 2 = 0.9981–0.9993), enabling 91.7% leave-one-condition-out wavelength accuracy and an irradiance mean absolute error of 0.86 mW cm −2 . Same-batch devices show strong kinetic fidelity (median relaxationtime coefficient of variation = 10.02%), but zero-shot transfer to a device from an independently prepared batch fell to 58.3% wavelength accuracy (7/12; p = 0.066 versus three-class chance), making cross-batch kinetic variability the principal barrier to calibration-free transfer. With readout delay withheld, 50 s segments yield 88% wavelength accuracy and a conditional event-age error of 5.5 s. This work demonstrates retrospective decoding of completed optical events in a conjugated polymer composite. A stored conductance peak and a post-illumination relaxation trajectory enable calibrated reconstruction of irradiance, wavelength, and elapsed event age.
items.authors: Md Al Raihan, Tian Xia, Michael S. Freund

items.title: The Pnictogen Oracle Provider: Multi-Fidelity Graph Landscapes To Benchmark Molecular Optimization
items.abstract: The informed discovery and inverse design of new molecules and materials is among the most active applications of data-driven procedures, such as statistical learning, to chemical problems. These approaches involve two key aspects: the dataset, and the exploration algorithms. Here, we cover both of these dimensions by introducing POP (Pnictogen Oracle Provider), a platform comprised by an extensive graph database and an optimization toolkit. The database contains almost 200,000 structures for phosphines, amines and arsines at different fidelity levels, explicitly including failed calculations and enforcing a topology based on substituent-level mutation operations. On the other hand, the software toolkit streamlines the application of optimization algorithms (search policies and predictive oracles) to such databases, pushing forward the development of benchmarks. We explore the baseline application of a varied set of such methods—evolutionary algorithms, Bayesian Optimization, LLM-based procedures and multifidelity approaches—to the optimization of a key property: the HOMO-LUMO gap across each of the three ligand families. In this manner, we reveal the relevance of graph topology in the guidance of these algorithms, as well as the performance differences these baseline methods depending on the particularities of each of the ligand families.
items.authors: Diego Garay-Ruiz, Rodrigo A. Vargas-Hernández, Sergio Pablo-García

items.title: Composition-Dependent Remodeling of the ABCB1Disordered Linker by Plasma-Generated ReactiveMixtures
items.abstract: Multidrug resistance (MDR) mediated by the efflux transporter ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) remains a major barrier in cancer chemotherapy. Because classical active-site inhibitors have largely failed clinically due to off-target toxicity, disrupting the interdomain mechanical coupling required for transport has emerged as an attractive alternative. Cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) generates coexisting reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) capable of sensitizing chemoresistant cells, yet how multicomponent reactive mixtures dynamically perturb the intrinsically disordered NBD1–TMD2 linker, a vital mechanical relay in ABCB1, remains unresolved. Here, we investigate the conformational and mechanical response of the structurally tethered ABCB1 linker exposed to binary and ternary mixtures of H2O2, NO, and O2 using all-atom molecular dynamics simulations. Characterization across a six-descriptor dynamical panel, synthesized into an Integrated Control-Relative Restriction Score (ICRRS), reveals that linker remodeling is governed by chemical composition rather than total molecular loading. Increasing molecular burden does not induce monotonic rigidity; instead, distinct mixture combinations selectively direct the linker toward divergent, polarized states of conformational restriction or conformational release. Crucially, benchmarking against isolated-species counterparts revealed pronounced composition-dependent contrasts, wherein co-solutes redirect local torsional kinetics, spatial breadth, and effective tethered stiffness. These findings establish that coexisting plasma-derived species selectively reconfigure the conformational state of the ABCB1 disordered relay. By demonstrating that mixture biophysics overrides concentration-dependent loading, this work provides an atomistic foundation for how multicomponent plasma biophysics can mechanically modulate ABCB1 allostery, offering new biophysical perspectives for overcoming P-glycoprotein-mediated chemoresistance.
items.authors: Mansoureh Hoseini, Hossein Abbasi

items.title: Mechanochemical nitrogen fixation into amides and nitriles.
items.authors: Maximilian Wohlgemuth, Lars Beissel, Maike Mayer, Etienne Comfai, Lars Borchardt

items.title: Metal-Free Photoinduced Divergent Activation of N2O and H2 Employing Main-Group Radical Pairs
items.abstract: Activating robust small molecules like nitrous oxide (N2O) and molecular hydrogen (H2) without transition metals is a key challenge in sustainable chemistry. To address this, we developed an efficient photochemical platform that uses silylphosphanes to divergently activate both the gases. Under photoirradiation, the silylphosphane’s P-Si bond undergoes rapid homolytic cleavage, releasing highly reactive silyl and phosphinyl radicals. When exposed to N2O, these independent radicals act parallelly to drive a double-deoxygenation cascade, yielding the corresponding tetra-aryldiphosphine dioxide and siloxane. Remarkably, this same transient radical pair can also activate H2 under exceptionally mild conditions. Supported by control experiments and DFT studies that confirm a purely radicaldriven mechanism, this work highlights main-group radical pair as a powerful, sustainable alternative to precious-metal catalysis.
items.authors: Reetu Rani Mondal, Rahul Mondal, K. Geetharani, Geetharani K

items.title: Pd-Cu-Ag Trimetallic Synergistic Catalysis for Decarboxylative/Deaminative Coupling of Carboxylic acids with Tertiary Amines
items.abstract: Palladium-catalyzed coupling reactions, such as the well-established Suzuki and Hiyama couplings of benzylic ammonium salts, have been widely employed for the synthesis of diphenylmethanes. In contrast, the decarboxylative coupling strategy for constructing such scaffolds remains largely unexplored. This paper reports a Pd-Cu-Ag trimetallic synergistic catalytic system that enables efficient access to diphenylmethane derivatives through C(sp3)–N bond cleavage of amines and decarboxylation of carboxylic acids. This innovative methodology involves the in situ generation of carbene precursors via Pd-catalyzed, electron-deficient alkyne-mediated deamination of tertiary amines, along with the formation of activated nucleophilic species through Cu/Ag-catalyzed decarboxylation of carboxylic acids. The protocol features mild reaction conditions, high efficiency, and excellent functional group tolerance.
items.authors: Yujuan Xie, Liliang Huang, Huangdi Feng, Erik V. Van der Eycken

items.title: A Solution-Gated Graphene Transistor Sensor for the Detection and Quantification of Guanine Quadruplexes.
items.abstract: SGGT G4 Detection 2 ABSTRACT. We report the design, realization, and testing of a Solution-Gated Graphene Transistor Sensor aimed at detecting and quantifying guanine quadruplexes. By using all-atom molecular dynamic simulations complemented with free energy methods we rationally design the architecture of the sensors, exploiting an economic and easy-available G4 ligand. The prototype of the sensor has shown the capacity to provide a linear response depending on the G4 concentration, hence showing the proof of concept of its applicability for G4 detection. The proposed sensors may allow the rapid detection of guanine quadruplexes in complex matrices, without relying on the use of antibodies or complex experimental apparatus.
items.authors: Aurianne Rainot, Dieu Linh Nguyen, Alessio Terenzi, Raphael Rouget, Stéphanie Grandemange, Giampaolo Barone

items.title: Coordination-Insertion Copolymerization of Norbornene with α-Olefins using Half-Titanocene Phosphinimide Catalyst
items.abstract: We previously reported the controlled coordination-insertion polymerization of 2-norbornene (NB) and 5-alkyl-2-norbornenes using a phosphinimide-ligated half-titanocene catalyst (1), affording high-molecular-weight polymers. In this study, the copolymerization of NB with α-olefins, including 1-octene (2), 1-octadecene (3), and 10-undecen-1-ol (4), was investigated to explore the monomer scope and functional group tolerance. Copolymers with Mn values ranging from 2.0 to 20 kg/mol were obtained in moderate to high yields. NB was consumed more rapidly than 2. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) analysis of the copolymers suggests that an α-olefin-derived titanium alkyl species undergoes chain transfer via a σ-bond metathesis with NB, affording the 2-norbornenyl moiety at the initiating chain end. In addition, copolymers containing up to 7 mol% of 4 were obtained through protecting the hydroxyl group with methylaluminoxane (MAO) prior to polymerization. Collectively, catalyst 1 exhibited broad reactivity, including the coordination-insertion and the σ-bond metathesis reactions, while remaining catalytically active in the presence of the alkoxyaluminum species.
items.authors: Taiki Inoko, Shin-ichi Matsuoka

items.title: Optimization of Sodium-Catalyzed Si–N Bond Formation Through a Comparative Study of Group 1 Alkoxides
items.abstract: A systematic comparison of group 1 tert-amylate (OtAmyl) salts as precatalysts for Si–N heterodehydrocoupling is reported with a focus on NatOAmyl. The heavier alkali metals provide good to excellent conversions with all substrates screened, including tertiary silanes and secondary amines, which are challenging substrates in prior literature reports. Although the activity of NatOAmyl is limited in comparison to rubidium and cesium congeners, this can be improved with judicious solvent choice, particularly DMSO. The overall findings support that a single inexpensive and sustainable catalyst can be primarily used for Si–N bond formation; however, if the substrates are particularly challenging, CstOAmyl will provide high conversion. This analysis provides a systematic approach for pragmatic catalysts to engage in bond formation with abundant silicon and nitrogen that serves synthesis and materials chemistry.
items.authors: Shakira A. Iyanda, Rory A. Wells, Gwyneth A. Oden, Rory Waterman

items.title: Cation Mixing Controls Photocatalytic Activity of Ionic Carbon Nitrides by Switching Exciton Character and Electron Localization
items.authors: Johannes Liessem, Arindam Konar, Changbin Im, Mohamed M. Elnagar, Dariusz Mitoraj, Pratibha Saini

items.title: Predictive Model for Acid-Catalyzed SN1 Solvolysis Racemization of Chiral Alcohols in Water
items.abstract: We have developed a predictive model for assessing the racemization risk of drug candidates featuring chiral alcohol motifs, addressing an important concern in drug discovery and development. Specifically, it predicts the activation free energy of stereoisomerization through the acid-catalyzed SN1 solvolysis mechanism based on the calculated electronic reaction energy associated with carbocation formation, the assumed rate-determining step. At the core of the framework is a linear regression model relating the calculated electronic reaction energy difference between the chiral alcohol and the carbocation intermediate to the activation free energy derived from experimental racemization kinetics. The resulting model showed a strong correlation and high statistical significance (R2=0.92, p=1.9 ∗ 10−8), reproducing the activation free energy with a root-mean-square error of 4.1 kJ/mol. Thus, the model has the potential to enable high-throughput assessment of racemization risk in drug candidates, supporting the development of safer pharmaceuticals and more efficient drug development pipelines.
items.authors: Fabian Sievert, Per-Ola Norrby, Arseny Kovyrshin, Christoph Bauer, Elliot H. E. Farrar, David Buttar

items.title: An Evidence-Graded Framework for Pharmaceutical Route Selection and Process-Risk Prioritization: A PN6047 Case Study
items.abstract: Purpose: To develop and demonstrate an evidence-graded framework for screening discovery-scale synthetic routes before experimental process development, using the publicly disclosed route to PN6047, a clinical-stage δ-opioid receptor agonist, as a case study. Methods: No synthesis was performed. Operations exemplified in two patent documents were inventoried; each transformation and its conditions were graded A–D by the strength of public evidence; documented regulatory and hazard attributes were flagged; two process-oriented variants were screened by step count, flags and an evidence-weighted validation burden; and a twelve-item risk register was ranked, with the sensitivity of the prioritization to the author-assigned ratings tested by perturbation. Results: The exemplified route (milligram to gram scale; final N-functionalization isolated in 16% by preparative HPLC) carries 11 documented flags, including an ICH Q3C Class 1 solvent, palladium and a benzotriazole-derived coupling reagent. Variants R1 and R2 carry 3 flags each but a higher validation burden (11 and 15 against 2, linear scale): fewer documented flags did not mean lower development uncertainty. Two risks, impurity purge when crystallization replaces chromatography and the undisclosed route to the vinyl bromide, stayed in the top three in about 87% of perturbations, conditional on the initial risk model. Conclusion: The framework converts public route information into an auditable experimental-prioritization strategy while explicitly separating documented process liabilities from unvalidated alternatives. It does not select a best route; it shows where the evidence is strong or assumed and which experiments carry the highest information value.
items.authors: Leon Sandler

items.title: Structural Description of Two-Dimensional Nanoscale Networks Using Graph Theory and Graph Growth Algorithms
items.abstract: Nanostructured networks stand out among other nanostructures for their unique combinations of properties and easily scalable energy-efficient synthesis. Their structural organization is, however, difficult to describe using traditional approaches based on crystallinity. Although revealing distinct structural patterns, the nanoscale networks also have a substantial degree of randomness. Two-dimensional (2D) nanostructured networks self-assembled from nanoparticles present a unique opportunity to develop the methodology for structural description of such materials. We describe nanostructured networks as sets of nodes and edges with corresponding weights taking advantage of the mathematical apparatus of Graph Theory (GT). Being extracted from electron microscopy images, the GT descriptors readily identify nanoscale networks obtained under different chemical conditions. Also important is that among the prior studies the GT description of properties has been extensively discussed, while better understanding of adequate GT descriptors is lagging. All GT descriptors were found to be scale-dependent, with average nodal degree, centrality metrics, multi-fractal dimension, and Ollivier-Ricci curvature following smooth superlinear or sublinear trajectories over several thousands of nodes. Statistical analysis of topological and metric parameters of nodes and edges enables development of topometric graph growth algorithms (TOGGA) that capture the structural uniqueness of each nanoscale network. Similarly to the infinite tiling of unit cells in crystals, TOGGA models enabled the extrapolation of nanoscale network structure, commensurate with both micro- and macroscale samples over 10 million nodes and 20 million edges. The predictions of electric transport through the networks comparable in size to experimental samples enable identification of knowledge gaps for rapid design of conductive nanoscale networks. TOGGA models can be used to map out experimentally realistic structures for inverse design of nanoscale networks.
items.authors: Pavel Khavlyuk, Xiongye Xiao, Will Stephenson, Dickson Owuor, Chung Man Lim, Volodymyr Shamraienko

items.title: Formation Pathways of Cyanocoronene (C24H11CN) in the Interstellar Medium and its Detectability with JWST
items.abstract: Cyanocoronene, the currently known largest cyano-substituted polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH), has recently been discovered in the molecular cloud TMC-1. In this work, we investigate its possible formation pathways using density functional theory (DFT) together with multireference CASSCF and NEVPT2 quantum chemical calculations. Six distinct formation mechanisms are explored, including HAVA-type growth pathways as well as alternative bottomup routes. To facilitate astronomical searches, anharmonic infrared spectra of cyanocoronene are computed and compared with continuum-subtracted JWST/NIRSpec observations. Our calculations indicate that, among the bottom-up growth pathways considered, early incorporation of the nitrile group generally facilitates subsequent PAH growth, while direct cyanation of an already formed coronene framework is also energetically favorable, exhibiting a submerged barrier. Comparison of the theoretical spectra with the available JWST observations does not reveal any convincing spectral signatures attributable to cyanocoronene in the different astrophysical environments examined.
items.authors: Sharadhi Vakuda, Suranjan Shil, P. Shalima, Shivani Mishra, Amit Pathak, suranjan shil

items.title: Tracking Surface Charge of Gold Single-Crystal Electrodes with Diffuse Layer Force Microscopy
items.abstract: Electrochemistry is a powerful approach for the interconversion of electrical and chemical energy. This is enabled by the nanoscale confined potential difference occurring at an interface, such as that between a solid and a liquid. As such, the structure of this region of separated charge, or electrical double layer, inherently includes molecular scale ordering in the liquid, as well as atomic scale details of the electrode, making it challenging to obtain a detailed picture of the potential-dependent state of electrochemical interfaces. In this work, we locally measure the long-range electrostatic interaction force (on the order of the screening length) between single-crystal gold electrodes and a microscale probe. Using such force spectroscopy, we observe three distinct electrochemical phenomena through the interaction force, i.e. non-faradaic charging of the interface and the potential of zero free charge, potential-induced surface reconstruction, and electrochemical oxidation of the gold surface. The results are interpreted within the Derjaguin-Landau-Verwey-Overbeek framework, relating the force measurement to the surface charge and the electrochemical state of the interface.
items.authors: Mark Aarts, Herman A.J. de Vries, Marc T.M. Koper

items.title: Alkyl-BODIPYs as a Self-Photoredox Catalyst for their Oxidative Hydroxymethylation
items.abstract: The adoption of photocatalytic approaches for utilising small organic molecules in self‑catalysed reactions offers opportunities in green organic synthesis. We report that alkylated boron‑dipyrromethenes (BODIPYs) act as self‑photoredox catalysts for their own oxidation under mild visible‑light conditions. Using an imidazolinium salt (NHC-H) as a quencher, alkylated BODIPYs are oxidised cleanly to the corresponding hydroxymethyl derivatives in a one‑pot process. Luminescence studies, including Stern–Volmer analysis, support a reductive‑quenching pathway in which the NHC-H transfers an electron to photoexcited BODIPY to give a BODIPY radical anion. The method proceeds without external photocatalysts or stoichiometric oxidants and shows good functional‑group tolerance, highlighting the potential of these chromophores both as substrates and catalytic light absorbers. Moreover, the synthesized molecules were demonstrated to behave as effective passivating agents for layered Mn2+
items.authors: Shaista Sultan, Praveen B. Managutti, Ahmed Abdelhady, Ramon Rios

items.title: On the impact of methodological configurations and data variations on chemical recycling life cycle assessment studies
items.abstract: The comparability of Life Cycle Assessment studies on chemical recycling processes for plastic waste conversion is challenging due to the wide range of investigated feedstocks, datasets, and methodological choices. Thus, this paper investigates the impact of various degrees of freedom within peer-reviewed Life Cycle Assessments of chemical recycling processes on the proposed environmental impact. In detail, methodological degrees of freedom, such as system boundary depth, functional units, allocation methods, and the utilization of substitution credits, as well as data-related degrees of freedom, including the use of plant-level, model-based, literature-derived, or third-party data at different data scales, such as experimental, laboratory, or pilot scale, are considered. Among the investigated Life Cycle Assessment studies, none of them applied the same combination of methodological choices, highlighting the methodological uniqueness of each study. However, changes in either methodological or data-related degrees of freedom substantially affect Life Cycle Assessment results in both magnitude and interpretation: without changing the methodology, data-related degrees of freedom shift the global warming potential for 1 kg of treated waste from 2.5 kg CO2-eq. below that of incineration as the reference waste treatment process to 0.5 kg CO2-eq. above. Utilizing the same database, methodological differences as reported in the investigated studies shift the global The underlined authors contributed equally and share first authorship. warming potential from 2.9 below to 0.3 kg CO2-eq. above the global warming potential of incineration. The same trend is found when comparing the products of chemical recycling to the fossil-based production routes, where the main levers affecting the results were identified as the declaration of products, the handling of side streams, and the choice of energy sources. These findings show that LCA results should not be interpreted on the basis of individual values alone, but in the context of methodological choices, data sources and quality, and sensitivity to both data and methodological assumptions. Without transparency regarding these aspects, reported values are of limited interpretive value and may offer unwanted possibilities for selective interpretation and may ultimately increase the risk of greenwashing in the communication of chemical recycling performance.
items.authors: Philip Biessey, Darius Steegborn, Meike Islamoglu, Lucas Wieczorek, Yu-Yi Lin, Manfred Renner

items.title: Aerobic ethanol oxidation by magnetic inductive heating of Pd NPs supported onto Ni foam
items.abstract: Selective aerobic oxidation of ethanol to acetic acid is an attractive example of the conversion of biomass-derived alcohol value-added chemicals. In this context, conventional liquidphase processes often rely on harsh conditions, long reaction times, inefficient external heating and limited catalyst recovery. Herein, a radically new strategy for acetic acid synthesis from ethanol is proposed and demonstrated. The catalyst used is designed not only as the active phase for chemical transformation, but also as the element responsible for local heat generation. Pd nanoparticles were immobilised onto magnetically-responsive Ni foam, affording a macroscopic, flow-compatible architecture that overcomes key limitations found for dispersed or powdered systems, including aggregation, active-phase loss and difficult reuse. Using a low amplitude alternating magnetic field of 9.2 mT, which corresponds to a lower magnetic flux density value than normally used for dispersed magnetic nanocatalyst, the Pd@Ni-foam system reached 90 % ethanol conversion after 8 h, while the acetic acid selectivity was 98 % already after 2 h reaction time. In analogous conditions, conventional heating was significantly less effective than magnetic induction, highlighting the advantage of delivering thermal energy directly at the Pd/liquid interface, thereby preserving ethanol availability at the active sites while limiting substrate evaporation. The structured catalyst showed direct reusability without regeneration, and analysis of the recovered catalyst revealed neither Pd NPs sintering, nor detectable Pd loss. By combining catalytic activity, lowfield magnetic responsiveness, stability, reduced bulk heating and continuous flow operation within a single tuneable material, a new approach to heterogeneous catalysis has been introduced, opening a modular route toward electrified, intensified and more efficient liquidphase transformations of renewable and volatile substrates, such as ethanol.
items.authors: Beatrice Muzzi, Martin Albino, Enrico Berretti, Giovanni Bertoni, Jacopo Lupi, Federico Totti

items.title: Total Synthesis of Site-Specifically Modified bHLHLz Transcription Factors Reveals Insights into the Regulatory Role of Posttranslational Modifications in the Myc–Max–Mad Network
items.abstract: The Myc–Max–Mad bHLHLz transcription factor (TF) network regulates the expression of ~15% of the human genome, and its dysregulation is implicated in nearly 70% of human cancers. Although its activity is primarily governed by competition for dimerization partners and occupancy of shared DNA target sequences, the molecular mechanisms controlling oligomerization and DNA binding remain elusive. Here, we employed total protein synthesis and combinatorial assembly to define how posttranslational modification (PTM) patterns regulate the Myc–Max–Mad TF network. Using native chemical ligation, we prepared a library of site-specifically modified Myc, Mnt, Mad, and phosphorylated or acetylated Max analogs. Remarkably, the isolation of homogeneous TFs enabled the combinatorial generation of all 24 heterodimeric complexes, allowing systematic analysis of dimerization and DNA-binding activity across the network. Our findings provide direct evidence that although Max phosphorylation and acetylation do not significantly affect its oligomerization with the Myc transcriptional activator, these modifications enhance its dimerization with the transcriptional repressors Mnt and Mad. Moreover, we found that Max-PTMs modulate DNA-binding activity by both specific PTM patterns and combinations, as well as the identity of the TF partner. Together, these findings demonstrate that PTM-dependent modulation of DNA-binding activity within the Myc–Max–Mad network constitutes a key regulatory layer governing gene expression.
items.authors: Raj V. Nithun, Muhammad Jbara

items.title: Multinotch Isolation Enables Efficient Native Top-down Mass Spectrometry of Proteins in Complex Mixtures.
items.abstract: Accurate identification of intact proteoforms and their complexes directly from heterogenous biological samples is essential to understand their role in health and disease. While native top-down mass spectrometry (nTDMS) workflows enable this, the extreme molecular complexity of biological samples inadvertently results in overlapping signals which confounds protein identification. One approach to resolving this complexity is gas-phase ion-ion reactions which separate analytical targets according to their original charge state. Charge reduction techniques coupled to mass spectrometry resolve signal overlap in m/z space, when ions differ in charge, and so they are especially useful in the analysis of large biomolecules like proteins that form multiple charge states during electrospray ionisation. Previously, we investigated multistage nTDMS of intact proteins sampled directly from tissue sections where the first experiment stage was separation by charge reduction, followed by collisional activation for sequence ion production. The specificity of product ion spectra was improved but at the expense of signal intensity owing to inefficient use of charge-reduced product ions. Here we establish the use of synchronous precursor selection (SPS) for nTDMS via multinotch isolation in a linear ion trap, enabling simultaneous isolation of multiple targets in m/z space and thereby increasing the number of ions available for fragmentation. We implemented SPS for nTDMS across three charge reduction techniques and collision, electron and photon mediated fragmentation methods on commercial and modified mass spectrometers. Improvements to the signal-to-noise ratio of product ions resulted in greater sequence coverage for example intact proteins and complexes up to ~44 kDa using the SPS workflow. We provide a freely-available SPS target calculator, Novalap, that enables simple SPS method development. SPS nTDMS is a methodological breakthrough for proteoform identification in complex mixtures, where specificity is essential, sequence coverage is desired and ion abundance is at a premium.
items.authors: Oliver J. Hale, Helen J. Cooper

items.title: GMAP: A General Purpose Hamiltonian Mapping Program for Computational Spectroscopy
items.abstract: Vibrational and electronic spectra provide useful information about structure, dynamics, and function in the condensed phase. Electrostatic mappings have proved to be powerful tools for predicting and interpreting both vibrational and electronic spectra. Numerous special purpose programs exist; however, a general purpose framework is still missing. In this paper, we present a new general purpose mapping program for bridging the gap between structural and dynamical information obtained in molecular dynamics simulations and programs for calculating spectroscopic observables. It comes with a number of preexisting maps to, for example, predict the amide I vibrational spectrum of proteins or to model the electronic Qy band of strongly coupled chlorophyll molecules in photosynthetic systems. The program applying mappings connecting structural or electrostatic properties with excitation frequencies, transition dipoles, and couplings is designed so that the user can easily adapt existing maps or add new maps for desired chromophores.
items.authors: Kim E. van Adrichem, Tim Zuidema, Stephanie Gonzalez-Migoni, Gijsbert A. H. ten Hoven, Kai Zhong, Mónica K. Espinoza Cangahuala

items.title: Ultra-lightweight Flexible Perovskite–Perovskite–Organic Triple-Junction Tandem Solar Cells
items.abstract: Triple-junction photovoltaics offer a promising route to surpass the efficiency limitations of single-junction solar cells, yet existing high-performance architectures are predominantly rigid and relatively heavy, limiting their use in weight-sensitive applications. Here, we report, to the best of our knowledge, the first ultra-lightweight and flexible monolithic perovskiteperovskite–organic triple-junction tandem solar cells. The devices integrate 2.05 eV and 1.62 eV perovskite front and middle subcells with a 1.33 eV organic bulk-heterojunction rear subcell on a 10 μm flexible polyethylene terephthalate substrate. The champion tandem device achieves a power conversion efficiency of 24.1%, with an open-circuit voltage of 3.27 V, a short-circuit current density of 9.32 mA/cm2, and a fill factor of 79.0%, corresponding to a power-per-weight of 11.2 W/g. The device exhibits a stabilized PCE of 24.6% under maximumpower-point tracking and negligible hysteresis between forward and reverse voltage scans. External quantum efficiency measurements yield closely matched integrated photocurrent densities of 9.39, 9.39, and 9.21 mA/cm2 for the three subcells, confirming efficient spectral utilization and current matching. These results establish flexible perovskite–perovskiteorganic triple-junction tandems as a promising platform for high-specific-power photovoltaics and open opportunities for lightweight energy harvesting in aerospace, unmanned aerial vehicles, wearable electronics, and portable power systems.
items.authors: FURKAN H. ISIKGOR

items.title: Multi-fidelity machine learning interatomic potential for the energetics and finite temperature structure of Pt surfaces and nanoparticles
items.abstract: Accurate accounting of exposed facets and surface sites is central to understanding metal nanoparticle catalysts, but modelling their structure at finite temperatures is computationally expensive. We benchmark the universal interatomic potential UMA (Universal Model for Atoms, Open Catalyst 2020 task) against Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof density functional theory (PBE-DFT) for Pt. UMA underestimates the surface energies of all 13 facets by 11-17 % and the excess energies of 28 differently shaped nanoparticles, each containing less than 500 atoms, most strongly for small particles. We distill UMA into a compact Deep Potential model by pre-training on UMA labelled bulk and slab data, then fine-tune it on a small PBE-DFT dataset that includes nanoparticles. The resulting multi-fidelity machine learning interatomic potential (MF-MLIP) gives a surface-energy root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 2.8 meV Å−2, 21 % lower than a DFT only model trained on the same data. On six nanoparticles, the MF-MLIP improves force accuracy over UMA, reducing the force RMSE by 29-52 %, with the largest gains at surface, edge and vertex atoms.
