Molecular dynamics at 500 K shows Pt(111) retaining its termination while Pt(100) and Pt(110) change strongly. At 500-700 K, the nanoparticles lose vertex sites and gain edge sites, and some restructure away from their ideal shapes. On the same CPU hardware, the MF-MLIP runs molecular dynamics simulations 60-100 times faster than UMA.
items.authors: Noor Aldin Alzghoul, Wo Bin Bae, Jun Hee Jang, Aditya Dilip Lele

items.title: Process and Systems Modeling of Hydrothermal Liquefaction for Fuels and
items.abstract: 17 Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) can convert wet organic waste into fuels and bioproducts, but 18 variation in feedstocks and operating conditions can propagate from product yields to system 19 performance and deployment. This study linked machine learning based HTL yield prediction with 20 process simulation, techno-economic analysis (TEA), life cycle assessment (LCA), uncertainty 21 analysis, and surrogate modeling. A literature data set of 402 experiments was used to predict 22 biocrude, aqueous, gas, and solids yields, with 71.8% of predictions within ±5 wt% of experimental 23 values. The predicted yields reproduced 77.1% of internal rate of return (IRR) and 83.2% of 24 GWP100 estimates within ±5% and ±10 kg CO2e/kg, respectively, and were integrated into two 25 deployment configurations (centralized and decentralized HTL) and two product pathways 26 (biobinder/biofuel and sustainable aviation fuel [SAF]). Process and system scale analyses 27 showed that operating conditions strongly affecting HTL performance could have weaker or 28 competing economic effects due to tradeoffs among product yields, water handling, energy 29 requirements, and capital costs. Across representative feedstocks, decentralized biobinder 30 systems achieved median IRRs up to 35.8%, compared with up to 8.0% for decentralized SAF 31 systems. Feedstock price, followed by biocrude quality, and biocrude yield emerged as the 32 leading economic drivers. Monte Carlo filtering identified waste tipping fee thresholds $25.1–33 196.7 per wet metric tonne for achieving the 10% IRR target. These results show that existing 34 tipping fee structure can support HTL deployment in some cases, while higher tipping fees or 35 additional financial incentives can expand viability and enable higher investment returns. 36
items.authors: Ali Ahmad, Rohit Bhagat, Kevin Warren, Saketnath Pabba, Yalin Li

items.title: Designing Alloying Interlayers for Metal Anodes in Batteries: Does Nanostructuring Improve Reversibility?
items.abstract: Metal anodes have been extensively explored as candidates for high-energy rechargeable batteries. However, uncontrolled electrodeposition of metals such as Zn often produces porous, disconnected “dead” metal that limits reversibility. A common mitigation strategy is to introduce an alloying functional layer, which is in general assumed to perform better when nanostructured due to its increased specific surface area and the diffusion scaling relation 𝜏~ 𝐿 2 𝐷 ⁄ . Here, we directly interrogate how the characteristic feature size of an alloying interlayer governs reversibility, using Ag functional layers with building blocks at three representative length scales: 100 nm, a few μm, and 100 μm, approximately. Combining operando visualization with ex-situ structural characterization, we find that Ag layers composed of few-μm particles exhibit the highest Zn plating and stripping reversibility. Coarse, 100-μm Ag particles provide poor areal coverage, such that beneficial Ag–Zn alloying is confined to isolated regions and does not effectively regulate deposition. In contrast, nanostructured Ag reacts rapidly and nearly completely, transforming into bulk intermetallic phases with large volume change that crack and delaminate from the current collector. Few-μm Ag features, on the one hand, provide sufficient surface coverage to promote uniform nucleation; on the other, Ag particles at this few-μm length scale prevent excessive intermetallic conversion and the associated mechanical failure. These results challenge the conventional wisdom that nanostructured layers are inherently more effective and reveal a previously overlooked mesoscopic design window for alloying interlayers. By explicitly linking alloying-layer feature size to diffusion-controlled phase transformation, mesoscale mechanical stability, and electrochemical behavior, this work identifies surface topography as a key design parameter for stabilizing multivalent metal anodes of high-energy batteries.
items.authors: Sydney C. Manning, J. X. Kent Zheng

items.title: A soluble conductive chromium coordination polymer with radical ligands and non-integer redox states
items.abstract: There are few conductive metal-organic materials that are solution processible or that feature electron-accepting conductive units. Thus, a soluble, semiconductive coordination polymer (1n+)x (n = 1 – 3) was developed by linking CrIII ions with electron-deficient back-to-back bis-terpyridine (btpy) ligands. CrIII promotes reduction of these ligands under mild conditions (starting at −0.16 V vs. Fc+/0), providing the first extended material with btpy•− or btpy2− units. Interestingly, (1n+)x undergoes non-integer redox changes (∣Δn∣ 1) in DMF solution, representing emergent electronic behavior that leads to a moderately high solid-state conductivity of 3.9 x 10−3 S cm−1 when n = 1.5. These solution-phase/solid-state correlations present a promising way to examine and tune the electronic properties of metal-organic radical materials.
items.authors: Iram F. Mansoor, Arya Patel, Joe K. Bush, Zeyu Cao, Li Ling Goldston, Xiao Luo

items.title: Density Functional Theory Bond Dissociation Energies of Model Compounds Relevant to LDL Oxidation: Bis-Allylic C–H, Phenolic O–H and Hydroperoxide O–H Bonds
items.abstract: Background: Oxidative modification of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) contributes to atherogenesis, with polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) as its main chemical target. Vitamin E is an effective chain-breaking antioxidant in vitro, yet large clinical trials showed no cardiovascular benefit. We calculated bond dissociation energies (BDEs) of model compounds to quantify the underlying thermodynamics. Methods: Density functional theory calculations (PySCF; B3LYP/6-311+G(d,p)//B3LYP/6-31G*, scaled zero-point energy, 0 K) were performed for butane (secondary C–H), 1,4-pentadiene, phenol, catechol and methyl hydroperoxide. Vitamin E was not calculated at the relaxed level; published values were used. A truncated tocopherol model (5,7,8-trimethylchroman-6-ol) was run at screening level only (B3LYP/6-31+G*, unrelaxed geometries, no zero-point correction), with phenol at the same level. Results: The bis-allylic C–H bond of 1,4-pentadiene (68.2 kcal/mol) was 28.3 below the secondary C–H bond of butane (96.5). Catechol O–H (73.4) was 8.4 below phenol (81.8). The hydroperoxide model (79.6) fell 2.2 below phenol, whereas experimental values place the two within about 1 kcal/mol, comparable to their uncertainties, so phenol is a weak test of the order; catechol was 6.2 below the hydroperoxide, as expected. In screening calculations the tocopherol model was 9.0 below phenol. Published values place α-tocopherol O–H at about 77 to 78 kcal/mol, about 10 below phenol, the same direction as our screening gap. For the four bonds with experimental references, computed values were 1.7 to 8.6 kcal/mol below them; no direct experimental value exists for the bis-allylic C–H. Gaps and ordering, not absolute values, are therefore interpreted. Conclusions: The calculations quantify the thermodynamic basis for PUFA vulnerability and for the stronger hydrogen donation of polyphenol-type O–H bonds. They do not by themselves show donation to peroxyl radicals. Bond energies cannot explain the clinical trial results; kinetics, LDL localization and tocopherol-mediated peroxidation must be considered. No clinical outcomes or biomarkers were computed.
items.authors: Yadlapalli Anirudh, Anirudh yadlapalli

items.title: The helium ground-state energy to 60 significant figures on a laptop
items.abstract: We report a variational upper bound on the nonrelativistic, infinite-nuclear-mass ground-state energy of helium whose first 60 significant figures are converged, E0 = −2.903 724 377 034 119 598 311 159 245 194 404 446 696 925 311 117 290 339 042 34 Eh, 16 more than the best previous record. The calculation runs on a laptop and the method, which we call FLAKE (Fock-log anisotropic Kronecker eigensolver), combines four ingredients. (i) A change of variables making Schwartz’s Hylleraas-type basis with logarithms an exact tensor product, so the Hamiltonian is a sum of 27 Kronecker products of small matrices. (ii) Exact, arbitrary-precision orthonormalisation of the small radial and angular Gram factors removes all cancellation from the large computation. (iii) Fixed-point products at about 280 bits are split without error into ordinary double-precision matrix multiplications. (iv) The variational space is anisotropic: it carries extra radial degree and a tower of (ln s)p functions only at low angular order, as dictated by channelresolved convergence rates. Every energy quoted is certified by an independent arbitrary-precision evaluation of the Rayleigh quotient of the explicit trial function. The remaining error is estimated from geometric convergence laws that predicted subsequent energy increments to within 2%.

items.title: Paper2CIF: An AI Agent for Reconstructing Atomistic Models to Discover Structure-Reactivity Relationships
items.abstract: Reinterpreting published chemical findings requires explicit atomic structures that connect experimental observations with reactivity. Here we report Paper2CIF, an artificial intelligence (AI) agent that reconstructs sample-specific atomic structures from published chemical evidence for structure-reactivity relationship investigations. Across 171 interdisciplinary articles, Paper2CIF achieves 97.08% phase identification accuracy and 91.23% final structural accuracy, with correct structures satisfying all applicable reported constraints, including composition, site occupancy, and local coordination. Calculations on reconstructed BiVO4 structures reveal distortion-dependent spatial contributions to the transition dipole, guiding targeted synthesis toward enhanced near-edge photon conversion. The resulting BiVO4-based Z-scheme pair exhibits a 3.47-fold increase in apparent quantum yield from 4.51% to 15.64% at 475 nm, compared with a 1.03-fold increase from 18.51% to 19.02% at 365 nm. The solar-to-hydrogen efficiency increases from 0.969% to 1.448% for overall water splitting. Paper2CIF establishes atomic reconstruction as a common basis for deriving chemical mechanisms from published evidence and translating them into experimentally testable principles for materials synthesis.
items.authors: Qixin Zhou, Yonghang Yue, Wenjie Guo, Yongfa Zhu, Yan Guo

items.title: A species-resolved well-balanced lattice Boltzmann framework for Maxwell–Stefan diffusion in non-ideal multiphase multicomponent transport
items.abstract: Simulating non-ideal multiphase multicomponent transport requires coupled solution of phase equilibrium, hydrodynamics, and multicomponent diffusion. Recent thermodynamically consistent and well-balanced lattice Boltzmann formulations have addressed multiphase equilibria, but their integration with multicomponent diffusion is less developed. In this work, a speciesresolved well-balanced lattice Boltzmann framework is developed to incorporate Maxwell–Stefan diffusion into non-ideal multiphase multicomponent transport. The formulation evaluates thermodynamic driving forces from chemical potentials and introduces pairwise interspecies resistance at the species-momentum level while preserving the well-balanced nature of the underlying multiphase model. Asymptotic analysis shows that the species-level force balance reduces to the Maxwell–Stefan constitutive relation under quasi-static diffusive conditions. The framework is assessed by equilibrium and phase separation tests, linear modal benchmarks, Arnold–Toor cross-diffusion cases, local Maxwell–Stefan diagnostics, and a buoyancydriven bubble dissolution illustration. The equilibrium tests recover the theoretical equilibrium compositions with nearly uniform chemical potentials and very low spurious velocities. The modal benchmarks reproduce the predicted exponential decay rates with errors below 0.2% for ideal mixtures and about 0.1–0.5% for non-ideal mixtures, while the Arnold–Toor and local diagnostic tests capture characteristic Maxwell–Stefan diffusion behavior. These results support the proposed framework as a thermodynamically consistent and well-balanced lattice Boltzmann approach for non-ideal multiphase multicomponent transport.
items.authors: Bowen Gao, Zheng-Hong Luo, Xiaolong Yin

items.title: Aza-Michael Addition of Aliphatic Amines to Weakly Polarised Alkenes via Organobase Catalysis
items.abstract: The direct addition of aliphatic amines to alkenes offers an atom-economical route to valuable N-alkyl amines, but remains challenging for weakly polarised alkenes. This is because C–N bond formation is poorly driven thermodynamically and difficult to achieve without strongly activating the alkene or generating more reactive nitrogen species. Here we report an organobase-catalysed strategy that enables anti-Markovnikov addition of secondary aliphatic amines to weakly polarised (hetero)aryl alkenes. Kinetic studies and calculations support a mechanism in which the organobase promotes C–N bond formation through hydrogen bonding and noncovalent stabilisation of the addition transition state, followed by rapid deprotonation of the addition complex. The developed conditions were also applicable to challenging C–C bond forming Michael addition reactions with enolate nucleophiles. These findings demonstrate that organobase catalysis can overcome the intrinsic kinetic and thermodynamic challenges associated with closed-shell additions to weakly activated alkenes.
items.authors: Bradley D. Cooper, Ethan R. X. Lim, Jonathan Da Luz, Thomas D. Harris, Abby Sutton, Jonathan R. Carney

items.title: Temperature-dependent Hydrocarbon Chain Packing in Fatty Acid Protocell Membranes at Mineral Interfaces
items.abstract: Fatty acid vesicles generated through water-rock interactions have been proposed as plausible models of protocells on early Earth. However, how mineral surfaces influence membrane properties over a wide range of temperatures remains unclear. Here, we investigate the temperature-dependent phase transition and hydrocarbon chain packing of vesicles composed of decanoic acid (DA) and 1-decanol (DOH) in contact with FeS, a key hydrothermal vent mineral. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that DOH incorporation enhances orientational ordering of the hydrocarbon chains, forming more densely packed and thermally stable membranes. This enhancement in molecular ordering induced by DOH incorporation was confirmed experimentally by in situ temperature-controlled micro-Raman spectroscopy and cross-polarized optical microscopy. Upon contact with FeS, DA/DOH vesicles preferentially adhered to FeS surfaces and underwent pronounced structural deformation in response to microscale mineral topology. Despite this deformation, the DA/DOH vesicles retained their liquid-crystalline membrane state. These results demonstrate that FeS surface reorganizes hydrocarbon chain packing in fatty acid membranes, suggesting that mineral-associated protocells possess structurally and dynamically distinct membrane states from free-floating vesicles under the thermally dynamic HV environments.
items.authors: Shunto Harada, Yuki Murakami, Hye-Eun Lee, Yamei Li, Aileen Cooney, Tomoaki Matsuura

items.title: Structure-Activity Relationship Studies of the Complement Regulator-Recruiting Peptide 5C6
items.abstract: Active recruitment of host complement regulators to biomedical surfaces emerges as a therapeutic strategy to prevent adverse immuno-inflammatory reactions to biomaterials and organ transplants. Coating with the macrocyclic peptide 5C6, which binds and recruits the central complement regulator factor H (FH), was shown to protect clinically relevant surfaces from complement attack. While we previously identified general determinants for the 5C6-FH interaction, more granular structure-activity relationship (SAR) studies have hitherto been missing. In the absence of published target structures, we employed a panel of focused amino acid substitutions combined with biomolecular interaction studies to achieve an SAR profile of 5C6. We identified three positions that are particularly amenable to affinity optimization and combined several changes to produce a next-generation 5C6 analog with enhanced target residence time and serum stability. Biomaterial-related assays suggest that such analogs may confer benefits under stress conditions, providing a path for the further development of 5C6-based coatings.
items.authors: Clément Bechtler, Jannes Felsch, Ekaterina Umnyakova, Lukas Kaufmann, Christina Lamers, John D. Lambris

items.title: An Annotation Consistency Checker for Evidence-Based Evaluation of Untargeted LC-MS/MS Metabolite Annotations
items.abstract: Untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics routinely produces complex annotation landscapes in which individual spectra can yield multiple candidate metabolite annotations. Although spectral similarity provides an essential foundation for library-based annotation, determining whether a candidate annotation is consistent with the available evidence and whether alternative explanations remain plausible requires integration of multiple lines of evidence. In current practice, this evaluation is largely embedded in expert judgment, making annotation review difficult to teach, standardize, and reproduce. Here, we introduce an annotation consistency checker that aids this expert review process by generating a user-inspectable report for spectral library matches. The framework integrates complementary evidence dimensions, including spectral agreement, structural relationships among candidate annotations, and competing library matches to highlight annotations that are supported by, or inconsistent with, the available data. Biological context is provided separately to aid interpretation of metabolite occurrence across organisms, tissues, and sample types but is not incorporated into the annotation score. By enabling systematic evaluation of multiple evidence streams, this approach provides a transparent workflow that helps users critically assess metabolite annotations, reduce overinterpretation of spectral matches, and make informed decisions beyond only accepting the top-ranked library match.
items.authors: Wilhan D. G. Nunes, Edward J. Mathias, Charles Terra, Audrey Le Gouellec, Mingxun Wang, Pieter C. Dorrestein

items.title: High-Sensitivity, Dual Ratiometric and Turn-on ABATaRs for Multiplexed Temporal Imaging of Ferroptosis Hallmarks in Living Cells
items.abstract: We present a computationally-guided workflow for designing dual turn-on and ratiometric Raman sensors. The workflow has been used to rationally design activity-based alkyne tagged Raman, ABATaR , sensors that overcome the inherently low Raman sensitivity via strategic placement of electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups. An ABATaR sensing scaffold designed via the workflow afforded ~ 9000 times higher Raman scattering cross-section than the dimethylsulfoxide C-H stretching-mode. The sensitivity of the scaffold was compared to that of 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine ( EdU ) to determine Raman intensity versus EdU , RIE, a parameter used to benchmark Raman probes. An RIE value of 170 was obtained which is one of the highest amongst previously reported monoyne and diyne-based Raman probes. The sensitive ABATaR -scaffold was developed into a dual turn-on and ratiometric Fe 2+ -sensor that was applied to distinctly quantify endogenous cellular labile Fe 2+ ion levels. In a key result, live-cell, temporal imaging with the Fe 2+ - ABATaR sensor revealed that intracellular labile Fe 2+ levels progressively increase with ferroptosis while the total Fe-level remains constant. To demonstrate the generalizability of the design workflow, we synthesized an orthogonal ABATaR -sensor for H 2 O 2 . The H 2 O 2 -sensor was applied together with the Fe 2+ -sensor along with inherent Raman peaks for cytochromes to enable simultaneous, multiplexed spontaneous Raman imaging of three distinct ferroptosis hallmarks—labile Fe 2+ , H 2 O 2 , and redox-sensitive cytochrome Raman signals—in living cells. Importantly, the ability to pre-design orthogonal ratiometric Raman sensors and simultaneously track three regulators of ferroptosis via discrete non-overlapping Raman peaks highlights the tremendous potential of Raman sensors toward attaining live cell multiplexed imaging and quantification.
items.authors: Sujit K Das, Heqi Xi, Saurabh Kumar, Katsumasa Fujita, Ankona Datta

items.title: Predicting Water-Induced Demixing of Ionic Liquid Mixtures with Associative Electrolyte PC-SAFT
items.abstract: Ionic liquids (ILs) can be mixed with other ILs to fine-tune their physicochemical properties. While ILs have been long considered inseparable, recent studies have demonstrated that the controlled addition of water enables the selective recovery of the constituent salts, opening new opportunities for sustainable IL recycling and separation. The rational design of these IL mixtures remains challenging due to the lack of predictive models capable of accurately capturing the interplay between competing short- and long-range interactions in IL-based systems, particularly in multi-IL systems, thereby limiting our ability to guide both the selection of optimal IL components and the development of efficient post-mixing recovery strategies. We propose in this work an associative electrolyte PC-SAFT (aePC-SAFT) model, that incorporates, in a physically balanced manner, the short-range dispersion and hydrogen bonding interactions, as well as the long-range Coulomb interactions. Ion-specific parameters are obtained from homologous series of [CnC1Im][NTf2] (1-alkyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide) and [C4C1Im][OAc] (1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium acetate), and subsequently transferred to functionalized ILs, including [C3OC1Im]+ (1-methoxyethyl-3-methylimidazolium), based on the liquid-liquid equilibria (LLE) and density of their mixtures with water and hydrocarbons. Without additional parameter adjustment, the model accurately predicts the LLE of binary and ternary IL-water systems, including the ether-functionalized ILs. This work establishes a robust, predictive, and physically grounded framework for modeling the thermodynamic behavior of ILs, enabling the rational design and optimization of separation processes in IL-based systems.
items.authors: Fufang Yang, Beatriz R. de Moraes, Rômulo A. Ando, Agílio A. H. Pádua, Margarida Costa Gomes

items.title: Fundamental Limitations of Cu(II)-based Oxides for Photoelectrochemical Nitrogen Reduction
items.abstract: The photoelectrochemical (PEC) nitrogen reduction reaction (N 2 RR) offers a potentially sustainable route to ammonia (NH 3 ) synthesis. However, reliable evaluation of PEC N 2 RR activity remains challenging due to contamination-induced false positives and competing reactions. Here, we comparatively investigate p -type CuBi 2 O 4 and the previously reported PEC N 2 RR-active photocathode CuO, using an ultra-clean, contamination-controlled measurement system. Despite favorable band energetics and measurable photocurrents, neither material exhibits statistically significant NH 3 production, suggesting that the previously reported activity of CuO most likely originated from contamination-induced false positives rather than genuine N 2 reduction. Density functional theory further shows that the first proton-coupled electron transfer step toward *NNH formation remains kinetically prohibitive, even on oxygen-deficient surfaces, strongly favoring the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). In addition, both photocathodes undergo surface reduction and photocorrosion. Nevertheless, comparative analysis reveals fundamentally different degradation pathways on the two photocathodes. While CuBi 2 O 4 retains its bulk structural integrity under photocathodic conditions, CuO undergoes extensive reduction, restructuring, and dissolution. Together, these findings highlight the importance of contamination control in evaluating aqueous PEC N 2 RR, as well as the challenges of overcoming vigorous competition with HER and photocorrosion processes using Cu(II)-based oxides.
items.authors: Maximilian Christis, Saswati Santra, Julian Beßner, Yiqun Jiang, Xiang Li, Jasmin Zitzmann

items.title: A transferable perturbation proteomics framework for phenotype- 1 based annotation and antiproliferative potency scoring of antineoplastic agents
items.abstract: Although antineoplastic agents target diverse proteins, whether they converge on conserved cellular response states remains unclear. Here, we generate a TMTpro 18-plex quantitative proteomics atlas of 367 antineoplastic agents in HepG2 cells and identify recurrent drug response phenotypes (DRPs). The higher-order organization of DRP is conserved across seven independent proteomic datasets and shows limited concordance with chemical structure and annotated mechanisms of action. Projection of 189 external profiles representing 94 compounds achieves 42.7% balanced reference-DRP recovery, a 3.8-fold enrichment above the permutation-derived baseline. DRPs also encode antiproliferative potency, enabling derivation of a six-protein Composite Proteomic Score (CPS-6; TBL1X, NAPA, PLEKHA7, ACSL1, ARL8B, and CCDC90B) that retains associations with relative antiproliferative potency across independent proteomic and transcriptomic datasets. Proteomic similarity further reveals phenotypic convergence among mechanistically distinct compounds and enables mechanism annotation of external compounds and natural products. An interactive portal enables projection of new perturbation proteomes for phenotype-based annotation and antiproliferative potency estimation. Together, our study establishes a transferable proteomic framework for antineoplastic agents, providing a scalable resource for mechanistic hypothesis generation, drug repositioning, and phenotype-guided drug discovery.
items.authors: Jing Liang, Jundan Tian, Rui Zhang, Yueying Yang, Xu Cai, Pingping Wang

items.title: A Response Surface Methodology Framework for Targeted MALDI‑TIMS Optimization and in‑Tissue Metabolite Resolution
items.abstract: Differentiating hexose‑phosphate isomers directly within tissue is essential for understanding glycolytic and pentose‑phosphate pathway activity, particularly in the kidney, where these metabolites play central roles in energy balance, redox regulation, and stress response. However, their high structural similarity and low endogenous abundance make on‑tissue discrimination analytically challenging. To address this, we systematically optimized MALDI‑TIMS‑TOF parameters using response surface methodology (RSM), developing a predictive model that revealed positive linear and negative quadratic effects of ramp time, a positive linear dependence on TIMS pressure, no significant contribution from the mobility window, and no factor interactions. Balancing analytical sensitivity and mobility resolution identified 720 ms ramp time and 2.5 mbar TIMS pressure as optimal conditions for targeted hexose‑phosphate separations. Under these optimized conditions, MALDI‑TIMS MSI of mouse kidney with lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced injury uncovered an endogenous feature with the same nominal mass as hexose phosphates but with mobility distinct from all tested standards, including glucose-6-phosphate, glucose-1-phosphate, fructose-6-phosphate and mannose-6-phosphate. This molecule showed differential localization between cortex and medulla and responded to LPS‑induced metabolic stress, revealing unanticipated biochemical heterogeneity within the hexose‑phosphate mass range. Together, these findings demonstrate that RSM‑guided TIMS optimization enhances the resolving power of mobility‑based separations and expands the discovery potential of MALDI‑TIMS MS for uncovering molecular complexity directly within biological tissues. INTRODUCTION Sugar phosphates are central intermediates that connect glycolysis, gluconeogenesis, the pentose phosphate pathway, and glycogen metabolism, thereby sustaining energy production and redox balance in mammalian tissues1. In the kidney—one of the body’s most metabolically demanding organs—hexose phosphates play essential roles in proximal tubular glucose handling and phosphate‑dependent metabolic regulation2. Among these metabolites, glucose‑6‑phosphate (Glc6P) links glycolysis to NADPH‑producing pathways important for maintaining tubular antioxidant defense3, fructose‑6‑phosphate (Fru6P) modulates carbohydrate flux in renal epithelial cells2, and glucose‑1‑phosphate (Glc1P) contributes to glycogen turnover and metabolic buffering during renal stress4, 5. Perturbations in these tightly regulated metabolites accompany inflammation and acute kidney injury1, 6, 7, underscoring the need for analytical strategies that can distinguish sugar‑phosphate isomers directly in tissue. Differentiating sugar‑phosphate isomers remains analytically challenging because their high polarity and minimal structural differences limit the resolving power of conventional approaches. Chromatographic strategies—including hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (HILIC),
items.authors: Keshav Karkamkar, Heidi Vandyk, Azuma Nanamatsu, Tarek M El-Achkar, Dušan Veličković

items.title: Expanded ensemble predictions of solvent–water partition coefficients for drug-like molecules using OpenFF 2.0 and GAFF 2.1
items.abstract: How well do general-purpose molecular mechanics force fields predict solvent–water partition coefficients for drug-like molecules? To answer this question, we performed massively parallel expanded ensemble free energy calculations using distributed computing to evaluate two widely used force fields—GAFF 2.1 and OpenFF 2.0—across a diverse set of 70 molecules and solvents (chloroform, dodecane, octanol and toluene). We find both force fields have comparable accuracy, with predicted transfer free energies having mean unsigned errors (MUEs) below 2 kcal/mol in nearly all cases. Our results also reveal systematic error, likely due to the known deficiencies of fixed-charge force fields. We expect that this dataset and our approach to systematic evaluation using distributed computing may be useful toward future efforts in force field validation and parameterization.
items.authors: Steven R. Goold, Vincent A. Voelz
items.title_zh: 使用OpenFF 2.0和GAFF 2.1预测药物分子的溶剂-水分配系数
items.summary_zh: 本研究旨在评估通用分子力学力场对药物分子溶剂-水分配系数的预测能力。我们采用大规模并行扩展集合自由能计算，利用分布式计算评估了两种广泛使用的力场——GAFF 2.1和OpenFF 2.0，涵盖70种多样的分子和溶剂（氯仿、十二烷、辛醇和甲苯）。结果显示，两种力场的预测精度相当，几乎所有情况下预测的转移自由能的平均无符号误差（MUE）均低于2 kcal/mol。同时，我们的结果揭示了系统性误差，可能与固定电荷力场的已知缺陷有关。我们期望此数据集及其基于分布式计算的系统评估方法对未来的力场验证和参数化工作有所帮助。
items.l1_lead: 本研究评估了GAFF 2.1和OpenFF 2.0力场对药物分子溶剂-水分配系数的预测能力，结果显示两者预测精度相当，且均存在系统性误差。
items.l2_summary:
本研究旨在评估通用分子力学力场在预测药物分子溶剂-水分配系数方面的能力。研究采用了大规模并行扩展集合自由能计算，并利用分布式计算对两种广泛使用的力场——GAFF 2.1（通用力场2.1）和OpenFF 2.0（开放力场2.0）进行了评估。研究涵盖了70种多样的分子和溶剂，包括氯仿、十二烷、辛醇和甲苯。结果表明，两种力场在预测精度上相当，几乎所有情况下预测的转移自由能（free energy of transfer）的平均无符号误差（MUE）均低于2 kcal/mol，这一结果显示了两种力场在实际应用中的可靠性。

然而，研究也揭示了系统性误差，这可能与固定电荷力场的已知缺陷有关。这一发现提示在使用这些力场进行药物分子性质预测时，需谨慎考虑其潜在的局限性。研究者希望此次数据集及其基于分布式计算的系统评估方法能够为未来的力场验证和参数化工作提供有价值的参考和支持。通过对这两种力场的比较，研究不仅为药物分子的溶剂-水分配系数预测提供了实证依据，也为分子力学力场的进一步改进和应用奠定了基础。

items.title: From torrefaction to pyrolysis: Influence of bamboo biochar production route on biochar characteristics and the thermal and mechanical performance of polylactic acid biocomposites
items.abstract: The transition toward sustainable manufacturing has accelerated the development of sustainable polymer composites reinforced with bio-based fillers such as biochar. This study investigates how the biochar carbonization route affects the thermal and mechanical properties of polylactic acid (PLA) biocomposites. Bamboo-derived torrefied biomass (TBB) and pyrolyzed biochar (PBB) were incorporated into PLA at loadings of 1 wt.% and 2 wt.%. PLA–TBB composites exhibited improved tensile stiffness and flexural performance, achieving improvements of 4.28% in tensile modulus, 18.72% in flexural strength, and 12.30% in flexural modulus compared with neat PLA. In contrast, PLA–PBB composites showed the highest compressive strength, with a 29.53% increase. Thermal analysis further revealed that biochar, regardless of the carbonization route, induced cold crystallization and slightly improved PLA thermal stability, with PLA–PBB2 exhibiting the highest peak degradation temperature and PLA–PBB1 showing the lowest weight loss. These findings demonstrate that the carbonization route influences the reinforcing performance of bamboo biochar, with lower-temperature torrefied biomass favoring tensile and flexural performance, while higher-temperature pyrolyzed biochar provides superior compressive and thermal properties. The enhanced tensile stiffness and flexural performance of PLA–TBB suggest potential for rigid applications, whereas PLA–PBB is better suited to compression-loaded applications. The results provide valuable insights into tailoring the conditions for bamboo biochar production to support the development of PLA biocomposites.
items.authors: Diana Rose R. Coronado, Aristotle T. Ubando, Alvin B. Culaba, Rigoberto C. Advincula
items.title_zh: 竹炭生产路径对生物复合材料性能的影响
items.summary_zh: 本研究探讨了竹炭的碳化路径对聚乳酸（PLA）生物复合材料热性能和机械性能的影响。将竹源热解生物质（TBB）和炭化生物炭（PBB）以1 wt.%和2 wt.%的比例掺入PLA中。结果显示，PLA–TBB复合材料的拉伸刚度和弯曲性能显著提高，拉伸模量提高4.28%，弯曲强度提高18.72%，弯曲模量提高12.30%。而PLA–PBB复合材料则展现出最高的压缩强度，增加了29.53%。热分析表明，无论碳化路径如何，生物炭均引发冷结晶并略微改善PLA的热稳定性，PLA–PBB2的降解温度最高，PLA–PBB1的质量损失最低。这些结果表明，碳化路径影响竹炭的增强性能，低温热解生物质有利于拉伸和弯曲性能，而高温炭化生物炭则提供更优的压缩和热性能。

items.title: Chemputing the synthesis and optimisation of arene fluorination in an automated platform
items.abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) relies on the rapid and efficient incorporation of fluorine-18 (18F) into molecular imaging agents, yet selecting appropriate radiofluorination conditions for new substrates remains ad hoc. Whilst decades of development have generated a wealth of experimentally validated reactions, this knowledge remains dispersed throughout literature and is difficult to exploit systematically for reaction planning. Here the chemputation-enabled arene radiofluorination, that is optimization and automated execution, captures both reaction transformations and the associated experimental conditions, providing a foundation for reasoning. Three complementary levels of analysis are implemented to interrogate the knowledge base, progressing from molecular similarity and electronic descriptors, through reaction abstraction based on bond–electron matrices, to AI-assisted contextual reasoning. The recommended literature precedents provide experimentally informed starting points that are subsequently refined using an optimization algorithm, enabling efficient exploration of multidimensional reaction-condition space beyond direct literature transfer and the optimized procedure is executed on a robotic platform using the Chemical Description Language (χDL), establishing a continuous digital workflow from literature knowledge to reproducible chemical synthesis. By integrating curated reaction knowledge, computational reasoning, experimental optimization, and digital execution, this work provides a general framework for data-driven radiofluorination that reduces experimental trial-and-error while improving reproducibility, safety, and scalability in PET tracer development.
items.authors: Filippo Protti, Nathan Jiscoot, Nicholas Capittini, Christian Knittl-Frank, Dean Thomas, Alessio Porta
items.title_zh: 自动化平台上芳烃氟化合成与优化的化学计算
items.summary_zh: 正电子发射断层扫描（PET）依赖于氟-18（18F）快速有效地融入分子成像剂，但为新底物选择合适的放射氟化条件仍然是临时的。尽管数十年的发展产生了大量经过实验验证的反应，但这些知识散布在文献中，难以系统性地用于反应规划。本文提出了化学计算驱动的芳烃放射氟化方法，通过优化和自动执行，捕捉反应转化及相关实验条件，为推理提供基础。采用三种互补的分析层次来探讨知识库，从分子相似性和电子描述符，到基于键-电子矩阵的反应抽象，再到AI辅助的上下文推理。推荐的文献前例提供了实验信息支持的起始点，随后通过优化算法进行精炼，实现了多维反应条件空间的高效探索，并在机器人平台上执行优化程序，建立了从文献知识到可重复化学合成的连续数字工作流程。

items.title: Copper binding to glucagon and glucagon-like peptide 1: Relevance to diabetes
items.abstract: Glucagon (GCG) and glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP1) are hormones involved in maintaining glucose homeostasis. Diabetic patients display a chronic dysfunction of these hormones along with an increase in copper levels in the bloodstream. Although GCG(1–29) and GLP1(1–37) harbour Cu2+-anchoring groups at their N-terminal regions, their metal-binding properties have not been assesed, nor their implications in metal homeostasis/hormone function. In this study, spectroscopic tools (circular dichroism, electron paramagnetic resonance and X-ray absorption spectroscopy) were used to elucidate the Cu2+-binding properties of GCG and GLP1, and to assay the ability of these hormones to compete for the metal ion with the extracellular Cu2+-binding site of the Copper transporter 1 (CTR1)–the major source of copper uptake in mammalian cells–and Metformin–the Cu2+-binding drug used as first-line treatment for Type 2 diabetes. Our results show that Cu2+-binding to GCG(1–29) and GLP1(1–37) is highly dependent on metal-to-hormone ratio, yielding at least two different Cu2+ complexes (Modes I and II) depending on the metal-to-hormone ratio. Mode I, favoured at low metal-tohormone ratio, can efficiently transfer Cu2+ to the metal-binding site of CTR1, while Mode II can only do a partially transfer, suggesting that Cu2+-hormone speciation could impact metal homeostasis. Metformin can deliver Cu2+ to GCG and GLP1, indicating that this drug could buffer Cu2+ accumulation in the bloodstream in diabetes, without preventing Cu2+-hormone interactions. Altogether, this study elucidates metal-hormone interactions that are crucial to understand the role of Cu2+ in the pathophysiology of diabetes and paves the way for evaluating the potential of Metformin, and other drugs, as regulators of Cu2+-hormone interactions in diabetes.
items.authors: Yanahi Posadas, Carolina Sánchez-López, Victor E. López-Guerrero, Christophe Den Auwer, José Segovia, Liliana Quintanar

items.title: From Industrial lignin biomass waste to bio-based organic semiconductors for sustainable electronics: a proof of concept based on Vanillin
items.abstract: Developing sustainable, bio-based organic semiconductors from renewable aromatic feedstocks opens new possibilities for sustainable electronics. Here, the present work uses vanillin as a sustainable aromatic platform extracted from industrial lignin biomass waste, which is chemically transformed into a π-conjugated semiconductor. The resulting donor–acceptor–donor molecule, IsoInd-CO-diCzBu, combines reversible redox activity with high thermal stability. Complementary space-charge-limited current measurements and organic field-effect transistors successfully demonstrate hole transport in vertical devices and p-type field-effect operation. An indepth study combining gate-bias stress, thermal annealing, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction connects device behaviour with molecular structure. These encouraging results establish vanillin as a platform for developing a series of bio-based semiconductors whose molecular architecture can be tuned to improve charge transport.
items.authors: Kelvine Letellier, Charaf. E. Benaddi, Emilie Jehanno, Vamsi K. Narra, Olivier Jeannin, Cassandre Quinton
items.title_zh: 从工业木质素生物质废料到可持续电子的生物基有机半导体
items.summary_zh: 本研究利用从工业木质素生物质废料中提取的香草醛，开发可持续的生物基有机半导体。香草醛经过化学转化，形成了π-共轭半导体分子IsoInd-CO-diCzBu，该分子结合了可逆的氧化还原活性和高热稳定性。通过空间电荷限制电流测量和有机场效应晶体管，成功展示了垂直器件中的孔导电性和p型场效应操作。结合栅极偏压应力、热退火和单晶X射线衍射的深入研究，将器件行为与分子结构联系起来。这些结果表明，香草醛可作为开发一系列生物基半导体的平台，其分子结构可调以改善电荷传输。

items.title: New approach for deciphering polyethylene terephthalate (PET)-based plastics’ diols: Application on PET daily-life packaging objects paving their chemical modifications
items.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is a thermoplastic polyester synthetized from a terephthalic diacid and a diol which is generally ethylene glycol. Given PET prominence in food packaging industry, a detailed study of this polymer is of utmost importance. The identification of the initial diols constituting PET-based bottles and containers along with their structural modifications, due to recycling procedures and/or weathering, is still a challenging research subject. In this study, PET diols were derivatized using a new approach combining an innovative methanolysis-benzoylation methodology with analysis by Orbitrap MS. First, a transesterification with methanol for freeing diols and/or polyols was performed followed by a derivatization with 4-dimethylaminobenzoyl chloride (DMABC) used as benzoylation agent under specific conditions. After reaction post-treatment, the derivatized products were analyzed using ESI ionization on an Orbitrap MS hyphenated to liquid chromatography LC−MS. This method was applied to PET-based daily-life bottles and containers in comparison to authentic diols and copolyesters used as references, showing extra new data on their diols’ composition that may be affected by recycling, manufacturing procedures and/or natural weathering. These PET-based packaging objects were differentiated according to the detected diols along with their oxidized compounds and hydroxy acids. Other polyesters and copolyesters can be studied using this same new strategy.
items.authors: Bayan ALMASRI, Christian ROLANDO
items.title_zh: 新方法解析聚对苯二甲酸乙二醇酯（PET）塑料的二醇
items.summary_zh: 聚对苯二甲酸乙二醇酯（PET）是一种由对苯二甲酸和乙二醇合成的热塑性聚酯。鉴于PET在食品包装行业的重要性，深入研究该聚合物至关重要。本研究采用新方法，通过创新的甲醇解酯化-苯甲酰化方法结合Orbitrap质谱分析，鉴定PET瓶和容器中的初始二醇及其因回收和/或自然老化而产生的结构变化。首先进行甲醇转酯化以释放二醇和/或多元醇，随后在特定条件下使用4-二甲氨基苯甲酰氯（DMABC）进行苯甲酰化。反应后处理后，衍生化产品通过与液相色谱联用的ESI离子化Orbitrap质谱进行分析。该方法应用于PET日常瓶和容器，比较了真实二醇和共聚酯作为参考，显示出回收、制造过程和/或自然老化可能影响的二醇组成的新数据。

items.title: Elucidation of the Hematite Direct Reduction Mechanism Using In Situ Spectroscopy
items.abstract: Research on alternative energy storage technologies continues, especially in the grid-scale long duration space where traditional battery technologies (including lithium-ion) suffer from either cost or safety concerns. Conversion anodes leveraging multi-valent iron promise high capacities, but key microscopic details of the mechanism for conversion are unknown. Towards this objective, this study aims to use in situ electrochemical cells combined with NMR and EPR spectroscopy to search for reaction intermediates directly, expanding on previous studies where largely ex situ methods or carefully constructed surfaces and morphologies were employed. Performing the spectroscopic measurements under realistic electrochemical cell conditions which maximize the reaction conditions (strongly alkaline media, elevated temperatures 60 °C) and using synthetic hematite aggregates demonstrated i) a lack of dissolved Fe3+ and ii) the presence of solvated Fe2+ species which scaled with applied current density. Leveraging ex situ Mössbauer spectroscopy in combination with the in situ measurements yielded evidence for an initial reduction step of Fe3+ to Fe2+ within the hematite structure. Collectively, these findings point to a solid-state reduction mechanism for hematite via a maghemite intermediate, followed by rupture and dissolution/reduction, with the steady-state solvated Fe2+ concentration gradually dissipating after the applied potential is removed. Detailed mechanistic knowledge will help inform future efforts to engineer further improvements to the direct electrochemical iron oxide reduction process.
items.authors: Casey S. Mezerkor, Ravi K. Kukkadapu, Carinna L. Lapson, Mark Bowden, Raj Shekhar, Eric D. Walter
items.title_zh: 利用原位光谱法阐明赤铁矿直接还原机制
items.summary_zh: 针对替代能源存储技术的研究持续进行，尤其是在传统电池技术（如锂离子电池）面临成本或安全问题的长时间持续储能领域。利用多价铁的转换阳极具有高容量的潜力，但其转换机制的关键微观细节尚不清楚。本研究旨在结合原位电化学池与核磁共振（NMR）和电子顺磁共振（EPR）光谱法直接寻找反应中间体，扩展以往主要采用外部方法的研究。通过在强碱性介质和60°C高温下进行光谱测量，使用合成赤铁矿聚集体，发现i）缺乏溶解的Fe3+，ii）存在与施加电流密度成比例的溶剂化Fe2+物种。结合外部Mössbauer光谱法与原位测量的结果表明，赤铁矿结构中Fe3+的初始还原步骤为Fe2+。这些发现指向通过磁赤铁矿中间体的固态还原机制，随后发生断裂和溶解/还原，稳态溶剂化Fe2+浓度。

items.title: VIBE-VIEW and QVF: portable visualization and checksummed archives for quantum chemistry
items.abstract: Quantum-chemistry results often span separate files for structures, orbitals, scalar fields, and spectra. We present VIBE-VIEW, a viewer for molecular and periodic calculations, and QVF (Quantum Visualization Format), its producer-neutral archive format. QVF combines visualization data with provenance, citations, and optional job specifications and run records in one ZIP file. A JSON manifest declares payload formats and SHA-256 checksums, with dtypes and shapes for numeric arrays. Consumers verify payload integrity before use and explicitly report unsupported extensions. A published schema, extension registry, and twelve-archive conformance corpus support independent implementations. VIBE-VIEW provides renderers or panels for 41 of 42 canonical kinds, with bonds incorporated into structure rendering. Browser, desktop, terminal, headless, notebook, and Python interfaces support inspection and figure generation from the same archive, without requiring installation of the original producer. A water calculation demonstrates the workflow. VIBE-VIEW is licensed under MPL-2.0; the QVF specification and reference writer toolkit use Apache-2.0. Graphical TOC summary. QVF combines molecular and crystal structures, orbitals, spectra, and calculation provenance in one checksummed file. The VIBE-VIEW application opens these archives through interactive and scripted interfaces, supporting inspection and figure generation without installing the original calculation program.
items.authors: Michael F. Peintinger

items.title: Tryptophan-induced nanometrization and hydrophobization of Fe 2+ /Fe 3+ oxyhydroxide green rust crystals enable their insertion into lipid particles
items.abstract: Compartmentalization and metabolic activity are recognized as intrinsic and essential to both extant life and the first protocells. Minerals found in early-Earth hydrothermal settings, such as the Fe 2+/3+ oxyhydroxide green rust (GR), are not only expected to have promoted the formation and assembly of amphiphiles into vesicles, but also to have acted as precursors of current membrane-embedded bioenergetic enzymes. In a previous paper, we identified nanometric size and surface hydrophobicity as two crucial properties for the embedment of GRCO 3 crystals in amphiphile-based vesicles, and demonstrated their acquisition upon exposure to two components of early hydrothermal settings: nickel and tryptophan. Here, we used lipids as model amphiphiles to systematically investigate how the evolution of size and hydrophobicity parameters in GRCO 3 crystals affects their interaction with free lipids and lipid-based particles, and identify the nature of the resulting GRCO 3 -lipid hybrid systems. By leveraging cryo-electron microscopy as well as zeta potential and Laurdan generalized polarization measurements, we demonstrate that modulations of two parameters are sufficient to drastically modify the fate of GRCO 3 -lipid hybrid systems. Size alone defines the directionality of adsorption processes between electrostatically-compatible GRCO 3 crystals and liposomes, yielding intricate mineral-organic interfaces. Subsequent variations in the surface hydrophobicity of the crystals not only orient the assembly of interacting lipids towards either liposomes or lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), but also enable their embedding within the hydrophobic core of both these lipid-based particles. These results suggest that GRCO 3 would have played numerous roles in the emergence of the first energized protocells, from promoting the synthesis of amphiphiles and their assembly into vesicles to embedding within the latter, thus enhancing them with redox and proto-metabolic properties. These new hybrid systems constitute both ideal tools to experimentally assess the proton-coupled electron transfers that were theorized to happen in the interlayers of GR, and promising platforms for therapeutical or depollution applications.
items.authors: Nil Gaudu, Orion Farr, Daniel Ferry, Georges Ona-Nguema, François Guyot, Wolfgang Nitschke
items.title_zh: 色氨酸诱导的绿锈晶体纳米化与疏水化促进其嵌入脂质颗粒
items.summary_zh: 本研究探讨了Fe 2+/3+ 氧氢氧化物绿锈（GRCO 3）晶体的纳米化和疏水化对其与脂质颗粒相互作用的影响。我们使用脂质作为模型表面活性剂，系统研究了GRCO 3晶体在与游离脂质和脂质颗粒相互作用时，尺寸和疏水性参数的演变。通过冷冻电子显微镜、ζ电位和Laurdan广义极化测量，我们发现这两个参数的调节足以显著改变GRCO 3-脂质混合体系的命运。尺寸的变化决定了电静电兼容的GRCO 3晶体与脂质体之间的吸附过程方向，形成复杂的矿物-脂质混合体系。

items.title: Meropenem degradation does not necessarily eliminate antibacterial activity: responses of model and environmental bacterial isolates
items.abstract: Carbapenems can degrade rapidly in aquatic systems, and disappearance of the parent compound is often interpreted as loss of antibacterial activity. Here, we compared the antibacterial effects of intact meropenem with those of a meropenem mixture incubated for eight days in the presence of biofilm-covered moving-bed biofilm reactor carriers. During incubation, parent meropenem became undetectable, while several transformation products (TPs) retaining a closed β-lactam ring, a key structural feature for antibacterial activity, formed and persisted through the incubation period. The intact antibiotic and the incubated meropenem mixture containing TPs were tested against Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas fluorescens and two environmental isolates, CIS1 and CIR3, using optical density and viable cell counts. While intact meropenem strongly reduced viable counts of E. coli, P. fluorescens and CIS1, CIR3 was able to grow in its presence. In contrast, the incubated meropenem TPs mixture exhibited lower toxicity overall. Little or no TP inhibition was detected for P. fluorescens and E. coli, while CIS1 showed a weaker and time-dependent response. CIR3 was not suppressed by the mixture. Although the observed responses were subtle, the results show that disappearance of parent meropenem does not necessarily coincide with complete loss of meropenem-derived biological effects. The findings highlight that meropenem TPs should be considered when evaluating the environmental relevance of meropenem degradation and its potential contribution to selective pressure of antibiotics.
items.authors: Alba Martinez i Quer, Florin Krijom, Antoine Maurel, Anders Johansen, Vaidotas Kisielius

items.title: Autonomous Robotic Workflow for Solution-Based Synthesis and High-Temperature Thermal Processing toward Self-Driving Laboratories
items.abstract: The growing need has pushed the development of autonomous laboratory automation for high-throughput materials research. Although self-driving laboratories (SDL) and automated liquid handling have advanced significantly, robotic material handling remains poorly integrated with high-temperature thermal processes. In this study, a solution-based synthesis autonomous robotic process was designed, developed, calibrated, and validated. Two cooperative robotic arms, a bespoke pneumatic pipetting end-effector, an RS485-controlled syringe pump, a modular crucible assembly, and automated furnace control were all integrated into the developed platform via a centralised Python-based architecture that uses Modbus TCP and RTU communication. The system handles liquid dispensing, sample mixing, robotic transfer, furnace loading, thermal treatment, controlled cooling, and sample retrieval on an independent basis. Deionised (DI) water, ethanol, and zirconium (Zr) acetate solution were used to calibrate the dispensing system to assess performance across liquids with various physical characteristics. With dispensing accuracy of 98.4%, all liquids showed excellent linearity between scheduled and dispensed quantities. After fluid-specific calibration, an error propagation study showed strong mechanical repeatability and predictable systematic error buildup, validating the system's capability for dependable automated precursor production. The independent synthesis of gadolinium zirconate (Gd2Zr2O7), a highly sought-after thermal barrier coating (TBC) composition for the next generation of aero gas turbines, was used to test the entire operation. The robotic platform effectively completed precursor dispensing, solution homogenisation, furnace processing at 1600 °C, controlled cooling, and sample recovery.
items.authors: Mohammadreza Lalegani Dezaki, Pushpender Singh, Dominic Price, Vikram Hastak, Rajib Das, Tanvir Hussain
items.title_zh: 面向自驾实验室的自主机器人工作流程研究
items.summary_zh: 随着对高通量材料研究的需求增加，自主实验室自动化的发展愈发重要。尽管自驾实验室（SDL）和自动液体处理技术已取得显著进展，但机器人材料处理与高温热处理的整合仍显不足。本研究设计、开发、校准并验证了一种基于溶液合成的自主机器人流程。该平台集成了两个协作机器人臂、定制的气动移液末端执行器、RS485控制的注射泵、模块化坩埚组件和自动化炉控制，采用基于Python的集中架构，通过Modbus TCP和RTU通信实现。系统能够独立处理液体分配、样品混合、机器人转移、炉加载、热处理、控制冷却和样品回收。通过去离子水、乙醇和醋酸锆溶液对分配系统进行校准，结果显示分配精度为98.4%，所有液体在计划与分配量之间表现出良好的线性关系。经过特定流体的校准，误差传播研究表明系统具有良好的机械重复性和可预测的系统误差积累，验证了系统的能力。

items.title: Combined Enhanced Conformational Sampling and Protein-Ligand Dockings on CYP3A4 Improves in Silico Prediction of Drug Metabolism
items.abstract: Cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP3A4) is the primary drug-metabolizing enzyme in humans. This is largely due to its highly flexible structure, which enables it to bind a broad spectrum of xenobiotics with a wide variety of shapes and physicochemical properties. This plasticity, however, presents challenges for in silico substrate prediction methods, in particular those that consider only a limited conformational space of the receptor or that rely on static crystal structures. In this study, we aim to explore the conformational landscape of CYP3A4 using Gaussian accelerated Molecular Dynamics (GaMD) and then to assess the viability of using this method to identify pro-reactive conformations through protein-ligand docking. GaMD simulations were initiated from distinct X-ray structures in triplicate 500 ns runs. The results demonstrate that the simulations cover a very large conformational space, including all reported X-ray structures as well as conformations with significantly expanded active-site geometries unseen in the experimental data. Protein-ligand docking of known CYP3A4 substrates onto the main cluster representatives from GaMD simulations allows the identification of metabolically active poses of the substrates. This is true even in cases where substrate-bound X-ray structures or docking against a single structure fails to yield productive results, as in the case of CYP3A4–Erythromycin. Furthermore, a classifier trained on ensemble docking scores discriminates CYP3A4 substrates from non-substrates better than any single conformation (ROC-AUC 0.735 vs 0.697), with performance increasing with ensemble size. Overall, the study shows that enhanced conformational sampling is crucial for accurately modelling highly flexible enzymes like CYP3A4 and can significantly improve metabolic predictions.
items.authors: Yassir Boulaamane, Christopher M. Baker, Lea Talmann, Jean-Didier Marechal

items.title: Estimand Divergence: Static Docking Versus Dynamics for Antimalarial Triage
items.abstract: We evaluated a multi-target docking framework in 136 docking systems spanning wildtype and mutant PfDHFR/PfCRT states, built from 396 African natural products and 454 synthetic antimalarials.A Resistance-Resilience Score stratified the primary cohort (n = 12) into five tiers that decouple wild-type binding from mutant-state retention.Explicit-solvent MD diverged directionally from static docking in 87.5 % (7/8; 95% Wilson CI 52.9-97.8%) of matched states: dynamic pocket relaxation retained poses that static grid scores penalized.Two external checks bounded this signal: DEKOIS 2.0 PfDHFR scoring was at chance level (ROC-AUC 0.450), and rigid ∆∆G did not track published mutant fold-shifts (direction agreement 28.6-41.7 %; 24-28 compounds per genotype).At single-replicate scope this divergence is a protocol-local calibration signal: static scores and short trajectories are complementary, non-equivalent triage metrics.
items.authors: Myke Vital SAO TEMGOUA, Jean-Pierre TCHAPET NJAFA, Penabei SAMAFOU, Fon Wilfred MBACHAM, Serge Guy NANA ENGO

items.title: Interfacial Solvent Engineering of Zinc Porphyrin Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks Enables Aggregation-Enhanced Electrochemiluminescence for Synthetic Cannabinoid Sensing
items.abstract: Zinc porphyrin hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (ZnTCPP HOFs) are prone to uncontrolled short-range π–π stacking at solid/liquid interfaces, which leads to aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) and consequently limits their electrochemiluminescence (ECL) efficiency. Current strategies for suppressing ACQ primarily depend on covalent or coordination bonds and often involve laborious synthesis. Addressing this challenge from the perspective of colloid and interface science, this study introduces a chitosan (CS)–DMF counter-solvent precipitation strategy. This approach reorganizes the hydrogen-bond network and fosters electrostatic association between CS and the carboxyl groups of ZnTCPP HOFs, thereby facilitating a controlled transformation of bulk crystals into micro/nano-aggregates. This synergistic effect suppresses short-range π–π stacking while enhancing long-range aggregation-induced emission (AIE), leading to a significant improvement in ECL efficiency without the need for an additional co-reaction promoter. On this basis, an aptamer-based ECL sensor was developed for the ultrasensitive detection of 5F-EDMB-PINACA, achieving a limit of detection of 8.61 × 10 -16 g/L and a linear range spanning nine orders of magnitude. These findings underscore the efficacy of colloidal-interface regulation in ECL sensing.
items.authors: Yanpei Zhang, Ding Jiang, Bingxue Fan, Mingyang Han, Suran Tian, Haibo Li

items.title: Utilization of heuristic approaches and molecular modelling to visualise chemical reactivity in small student groups
items.abstract: According to current psychometric analyses, a vast majority of novices in universities mostly utilize algorithmic mental processes to solve given tasks and tests. Although algorithmic thinking is an essential part of brain functions, experts on didactics call for methods which also develop conceptual thinking in beginners. In this sense, heuristic molecular modelling plays an important role in chemistry education since it inherently employs several conceptual thinking principles. Herein, we present eight different molecular modelling tasks of Diels-Alder reactions to develop understanding of the concept of chemical reactivity in undergraduate students of chemistry. The aim of this study is to provide teachers of chemistry with an example lesson utilizing heuristic education techniques and molecular modelling. The present study was evaluated in a university course on advanced organic chemistry for students in the third year of a chemistry master program. Interviews with the involved students and analyses of the applied pre/post didactical tests show that the proposed lesson has a positive impact on the understanding of basic chemical concepts related with chemical reactivity and Diels-Alder reaction.
items.authors: Rafael Dolezal, Natálie Karásková, Nadezhda V. Maltsevskaya, Karel Kolář

items.title: High-Spin Diradical-Dominated Chemiluminescence
items.abstract: We report a quantum-chemical investigation into the chemiluminescence mechanism of cyclometalated Ir (III) Schiff base complexes, promising chemiluminophores for biological imaging. The reaction proceeds via ring-opening of a key oxaziridine intermediate to yield a singlet diradical, which undergoes rapid intersystem crossing (ISC) to its triplet counterpart, followed by deprotonation to generate the emissive triplet product. Within this process, the Ir (III) center not only activates the imine via Lewis-acid coordination but also reverses the singlet-triplet energy ordering of the diradical intermediate, rendering the triplet diradical thermodynamically favored with an equilibrium population of ca. 86% at ambient temperature. The heavy-atom effect of iridium provides substantial spin-orbit coupling; combined with a low-lying minimum-energy crossing point (MECP, 1.7 kcal mol -1 ) and large Franck-Condon-weighted density of states, this accelerates ISC to a rate of 1.5 × 1011 s -1 . Notably, the two radical centers are separated by an 𝑠𝑝3-hybridized carbon, and the intervening C-H bond is strongly polarized by the adjacent O-centered radical, rendering deprotonation nearly barrierless. These collective computational findings establish design principles for two distinct goals: stabilizing diradical species to extend their lifetimes for EPR characterization, and informing the rational development of non-precious-metal chemiluminescent systems.
items.authors: Heng-Ding Wang, Ziyan Ye, Chiyuan Wei, Wei Fang, Mingle Li, Xiaoqiang Chen

items.title: From Peroxides to Qubits: Using Glow-Stick Chemistry to Introduce Excited States, Conical Intersections, and Quantum Computing to Undergraduates
items.abstract: Glow sticks provide a familiar and visually striking entry point to chemiluminescence and excited-state chemistry. We present a self-contained computational teaching module that uses peroxide bond breaking to introduce multireference electronic structure, conical intersections, and quantum computing. In a Jupyter/Google Colab notebook, students first stretch the O–O bond of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and observe the emergence of biradical character. They then examine 1,2-dioxetane as a tractable model for cyclic-peroxide decomposition, using state-averaged complete active space self-consistent field (SA-CASSCF) calculations to explore near-degenerate electronic states and examine the local conical topology of an S0/S1 intersection. The resulting active-space problem is then represented on a quantum simulator using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and the subspace-search VQE (SSVQE), and finally extended to state-averaged orbital-optimized VQE (SA-OO-VQE), in which the orbitals are optimized as well. The activity emphasizes that quantum algorithms are motivated by the structure of challenging multireference problems rather than presented as immediate replacements for classical methods. Designed for one 2–3 h laboratory session or two 75-min recitations, the module requires no advanced quantum mechanics or computer-science background and includes learning objectives, assessment questions, implementation guidance, and a complete tested notebook.
items.authors: Seenivasan Hariharan

items.title: Polarization-Driven Hydride Transfer Promotes Cobalt Tetrasulfophthalocyanine-Catalyzed Hydrogen Evolution by Five Orders of Magnitude
items.abstract: The hydricity of M–H intermediates is a key descriptor and optimization target for the rational design of molecular hydrogen evolution electrocatalysts. Adsorption to an electrode surface is known to augment catalytic rate, but it remains unclear how adsorption affects M-H hydricity. Herein, we quantitatively compare the catalytic activity and mechanism of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) from cobalt tetrasulfophthalocyanine (CoTSPc) in a dissolved aqueous form (CoTSPc (aq) ) and when adsorbed to the surface of a carbon electrode (CoTSPc/C). At the same electrode potential, CoTSPc/C catalyzes HER at a rate that is over five orders of magnitude faster than CoTSPc (aq) . Mechanistic studies indicate that both CoTSPc/C and CoTSPc (aq) catalyze HER via a rate-limiting hydride transfer to a proton donor in solution to form H 2 . Hydride transfer from Co-H in CoTSPc (aq) is a purely chemical step defined by a constant hydricity of 22.4 kcal mol −1 that is independent of applied potential. In contrast, hydride transfer from Co-H in CoTSPc/C is strongly polarization dependent, decreasing hydricity by ~23 kcal mol −1 V −1 to values as low as 1.2 kcal mol −1 at −1.1 V vs SHE, leading to the observed rate promotion. We attribute this mechanistic change to the positioning of the CoTSPc-H intermediate within the electrochemical double layer, such that the hydride traverses the interfacial electrostatic potential difference during the RLS. These results demonstrate the power of surface adsorption to generate highly reactive molecular hydrides and fundamentally reshape the free energy landscape of electrocatalysis.
items.authors: Joel G. Gardner, Jon A. Kephart, Vennela Mannava, Yogesh Surendranath

items.title: Green-function thimbles for internal conversion
items.abstract: Oscillatory real-time integrals and the complete quadratic transformation between electronic-state normal modes are persistent obstacles in molecular internal-conversion calculations. We develop a finite-temperature Tyablikov–Moskalenko Green-function formulation that retains unequal frequencies, equilibrium displacement, Duschinsky rotation, the anomalous squeezing block, and a general first-order Herzberg–Teller nonadiabatic operator. The closed equations of motion reconstruct the vibronic correlation function by coupling-constant integration, while analytic continuation to complex time permits both a systematic saddle expansion and globally controlled integration on Lefschetz thimbles without numerical damping. For the 102-mode tetraoxa[8]circulene (4B) model at 300 K, the complete rate is 1.656× 10 7 s −1 at 18500 cm −1 . Herzberg–Teller coupling and Duschinsky rotation increase the rate by factors of approximately 2.45 and 2.06, respectively, while the squeezing contribution is about 46% in the mode-mixed calculation. The next-to-leading saddle result differs from the full thimble value by 0.66% at the molecular gap; one contributing thimble and no Stokes transition are found throughout 5000–35000 cm −1 . The same formalism gives aligned electric-and magnetic-field thresholds of 1.06 × 108 V m −1 and 41.6 T. The method therefore provides a fast, damping-free route to complete harmonic vibronic rates together with an explicit global test of the integration contour.
items.authors: Rashid Valiev

items.title: Chirality Relay via Non-stereogenic Carbocations: from Stereogenic Alcohol to Twisted Tricyclic Skeleton
items.abstract: Stereogenic carbon loses its stereochemistry when it is converted into planar carbocation. Retention of the chirality is difficult unless static reference chirality is introduced within reactant to change the reactions diastereoselective. Herein we report a rare reaction in which a stereogenic alcohol gives a chiral twisted tricyclic skeleton by acid-mediated dehydrative cyclization. The intermediates are carbocations without any stereogenic centers, and their non-stereogenic conformational features relay the chiral information to the product. The chiral twist is computed to be flexible in the alcohol reactant and initial carbocation intermediate, but it is induced through the reaction steps to acquire thermal robustness. This chirality relay also provides an effective synthetic method for each enantiomer of the product, which is a valuable intrinsically chiral building block.
items.authors: Kenichi Kato, Nagisa Kawabata, Yori Kajiwara, Tatsuya Nishimura, Katsuhiro Maeda, Shunsuke Ohtani

items.title: Efficient Customizable Synthesis Planning with Graph Grammars, with an application to Elastase B inhibitor candidates
items.abstract: Computer-assisted synthesis planning (CASP) software allows experimentalists to streamline setups and reduce unsuccessful experiments. CASP has a long history, yet remains an active research area. Although various tools have been developed and published, few have remained publicly available and continue to be supported. Those available at no-cost typically operate on generalized global databases, ignoring domain-or laboratory-specific constraints. Here, we present LAGER, a graph-grammar-based retrosynthesis engine built on the Double Pushout (DPO) formalism of the MØD framework. Retrosynthetic pathways are resolved by a state-based A∗ search with a weighted evaluation function. The path cost, g(n), penalizes pathway length and chemoselectivity risks from competing side reactions, whereas the heuristic h(n) estimates chemical distance to available reactants using fragment-based synthetic accessibility score (SAscore) to prioritize structurally simpler precursors and limit search-space expansion. LAGER is designed to accelerate synthesis planning for subsequent generations of a specific compound series by leveraging synthetic knowledge from previous generations. Its reaction library therefore comprises well-established reactions routinely used within a particular laboratory alongside readily available starting materials. We evaluate LAGER on a benchmark of 109 investigated inhibitors of elastase B (LasB), a key virulence factor of the Gram-negative bacterium Pseudomonas aeruginosa. With appropriate heuristic weighting, LAGER recovers the experimentally used pathway among Top-3 proposed pathways for up to 81% of targets. Importantly, deviation from the reported route did not imply chemical infeasibility: at least one chemically valid pathway was identified within the Top-3 candidates for 98% of targets. However, our results indicate limitations of SAscore as a chemical distance metric for targeted retrosynthesis, highlighting the need for more robust, computationally efficient alternatives. Comparison with AiZynthFinder using identical starting materials further demonstrated the importance of laboratory-specific reaction knowledge, as general reactiontemplate sets rarely reproduced the complete literature route for the investigated compounds and often included only a subset of the key transformations in the proposed pathways. Scientific Contribution. This work demonstrates the value of incorporating laboratory-specific reaction knowledge into automated retrosynthetic planning. Unlike general-purpose approaches, LAGER explicitly encodes domain-specific transformations within an interpretable graph-grammar-based search framework, providing a customizable approach for synthesis planning within a defined chemical space.
items.authors: Arina Shelashen, Thomas Gatter, Charlotte R. O’Donnell, Angeliki Vgenopoulou, Anna K. H. Hirsch, Peter F. Stadler

items.title: Reversible Ion Transport Through an Irreversibly Percolating Li 2 S Interphase at the Li/Li 6 PS 5 Cl Interface
items.abstract: Interfacial resistance growth between Li metal and sulfide solid electrolytes is a leading cause of failure in solid-state batteries, yet the atomic-scale processes that govern this growth under an electrochemical driving force are poorly resolved. Herein, we combine a fine-tuned machine-learning interatomic potential with dynamically updated atomic charges to simulate the Li/Li 6 PS 5 Cl interface for nanoseconds under both field-free and electric-field-driven conditions. Without a field, the electrolyte decomposes spontaneously into a Li 2 S-rich interphase whose thickness follows square-root-of-time kinetics, consistent with diffusion-limited growth. Applying a field to the same initial interface accelerates this growth nearly seven-fold and converts the entire electrolyte slab within ∼100 ps. In both cases, the Li 2 S-like product forms a single connected network, while Li 3 P-and LiCl-like decomposition products remain confined to small, disconnected clusters. Although reversing the field reverses the direction of Li flux almost immediately, the percolating Li 2 S network persists unchanged and the argyrodite coordination does not recover. This decoupling shows that structural memory, not instantaneous transport direction, determines the interphase that Li ions actually cross. Because this connectivity survives stripping, our results suggest that anode-interface resistance and reactivity in solid-state batteries are set early in cycling and are not reset by current reversal.
items.authors: Tianmu Yuan, Zhimin Chen, James A. Dawson

items.title: From Bulk Hygroscopicity to Nanoscale Water Activity: Breakdown of Continuum Theories in Sub-4 nm Secondary Organic Aerosols
items.abstract: Interactions between water and organic molecules in sub-10 nm clusters surrounded by air play a key role in the chemistry and microphysics of secondary organic aerosol (SOA). However, water-organic interactions in such small clusters are difficult to probe experimentally and remain poorly constrained. Here, we use molecular dynamics simulations to examine morphology, molecular interactions, and water evaporation energetics of nanoclusters formed by nine representative SOA compounds across sizes and water contents. Nanocluster water affinity depends on size and water content, with distinct controlling mechanisms emerging during RH-driven drying. At high and moderate water contents, clusters larger than 4 nm follow a Kelvin baseline based on their bulk-mixture surface tension. In contrast, sub-4 nm organic-shell clusters sometimes retain water much less strongly than expected based on the Kelvin relation as their phase-mixing state changes with cluster size. At low water content, loss of water-network connectivity fragments the water domain into isolated pockets, shifting control of water retention to specific water-organic and water–water interactions, ionic coordination, and steric accessibility, producing species-dependent water affinity that bulk hygroscopicity cannot predict. These results identify where continuum descriptions break down and inform the representation of water in SOA nanoclusters in atmospheric models.
items.authors: Jiaqi Wen, Xiaohan Li, Ian C. Bourg

items.title: Orthogonal Perturbations Resolve a Robust High-Frequency Relaxation in Nanocrystal-Derived Ag₄Zr₃S₈ Assemblies
items.abstract: Nanocrystal (NC)-derived ion-conducting solids combine compositionally tunable nanoscale building blocks with dense networks of particle–particle and electrode contacts, making it difficult to distinguish material-associated relaxation dynamics from assembly-dependent impedance. Here, colloidally synthesized Ag₄Zr₃S₈ NCs are consolidated into pellets and interrogated by pressure- and temperature-resolved electrochemical impedance spectroscopy using Ag + -blocking (Au) and Ag + non-blocking (Ag) contacts. An objective discontinuity criterion is used to identify a continuous high-frequency analysis window, which is evaluated by Bayesian Hilbert-transform diagnostics and distribution-of-relaxation-times (DRT) analysis. Across 0.43–8.67 MPa and 298–393 K, Au-contacted pellets exhibit a dominant sample-associated relaxation centered near tau ~ 10⁻⁶ s. The dominant mode remains within the microsecond relaxation-time regime across the investigated pressure and temperature ranges, while both its characteristic time and spectral weight vary non-monotonically with the applied perturbation. The same fast response persists after changing Au to Ag contacts and pellet preparation history, whereas slower DRT features are more configuration-sensitive. A frequency-matched dummy-cell control exhibits its principal relaxation approximately one decade later in time. These results demonstrate how orthogonal mechanical, thermal, electrode, and assembly perturbations can distinguish sample-associated relaxation dynamics from configuration-sensitive impedance in NC-derived chalcogenide solids.
items.authors: Yunhao Xu, Isabella Campbell, Oluwaseyi Saliu, Simran Choudhary, Progna Banerjee

items.title: Programmable Uniform Gel Networks Amplify Weak Interactions via Multiple Anchoring for In Situ Growth of Gold Nanoparticles
items.abstract: Synthesizing ultrasmall thermoresponsive nanoparticles within poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPA) hydrogels without the use of strong ligands remains challenging, as intrinsically weak interfacial interactions and structural heterogeneity in conventional networks often lead to poor size control and aggregation. Here, we report a programmable PNIPA-based hydrogel constructed from star-shaped polymers via living radical polymerization, in which a homogeneous network containing locally reinforced crosslinking domains enables ligand-free in situ formation of ultrasmall metal nanoparticles. The uniform network provides a spatially consistent reaction environment, allowing synchronized and controllable particle growth across length scales. Nanoparticle size is governed by network architecture rather than by synthetic conditions, and the resulting hydrogel composites exhibit exceptional stability under thermal cycling and harsh chemical environments, despite relying solely on amide functionalities. Stabilization does not arise from rigid immobilization or strong ligand coordination along the polymer chains; instead, it emerges from the collective engagement of multiple spatially distributed, amide-enriched crosslinking domains. These reinforced domains generate a cooperative multiple-anchoring effect, creating a soft yet adaptive chelation-like confinement. This work establishes a versatile platform for strong-ligand-free yet robust and controllable nanoparticle synthesis, extendable to colloidal dispersions, diverse polymer matrices, and various metal nanoparticles.
items.authors: Yian Wang, Junjia Zhang, Kazutaka Akiyoshi, Guohao Gao, Yinglu Liu, Kai Kawabata

items.title: StereoAtlas: A Large-Scale Dataset of Chiral Compounds with Distinct Bioactivities Curated from ChEMBL37
items.abstract: Stereoisomers share identical two-dimensional molecular topology and exhibit a Tanimoto similarity score of exactly 1.0 under standard fingerprint methods, rendering their bioactivity differences invisible to conventional data-driven or physics-based activity prediction approaches. Here, we present StereoAtlas, a dataset of 155,526 experimentally measured true isomer families derived from ChEMBL37, in which paired or families of stereoisomers exhibited pharmacological activity for the same biological target, in the same organism. Fold differences in activity between stereoforms were computed under two complementary strategies — MinMax and reference-form— and classified into five stereoselectivity tiers: None ( 2×), Mild (2–5×), Moderate (5–10×), Strong (10–50×), and Extreme ( 50×). Among 38,446 IC50 families, 9.5% exceed the 50-fold Extreme threshold, and the maximum fold difference observed is 195,000,000× at the oxytocin receptor (Kd) for the stereoisomeric families CHEMBL386547 (potent isomer) and its inactive counterparts (CHEMBL274635 and CHEMBL414373). Spanning 420,721 unique compounds, 4,519 biological targets, 471 organisms, and 879 activity types, this dataset provides a detailed, systematic, large-scale experimental resource for chirality cliff-based analysis. All data and pipeline scripts are publicly available.
items.authors: Saisaran Thangaraj, N. Arul Murugan, Arul Murugan Natarajan

items.title: Quantifying the Rate Performance of 3D-Printed LFP Electrodes from Water-Based Inks
items.abstract: Additive manufacturing enables the fabrication of battery electrodes with controlled architectures that can mitigate transport limitations at high activematerial loadings. In this work, water-based lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4, LFP) inks containing carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) as binder were processed by doctor-blade coating (DB) and direct ink writing (DIW) to fabricate planar and 3D-structured electrodes. Planar electrodes produced by both deposition methods exhibited comparable apparent porosity, tortuosity, electronic conductivity, and rate performance, confirming that the DIW process itself did not introduce a measurable electrochemical penalty.
