items.abstract: The aim of this work is to provide an iterative process for generating new monotonic properties for positive solutions of the second-order delay differential equation y″(t)+p(t)y(τ(t))=0, which will lead to the improvement of known oscillatory criteria.
items.authors: Blanka Baculikova, Jozef Dzurina

items.title: Targeted DNA Sequencing Reveals Distinct Rare-Variant Profiles in Pulmonary Hypertension Associated with Chronic Lung Diseases
items.abstract: The mechanisms underlying the development and severity of pulmonary hypertension (PH) in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and interstitial lung disease (ILD) remain poorly understood. To investigate the contribution of genetic factors, we performed targeted sequencing of PH-related genes in 63 patients with COPD, 51 with ILD, and 38 with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH), stratifying COPD and ILD patients according to PH severity, assessed by right heart catheterisation. Patients with ILD-associated PH harboured fewer genetic variants than those without PH, whereas an opposite trend was observed in COPD-associated PH. Variants of uncertain significance (VUS) in PAH-associated genes (BMPR2, BMPR1B) were identified in two out of 28 patients with severe COPD-PH and in one with nonsevere ILD-PH (SMAD9). VUS in extracellular matrix-related genes (THBS1, LOXL2) were also identified in four patients with severe COPD-PH, and in inflammatory-related genes (TNFAIP6) in two patients with ILD-PH. Pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in PAH-associated genes were exclusive to IPAH. We conclude that there is limited genetic overlap between COPD-PH and ILD-PH, with a stronger genetic contribution to PH in COPD, particularly in its severe form, where a subset of patients carries VUS in PAH-associated genes or genes involved in vascular remodelling.
items.authors: Adelaida Bosacoma, Agustín R. Garcia, Irene Madrigal, Juan-José Lozano, Julia Sidorova, Daniel Aguilar

items.title: Design and Optimization of an Asymmetric CLLC Resonant Converter with Interleaved Totem-Pole Front-End for Wide Voltage Range Single-Stage EV Charging
items.abstract: The increasing adoption of 800 V-class electric vehicles has created strong demand for single-stage onboard chargers capable of operating over a wide output voltage range while maintaining high efficiency and power density. This paper presents the design and multi-objective optimization of a single-stage bidirectional AC-DC converter that integrates a three-phase interleaved totem-pole front-end with an asymmetric CLLC resonant converter. The proposed topology eliminates large electrolytic DC-bus capacitors by using only small film capacitors and enables seamless operation across an ultra-wide battery voltage range of 100–850 V. The asymmetric CLLC parameters were optimized using a combination of fundamental harmonic approximation (FHA), time-domain analysis (TDA), and multi-objective particle swarm optimization (PSO) to achieve high voltage gain, wide zero-voltage switching (ZVS), and high efficiency. Simulations show a peak efficiency of 97.1%, an input-current THD of 2.8%, primary ZVS down to about 18% load, and bidirectional (V2G) operation. The design is a candidate for 800 V-class onboard chargers that must cover 100–850 V.
items.authors: Guobing Pan, Alberto Lizardo, Li Pan

items.title: Comparative Characterization of α-Carbonic Anhydrases from Bacteria Aeromonas hydrophila, Halomonas binhaiensis, and Roseibium salinum: Insights into Halotolerance and Thermostability
items.abstract: Halotolerant enzymes are promising biocatalysts for industrial applications due to their ability to function under high salinity and temperature conditions that typically inactivate conventional enzymes. This is particularly relevant for biomineralization-based carbon capture, where carbonic anhydrases (CAs) catalyze the reversible hydration of CO2 but often lack stability in harsh environments such as brine. Here, α-CA genes from three halotolerant bacteria, Aeromonas hydrophila (AhCA), Halomonas binhaiensis (HbCA), and Roseibium salinum (RsCA), were cloned and expressed, and the corresponding enzymes were purified and characterized. Enzymatic activity was evaluated following incubation under different conditions: NaCl concentrations (0–4 M), temperatures (30–80 °C), and divalent metal ions. AhCA and RsCA retained high activity under elevated salinity, with RsCA exhibiting pronounced salt activation after incubation at 4 M NaCl, whereas HbCA displayed comparatively lower salt tolerance but greater thermostability, maintaining activity after incubation at 80 °C for 1 h. Co2+ and Mg2+ produced the strongest activation for AhCA and RsCA, respectively, with metal-dependent effects varying considerably among the three enzymes. Molecular dynamics simulations performed at different NaCl concentrations revealed enhanced structural stability of RsCA under saline conditions, consistent with its superior catalytic performance. A surface physicochemical analysis identified an extensive negatively charged surface characteristic of salt-adapted proteins. Together, these findings identify RsCA as a candidate for further evaluation and provide structural insight into the molecular basis of halotolerance in α-CAs.
items.authors: Isabella del Furia, Nina Gehres Dietz, Carsten Jers, Ivan Mijakovic, Colleen Varaidzo Manyumwa

items.title: The Wrapped Q-Lindley Distribution: A New Circular Model with Statistical Properties, Classical and Bayesian Inference, and Applications to Directional Data
items.abstract: Circular data arise naturally in a wide range of scientific fields, including biology, geology, meteorology, and environmental sciences, where conventional linear statistical methods are inappropriate unless the circular structure of the observations is taken into account. Motivated by the need for parsimonious, analytically tractable models for unimodal directional data, we introduce a new one-parameter circular model, the Wrapped Q-Lindley (WQL) distribution. The proposed model is obtained by wrapping the Q-Lindley distribution and has a specific unimodal asymmetric shape. Closed-form or analytically tractable expressions are derived for several important distributional properties, including the characteristic function, trigonometric moments, circular descriptive measures, and Rényi entropy. We investigate parameter estimation using ten classical estimation methods, along with Bayesian inference, under four symmetric and asymmetric loss functions. A Monte Carlo simulation study evaluates and compares the finite-sample performance of the competing estimators. The practical usefulness of the proposed model is illustrated through two real directional datasets involving sun compass orientation measurements of starhead topminnows and wind direction observations. Comparisons with several established circular models indicate that the WQL distribution provides competitive fitting performance for the considered datasets. We discuss its parsimonious structure and analytical tractability, along with the implications of its structural discontinuity at the wrap point, in the context of directional data analysis.
items.authors: Swapnil Swagat Phookan, Sajadul Hussain, Partha Jyoti Hazarika, Diego I. Gallardo, Osvaldo Venegas

items.title: Emergency Vehicle Car-Following Across Driving Regimes with Retrospective and Past-Only Regime Assignment
items.abstract: This study examines whether regime-specific calibration improves the local acceleration representation of emergency-vehicle following episodes. Field trajectories of ambulances performing emergency-response tasks were obtained from two monitoring sites on Shaoshan East Road in Xiangtan, China, during February–December 2025 and screened into 499 valid following pairs. Standardised window features were reduced by principal component analysis and clustered using training pairs only. Three assignment protocols were compared: retrospective windows with acceleration, retrospective windows without acceleration, and acceleration-free windows completed strictly before the response time. Five car-following models were calibrated with fixed or regime-specific parameters and evaluated on identical observations. In the primary past-only analysis, the common test support comprised 1678 observations from 69 pairs. The Longitudinal Control Model (LCM) had the lowest test RMSE, 1.0478 m/s2, and reduced RMSE by 13.43% relative to its fixed-parameter counterpart; the paired pair-level bootstrap interval for the RMSE difference was [−0.2225, −0.0973] m/s2. Improvements for the other four models were smaller and their intervals included zero. LCM retained the lowest error with two and four clusters and under expanded parameter bounds, although its fitted parameters remained sensitive to constraints. These results support a dataset-specific benefit for LCM local acceleration representation.
items.authors: Linlong Lei, Zhizhen Liu

items.title: From Rules to Reality: Cultural Property Protection in the Western Balkans
items.abstract: This paper examines how the effectiveness of cultural property protection frameworks in five Western Balkan countries is assessed in the existing literature, with particular attention to cross-border challenges related to illicit trafficking, provenance verification, and enforcement practices. It contributes to the comparative literature by providing a structured synthesis of how the practical operation of legal provisions for cultural property protection is described across the region. The study employs a systematic literature review following PRISMA guidelines, ensuring a transparent and replicable process for identifying, screening, and evaluating relevant academic and policy sources published between 2000 and 2025. The review covers Albania, Serbia, North Macedonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Montenegro, integrating legal and institutional perspectives. The findings indicate that, although the countries examined have made significant progress in aligning their legal frameworks with EU and international standards, substantial implementation challenges persist. These include limited institutional coordination, insufficient traceability mechanisms, and uneven enforcement capacity across jurisdictions. The role of intermediaries and the complexity of cross-border movements further complicate effective regulation. Overall, the study demonstrates that the effectiveness of cultural property protection depends not only on formal legal alignment but also on the institutional capacity to implement and enforce existing rules. By identifying shared challenges and differences across national contexts, the paper contributes to ongoing efforts to strengthen cultural heritage protection and regional cooperation in the Western Balkans.
items.authors: Klodiana Gorica, Ermira H. Kalaj, Sanja Kovačić, Valentina Todoroska, Kosjenka Dumančić

items.title: Personalized Management of Hydrosalpinx Before IVF: A Narrative Review of Reproductive Outcomes and Treatment Timing
items.abstract: Background and Objectives: Hydrosalpinx is an important and treatable cause of impaired in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes, but the optimal intervention and its timing remain uncertain. This narrative review evaluates contemporary evidence to support individualized management before IVF. Materials and Methods: Targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE records and publisher websites prioritized systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomized trials, cohort studies, and international guidelines published from January 2015 to September 2026, while retaining earlier landmark studies. Evidence concerning salpingectomy, laparoscopic proximal tubal occlusion (PTO), aspiration, sclerotherapy, ovarian reserve, and treatment timing was synthesized narratively. Results: Clinically significant communicating hydrosalpinx should generally be treated before embryo transfer. Salpingectomy remains the most established definitive intervention, whereas laparoscopic PTO appears to provide comparable clinical pregnancy outcomes and may reduce tubo-ovarian vascular disruption in selected patients. Evidence regarding ovarian reserve after salpingectomy is conflicting: total oocyte yield is often preserved, although some studies report lower anti-Müllerian hormone, antral follicle count, or ipsilateral follicular recruitment. Aspiration and sclerotherapy may be considered when standard surgery is not feasible, but recurrence and limited randomized evidence restrict routine use. Observational studies do not establish a universally superior sequence of surgery and oocyte retrieval. Conclusions: Management should move from a uniform procedure-centered approach toward patient-centered selection. Reproductive age, ovarian reserve, laterality, pelvic adhesions, surgical complexity, and treatment urgency should guide both the intervention and its timing, while effective hydrosalpinx treatment should precede embryo transfer.
items.authors: Eduard Cristian Mihoci, Demetra Socolov, Răzvan Vladimir Socolov, Ana Maria Mihoci, Dragos Nemescu

items.title: Genetic Determinants of Circulating Adiponectin Levels, a Complex Multifactorial Intermediate Phenotype
items.abstract: Circulating adiponectin represents a complex trait with a multifactorial background influenced by internal and external genetic and non-genetic factors, as well as physiological and pathological conditions. It is an important intermediate phenotype characterized by unusually high levels, paradoxical associations with obesity or mortality, and analytical difficulties. Family studies, genome-wide linkage and association analyses demonstrate genetics as a major determinant, though possibly of lesser importance than in similar traits. Heritability values estimated by classical family studies vary significantly (30–93%), depending on study design, age, sex and ancestry. The strongest signals characterized by population differences are on chromosome 3 and 16, where ADIPOQ and CDH13 encoding adiponectin and T-cadherin reside, but tens of other loci situated on almost all chromosomes and genetic variants related to over 150 genes are suspected to modulate plasma levels, frequently by unexplained mechanisms. Population-specific high-impact rare missense mutations (e.g., G45R, R55C, G84R, G90S, R112C, I164T) and common synonymous exon (rs2241766), intron (e.g., rs1501299, rs17366568) or regulatory sequence (e.g., rs17300539, rs266729, rs6773957) variants of ADIPOQ, often in linkage disequilibrium, affect circulating adiponectin levels, usually by altering multimer assembly or gene expression regulation. Three decades of adiponectin genetics research contributed significantly to deciphering adiponectin biology, and emerging genomic technologies may clarify current knowledge gaps.
items.authors: Katalin Csép

items.title: An IoT Malware Detection Framework Based on Large Language Models and Deep Learning Techniques
items.abstract: Rapid growth in IoT devices has led to the creation of crucial cybersecurity threats since existing methods of malware detection which use signature matching and numerical feature analysis are incapable of capturing the contextual behavioral semantics of IoT attacks. The presented work proposes an innovative malware detection framework incorporating a pipeline of behavior-to-text transformation together with transformer-based Large Language Models (LLMs) to perform binary classification of IoT network traffic. Selected through the process of SHAP-based feature importance analysis, the numerical features of network flows from the initial set of 41 features are transformed into natural language descriptions, allowing encoder-based LLMs to capture the context of IoT traffic behavior. Four LLMs, including DistilBERT, BERT-base, RoBERTa, and DeBERTa, were fine-tuned and rigorously tested against four Deep Learning baselines, Neural Network, LSTM, BiLSTM, and CNN, and four Machine Learning baselines, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost, using the CIC-IoT-2023 dataset under three experimental setups: balanced classification, realistic imbalanced distribution, and unseen variant detection. Additionally, a four-class multi-class classification experiment and an ablation study were conducted to further validate the framework. On a balanced dataset consisting of 400,000 samples, BERT-base and RoBERTa achieved the highest F1-scores of 98.94% with precision above 99.96%. In the imbalanced case of 90% attack and 10% benign traffic, the precision of all models was equal to 99.99%. The framework attained an F1-score of 99.99% for unseen variant detection on a completely unseen Mirai botnet variant with zero false negatives. The four-class multi-class experiment achieved a Macro F1-score of 88.80%. Statistical analysis across three independent runs confirmed high result stability with standard deviations below 0.03%. SHAP analysis revealed that packet count, ACK flag number, and HTTPS indicator were the most discriminative features, while attention visualization confirmed token-level interpretability. All LLMs consistently outperformed all Deep Learning baselines, providing evidence for the effectiveness of the behavior-to-text transformation paradigm for IoT malware detection, while classical ML models achieved marginally higher F1-scores due to their efficiency with numerical features, providing evidence for the effectiveness of the behavior-to-text transformation paradigm for IoT malware detection.
items.authors: Hamza K. Al-Daoud, Adnan H. Al-Helali

items.title: Fatty Waste from Industrial Vegetable Oil Esterification as an Alternative Substrate for Rhamnolipid Production
items.abstract: Biosurfactants are amphiphilic molecules produced by microorganisms that have attracted increasing interest as alternatives to conventional surfactants. However, the use of low-cost substrates is essential for improving the economic and environmental feasibility of their production. This study evaluated fatty waste from industrial vegetable oil esterification reactions as an alternative substrate for rhamnolipid (RL) production by Pseudomonas aeruginosa LBI. The residue, consisting of a mixture of carboxylic acids and esters, was used as a carbon source in the culture medium. After 144 h of cultivation, 97% of the residue was consumed, resulting in 9.32 g/L of RL. Analysis of the residual substrate indicated preferential utilization of free fatty acids followed by ester compounds. The RL product exhibited a critical micelle concentration (CMC) of 44.3 mg/L, while chemical characterization confirmed the presence of RhaC10C10 and Rha2C10C10 congeners. In detergency assays, the RL preparation promoted the removal of grease and tomato sauce soils from stainless steel and glass surfaces, providing preliminary evidence of the detergency potential of RL produced from the fatty residue. These findings demonstrate the potential of using the fatty residue from the chemical esterification process as a feedstock for RL production and highlight its value for waste valorization and the development of sustainable cleaning formulations.
items.authors: João Paulo Chiconelo Sutilo de Arruda, Marcia Nitschke

items.title: Effect of Gallium Doping on the Oxygen Exchange Kinetics in La2SrFe2O7−δ Ruddlesden–Popper Phases
items.abstract: This study investigates the oxygen exchange kinetics between O2 and Ga-doped La2SrFe2O7−δ, focusing on the role of gallium substitution in modifying the surface exchange properties of materials. Two compositions, undoped La2SrFe2O7−δ and Ga-doped La2SrFe1.8Ga0.2O7−δ, were synthesised via conventional solid-state reaction. The phase composition and microstructure of the resulting powders were analysed using X-ray powder diffraction (XRPD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area analysis, and laser scattering techniques. Oxygen surface exchange kinetics between the oxides and O2 was studied using the 18O/16O isotope exchange pulsed method across a temperature range of 400–900 °C under a He/16O2 gas carrier mixture (19 vol. % O2). The results reveal that both Ga doping and temperature significantly influence the exchange mechanism and rate-determining step, demonstrating tunable catalytic activity in oxygen reduction reactions relevant to solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) cathodes.
items.authors: Egor V. Gordeev, Anna V. Khodimchuk, Dmitriy M. Zakharov, Natalia M. Porotnikova, Denis A. Osinkin

items.title: Botulinum Toxin A for the Management of Post-Laryngectomy Salivary Leak and Pharyngocutaneous Fistula: A Case Series and Narrative Review
items.abstract: Post-laryngectomy salivary leak and pharyngocutaneous fistula (PCF) are recognised complications that prolong hospitalisation, delay adjuvant treatment and, in severe cases, risk major vessel exposure; current management relies on conservative measures or systemic anticholinergic agents, which carry a substantial burden of unwanted effects. We present four consecutive patients treated with a standardised regimen of botulinum toxin A (BoNT) injected into the parotid tail, parotid body and submandibular gland after failure of conservative management for post-laryngectomy salivary leak/PCF; all four achieved clinical and radiological resolution without significant local or systemic complications. We conducted a narrative review of the literature (PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane, Google Scholar) using a structured search and screening process, screening 1198 records (701 after deduplication) and identifying 13 eligible studies (231 patients who received BoNT across 12 primary studies) evaluating BoNT for salivary leak/fistula across post-laryngectomy PCF and post-parotidectomy sialocele/fistula populations. A previous systematic review is discussed as supporting context; its patient cohort is not included in the total above, as its 27 source articles may overlap with the primary studies included in this review. Across the case series and a limited, predominantly observational literature base, BoNT was associated with rapid salivary suppression (up to ~95% reduction in one study), high fistula closure rates (54–100%), and accelerated healing, including a statistically significant reduction in healing time in one comparative study (18.5 vs. 26 days, p = 0.008); adverse events were reported as rare and minor, though these findings warrant cautious interpretation given the evidence base. BoNT injection is a low-risk, potentially high-yield adjunct for post-laryngectomy salivary leak and PCF, avoiding the systemic anticholinergic burden of alternative pharmacological treatments; multicentre studies with standardised dosing protocols are needed to establish its role in standard practice.
items.authors: Ishtiak Mahamud, Jake Ahmed, Daniel Leopard
items.category_raw: Journal of Otorhinolaryngology, Hearing and Balance Medicine

items.title: Transfer of Undertakings and the Limits of Employee Protection: Turkey and the United Kingdom Beyond the EU Directive 2001/23/EC
items.abstract: The transfer of undertakings (TUs), whether by sale, merger, outsourcing, or comparable restructuring, poses a persistent challenge to employment law in terms of how to reconcile an employer’s freedom to reorganise its business with the protection of employees. This article compares the United Kingdom’s (UK’s) and the Turkish responses to that tension, asking how far Turkish law has converged with a regime derived from Council Directive 2001/23/EC despite Turkey’s non-membership in the European Union, and how far it still diverges in practice. The article examines TU-related provisions in both countries: Article 6 of Turkish Labour Act No. 4857 and the Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006 in the UK. It considers the constituent elements of an undertaking, the circumstances in which an economic entity retains its identity, and the consequences for employees and employers in each jurisdiction. Substantial structural convergence emerges. Both treat the transfer as substituting the identity of the employer rather than terminating the employment relationship; both exclude the protective regime where the transfer occurs in insolvency-driven liquidation; both construe the underlying legal transaction broadly; and both resist reducing the identity of the economic entity to any single criterion, relying instead on a multifactorial and casuistic assessment. Beneath this shared architecture, however, material differences leave Turkish employees comparatively less protected. Turkish law remains fragmented across several statutory instruments rather than consolidated; its case law approaches identity through the undertaking’s essential, property-linked elements rather than through the more developed UK inquiry into the qualification, skill, and intensity of the workforce; it affords no general right to object to a transfer, the sole exception being confined to mergers, divisions, and conversions of commercial companies; and it imposes no duty to inform or consult employees or trade unions in advance. Turkish law is stronger in one respect only: its broad, automatic joint and several liability for pre-transfer claims, as against the narrowly circumscribed UK position. The article concludes that targeted reform is warranted: consolidation of the provisions, extension of the right to object, and the introduction of a genuine information and consultation duty. Such reform would bring Turkish practice closer to the UK protective standard without departing from the conceptual framework the two systems already share.
items.authors: Mustafa Nalbant, Deniz Otay Korkmaz

items.title: Counterfactual Routine Deviation: Personalised Behavioural Modelling for Insider Threat Detection
items.abstract: Insider threats remain particularly challenging to detect because malicious activity can be carried out by authorised users with legitimate credentials and established access to organisational systems. Conventional population- and peer-based anomaly detection approaches may compound this challenge by treating legitimate differences in occupational behaviour as suspicious. This paper formalises and evaluates Counterfactual Routine Deviation (CRD), a personalised behavioural analytics framework that assesses observed user activity against expectations derived from the individual’s own historical behaviour. By modelling deviations from established personal routines, while retaining peer-relative deviation for comparative evaluation, CRD examines whether personalised behavioural reference points provide more informative signals than population-relative comparisons. CRD was evaluated on the CMU SEI CERT Insider Threat Dataset Release 6.2 using 559,516 user-day observations from 4000 users. Only 140 user-days were labelled within insider-risk windows (0.025% prevalence), creating a stringent base-rate setting. Behavioural features captured routine, content, destination and organisational-change signals, including authentication and device activity, file and web behaviour, removable-media use and short behavioural sequences. Performance was assessed using AUROC with bootstrap confidence intervals, average precision, precision at fixed alert budgets, scenario-stratified analysis, complete-user grouped validation, and a forward temporal holdout. Under the primary evaluation framework, the strongest discriminator was a logistic combination of CRD components, which achieved an AUROC of 0.755 (95% bootstrap CI 0.725–0.788). The best direct within-user score, all_features_within_user_crd, achieved an AUROC of 0.571, compared with 0.370 for its peer-relative counterpart. Routine within-user CRD similarly exceeded routine peer CRD (0.538 versus 0.312), while the content-based difference was smaller (0.543 versus 0.511). The unweighted combined CRD score was non-discriminative (AUROC 0.479), demonstrating that deviation magnitude alone was insufficient and that the weighting of behavioural signals materially affected performance. Operational performance remained constrained by extreme class imbalance. The logistic score achieved an average precision of 0.000801 and Precision@100 of 0.01 despite its moderate ROC discrimination. Under complete-user grouped evaluation, the logistic combination achieved an AUROC of 0.434, indicating poor and unstable discrimination for previously unseen users, while the forward temporal holdout achieved an AUROC of 0.678, indicating that some discriminatory ability was retained on chronologically later observations. Scenario-level performance was also heterogeneous: Scenario 4 accounted for 135 of 140 positive user-days (96.4%) and therefore dominated the aggregate results. These findings provide qualified support for the construction of personalised behavioural references. Within-user deviation generally contained more discriminatory information than corresponding peer-relative measures, but this advantage did not translate into high operational precision or reliable unseen-user generalisation. CRD should therefore be interpreted as a personalised behavioural ranking and research framework rather than a deployment-ready detector. Its principal contribution is the formalisation and empirical comparison of within-user and peer-relative counterfactual behavioural deviation, while further validation on independent datasets and real enterprise telemetry remains necessary.
items.authors: Christian Bowie, Hadi Larijani, Ayyaz Qureshi

items.title: Effect of Pre-Corrosion on the Fatigue Behavior of 347H Austenitic Stainless Steel at Elevated Temperature
items.abstract: The combined damage induced by the nitrate molten salt corrosion and cyclic loading at elevated temperatures is an important damage issue for the reliable operation of concentrated solar power (CSP) plants. In previous works, the effect of the molten salt pre-corrosion on the fatigue behavior of 347H stainless steel remains insufficiently understood. Based on this, the present work investigated the corrosion behavior of 347H stainless steel in nitrate molten salts at 565 °C, with particular attention to chloride impurities. The effects of pre-corrosion on cyclic deformation characteristics, fatigue life, and failure mechanisms were discussed. The results indicated that the oxide-scale growth follows approximately parabolic kinetics in chloride-free salt, whereas chloride-containing salt exhibits sub-parabolic growth with a lower kinetic exponent. Chloride addition produces a thicker and less stable oxide scale characterized by cracking, spallation, and chromium depletion. The pre-corrosion does not alter the cyclic hardening characteristic of 347H stainless steel but significantly reduces its fatigue life. The corrosion-induced damage morphology also changes the subsequent fatigue crack initiation behavior. The relatively uniform oxidation promotes crack initiation at the oxide layer-substrate interface, whereas chloride-induced scale degradation introduces more severe local damage and accelerates crack initiation and propagation.
items.authors: Hao Chen, Hai-Ying Lei, Xue-Jing Sun, Jian-Guo Gong, Yu-Hui Huang, Fu-Zhen Xuan

items.title: A Self-Sensing Control Method for Active Magnetic Bearings Based on the Star-Point Voltage
items.abstract: Methods for self-sensing position determination in active magnetic bearings enable a reduction in system costs and complexity. Many well-known methods rely on current measurements or their derivatives to estimate the rotor’s displacement relative to the centre. However, measuring voltage often yields a better signal-to-noise ratio compared to current measurements, especially considering smaller machines where the current is often sensed using a shunt. Nevertheless, star-connected active magnetic bearings and the associated star-point voltage are rarely addressed in research. The star-point voltage provides valuable information for self-sensing position determination in other types of electric machines, such as permanent magnet synchronous motors. The goal of this research is to exploit the star-point voltage of an active magnetic bearing to estimate the rotor position. This study presents an analytical derivation of the star-point voltage for a four-phase active magnetic bearing, followed by a description of a differential measurement method for the star-point voltage. It is shown that, under the selected operating conditions, the resulting measured values depend exclusively on the coil inductance and the known DC supply voltage. To extract the position information from the obtained signal, the system was characterized at a standstill. The resulting measured values were used for polynomial fits, which were implemented on the microcontroller. Finally, the proposed method was experimentally validated inside the control loop under quasi static conditions. Experiments conducted on a laboratory prototype with a large air gap of 2 mm showed an RMS value of the estimation error ranging from 9.2 μm to 36.9 μm and a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 70 dB.
items.authors: Jonah Vennemann, Niklas König, Rudolf Gerlich, Matthias Nienhaus

items.title: Characterization of CTC-HER2 Status in Patients with HER2-Low Invasive Breast Cancer
items.abstract: Background: HER2 status is a dynamic process where one in ten patients with invasive breast cancer may undergo receptor conversion. We characterized HER2 status on circulating tumor cells (CTCs) in patients with HER2-low breast cancer. Methods: Patients with HER2-low expression, defined as immunohistochemistry (IHC) score of 1+ or 2+ with negative HER2 fluorescent in situ hybridization, were enrolled from 2019 to 2023. All patients were treatment-naïve to HER2-targeted therapies. Blood draws were collected serially q3–6 months. CTCs were enumerated using CellSearch™ and HER2 expression on CTCs were detected using an anti-HER2 fluorescent antibody. Presence of ≥1 CTCs was considered positive. Wilcoxon rank-sum, Fisher’s exact test, and Kaplan–Meier method were used for statistical analysis. Results: Among 39 HER2-low patients, median age was 49.0 years (IQR 40.5–58.5). Patients were predominantly Non-Hispanic White (26, 66.7%), with node-positive (29/38, 76.3%), ductal (27, 69.2%), stage II-III (24, 61.5%) disease. Over half (23, 59.0%) had inflammatory breast cancer (IBC). Rates of ER and PR positivity were 56.4% (22) and 51.3% (20), respectively. Majority of patients underwent surgery (23 mastectomy, seven segmental mastectomy) with a pCR rate of 17.2%. Up to 53.8% (21) of patients had HER2-positive CTCs during treatment course. Of these, 13 (61.9%) and eight (38.1%) were present before and after surgery, respectively. There were no differences in age, BMI, grade, histology, lymphovascular invasion, IBC status, and pCR rate by CTC-HER2 status. At a median follow up of 3.8 years (95% CI: 2.6–4.9), patients with HER2-positive CTCs demonstrated a trend of worse prognosis compared to those with HER2-negative CTCs (5-year overall survival 59.8% vs. 88.9%, p = 0.11). Conclusions: In this study cohort, a high proportion of HER2-low expressors demonstrated HER2-CTC positivity. These findings support the potential use of HER2 expression on CTCs as a biomarker to personalize therapies among patients with HER2-low breast cancer.
items.authors: Jennifer H. Chen, Salyna Meas, Roland L. Bassett, Vanessa N. Sarli, Joshua Upshaw, Anthony Lucci

items.title: Exposure-Time-And Orientation-Dependent Germination and Early Seedling Responses of Maize (Zea mays L.) Caryopses Treated with Atmospheric DDBD Non-Thermal Plasma
items.abstract: Non-thermal plasma (NTP) is an emerging technology in different areas, including agriculture, and scaling it requires understanding its physical and chemical interactions with tissue. This study evaluated the physiomorphic, thermodynamic, and electrodynamic interplays between an air-based double dielectric barrier discharge (DDBD) plasma and the structure of two maize (Zea mays L.) genotypes: white (PBB-DH-183) and yellow (H-394 A). Electrodynamic characterisation confirmed a filament discharge with a power of 22.5 W. Long-wave infrared (LWIR) thermographic profiling demonstrated that the surface temperature of the caryopses stabilised at 25.0 °C (ΔTemp = 4.7 °C), assuring a non-thermal regime and indicating that non-thermal electric and electrochemical interactions drive cellular responses. Tests revealed an exposure-time-dependent, non-linear hormetic response. A 60 s window optimised germination efficiency (GE) in the white genotype, achieving a net increase of +7.02% at the M position (embryo-up orientation), an effect attributed to physical surface etching that accelerates water imbibition. Conversely, yellow maize reached its maximum GE (+3.22%) at 60 s under the N position (endosperm-up orientation), where the starch matrix acts as a shield. Overexposure (≥120 s) induced significant distress and phytotoxicity, collapsing the primary seminal root by −16.9% (white) and −36.0% (yellow). Optimising NTP relies on adjusting the kinetic windows to account for tissue anisotropy, dielectric properties, and genotypic sensitivity.
items.authors: Jorge Jurado-Páramo, Rafael Alejandro Rodríguez-Moreno, Diana Guadalupe Gutiérrez-León, Régulo López-Callejas, Benjamín Gonzalo Rodríguez-Méndez, Diego Medina-Castro

items.title: Lending Through the Fire: Credit Expansion and Rising Bank Risk After the 2025 California Wildfires
items.abstract: The 2025 Los Angeles (LA) County wildfires destroyed more than 16,000 structures and were followed by more than $20 billion of insurance payments within seven months. We use a difference-in-differences (DiD) design to examine how this acute physical climate shock transmitted through banks’ capital, credit risk, profitability, management efficiency, liquidity, funding, and credit supply. Treated banks are commercial banks headquartered in LA County; control banks are headquartered in counties with no FEMA major disaster declaration over 2022Q1–2025Q4 and have no LA County branch. We estimate entropy-balanced DiD and event-study models with bank and quarter fixed effects on a seven-quarter window (2024Q1–2025Q3) with onset in 2025Q1. To separate the effects of the wildfires from pre-existing trends and from differences between LA County banks and other banks that appear even in a year without a fire, we examine each effect with parallel-trends and placebo-timing diagnostics. The cleanest evidence comes from the single-county sample. Relative to the control banks, single-county treated banks’ non-performing loan ratio rose, and their management efficiency and return on assets deteriorated, while their total and real estate lending grew and the yields on these loans and their cost of deposits fell. We term this coexistence of rising credit risk and expanding intermediation the disaster liquidity paradox. For the full sample, only the increase in non-performing loans and the decline in the cost of deposits pass all diagnostics. The full-sample deposit and lending expansion, however, is of a size that LA County banks also display in a year without a fire, so we present it as a description of the post-wildfire period rather than as a causal effect of the wildfires. Insurance and relief payments sustaining bank funding are a possible explanation for this pattern; because Call Report data cannot trace these flows, the analysis does not directly demonstrate this mechanism. As all treated banks are headquartered in a single county and experienced a single event, the estimates describe this episode and may not generalize to other disasters or banking markets.
items.authors: Daniel Crowley, Lin Guo, Ki Han

items.title: Effects of a Benzimidazolium Salt on Colorectal Cancer Cells: Involvement of Apoptosis and Autophagy
items.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, necessitating the identification of novel small molecules capable of targeting multiple survival pathways. In this study, the antiproliferative potential of dds benzimidazole-palladium (Pd) complexes was evaluated across breast cancer (4T1, MDA-MB-231) and CRC (DLD-1, HT-29) cell lines using MTT assays. Following initial screening, CRC models were prioritized for mechanistic investigation due to the complexes’ superior cytotoxic profile, particularly that of the lead candidate 3a, which exhibited significant dose-dependent efficacy. Mechanistic analyses, employing immunofluorescence staining for LC3 and mTOR alongside Annexin V/PI flow cytometry, revealed that compound 3a triggers a potent dual response characterized by concomitant autophagy and apoptosis. Furthermore, functional assays indicated that 3a significantly impairs the metastatic hallmarks of CRC cells by inhibiting migration, cell adhesion, and colony formation. Gene expression profiling further elucidated that the anticancer efficacy of 3a is mediated by suppression of the AKT/mTOR/STAT3 signaling axis, thereby triggering an autophagic response that destabilizes cell adhesion and accelerates apoptosis. These molecular findings were corroborated by in silico molecular docking analyses, which demonstrated favorable binding affinities between compound 3a and key regulatory proteins, specifically BCL-2 and Caspase-3. Collectively, these results identify compound 3a as a promising multi-targeted anticancer agent that disrupts critical survival and metastatic pathways in CRC, warranting further preclinical and mechanistic exploration for therapeutic development.
items.authors: Mustafa Cakir, Eda Acikgoz, Burak Kuzu, Sakine Akar, Halil Ozkol, Hamiyet Donmez-Altuntas

items.title: Prediction of Tumor Complete Response Using Genomic and Clinical Data in Solid Cancer Undergoing Definitive Radiation Therapy
items.abstract: In this retrospective, single-center observational study, targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) was performed on pre-radiation therapy (RT) tumor specimens to identify genomic features associated with RT response and clinical outcomes. This study included 77 eligible patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC, n = 23), non-human papilloma virus-related head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC, n = 24), and rectal adenocarcinoma (RAC, n = 30) treated between 2014 and 2020. Treatment was employed for definitive aim (chemoradiotherapy or pre-operative chemoradiotherapy followed by radical surgery). Treatment response was assessed using clinical and pathological criteria and was dichotomized as complete response (CR) versus non-CR. Targeted NGS was performed using a customized panel composing 161 genes. A total of 1263 nonsynonymous somatic variants were identified across 153 genes. The most commonly altered genes were TP53 (70.1%), APC (41.6%), NOTCH1 (41.6%), KMT2C (39.0%), NOTCH3 (36.4%), and NOTCH2 (35.1%). Overall, 25 (32.5%) and 52 patients (67.5%) were classified as CR and non-CR, respectively. APC (P = 0.008), KMT2C (P = 0.018), and KRAS (P = 0.012) alterations were associated with non-CR, whereas CD274 (P = 0.003), MSH3 (P = 0.011), and NOTCH3 (P = 0.048) alterations were associated with CR. KRAS alterations occurred exclusively in RAC, and most concurrent APC–KMT2C alterations in non-CR tumors were also observed in RAC, suggesting that these associations may partly reflect tumor type-specific genomic backgrounds. An exploratory pooled model incorporating age and six candidate genomic variables achieved a cross-validated area under the curve of 0.867 for CR prediction. In survival analysis, alterations in CCND1, CXCL9, ERCC6, LIF, and RAD51B were independently associated with poor recurrence-free survival. Pre-RT tumor genomic profiling identified candidate features associated with RT response and recurrence-free survival in this heterogeneous cohort. The pooled genomic associations and prediction model should not be interpreted as pan-cancer biomarkers or predictors and require validation in larger, independent, cancer-specific cohort.
items.authors: Jun Young Chang, Seung-Hyun Jung, Dong Soo Lee

items.title: REW-DETR: A Lightweight Real-Time Detection Transformer for Bridge Surface Defect Detection
items.abstract: Timely detection of bridge surface defects is important for structural safety assessment and inspection efficiency. To address defect scale variation, complex background interference, and the high computational cost of RT-DETR-R50, this study proposes REW-DETR, a lightweight bridge surface defect detector. REW-DETR adopts a coordinated lightweight design integrating efficient feature extraction, multi-level channel recalibration, and localization optimization. RepNCSPELAN4–ADown is employed to reconstruct the backbone and fusion stages, ECA is embedded at the P3–P5 feature levels to enhance channel-wise feature discrimination, and Wise-IoU v3 optimizes bounding-box regression without inference-time overhead. On the test set of the bridge surface defect dataset, REW-DETR achieved Precision, Recall, mAP50, and mAP50:95 values of 87.0%, 70.4%, 73.7%, and 42.4%, respectively. These values exceeded those of RT-DETR-R50 by 3.8, 5.5, 4.0, and 4.5 percentage points, respectively. Meanwhile, the parameters and FLOPs were reduced by approximately 53.3% and 60.6%, respectively, while FPS increased from 51.2 to 70.8. After dataset-specific retraining on the bridge-defects-detection dataset from Roboflow Universe, REW-DETR achieved a Recall of 58.0% and an mAP50 of 55.4% while retaining a lightweight configuration. These results demonstrate an improved accuracy–efficiency trade-off and motivate further evaluation of REW-DETR for UAV-assisted bridge inspection, while onboard inference performance remains to be validated.
items.authors: Xiaohui Cheng, Yonghong Pang, Yanjun Wang, Yun Deng, Qiu Lu

items.title: 3DMAUNet: A 3D Memory-Augmented Deep Unfolding Network with Dynamic Momentum Updating for Snapshot Compressive Spectral Imaging
items.abstract: Coded aperture snapshot spectral compressive imaging (CASSI) enables the recovery of hyperspectral images (HSIs) from a single two-dimensional compressive measurement, serving as a core paradigm in modern computational imaging. However, HSI reconstruction from under-sampled measurements is a severely ill-posed inverse problem. Existing deep unfolding methods typically treat each iterative stage independently and model spatial–spectral features in a decoupled manner, which neglects intrinsic spatial–spectral coupling and lacks persistent cross-stage information propagation. To tackle these issues, we propose a deep dynamic 3D memory-augmented unfolding network (3DMAUNet) for HSI reconstruction. Based on the momentum-accelerated generalized alternating projection framework, 3DMAUNet retains the strict mathematical interpretability of iterative optimization while integrating data-driven learnable components. Specifically, we design two key modules: (1) a 3D memory-augmented learning module equipped with a persistent memory bank, which explicitly encodes cross-layer spatial–spectral correlations to enable efficient inter-stage information transfer and long-range dependency modeling; and (2) a learnable dynamic fast momentum updating module, which fuses cross-stage spatial–spectral attention features to estimate task-adaptive momentum coefficients, accelerating convergence and enhancing the robustness of feature updating. Comprehensive experiments on synthetic and real-world HSI datasets demonstrate that 3DMAUNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative and qualitative reconstruction performance.
items.authors: Zheng Zhou, Jintao Lai, Xiaofei Yang, Zhong Cao, Wenbiao Yang, Wenli Shang

items.title: Regime-Dependent Effectiveness of Spectral Nudging in WRF–Chem: Meteorological and Saharan Dust Skill over the Central Mediterranean
items.abstract: Regional WRF–Chem dust simulations may require continuous integrations when state continuity is scientifically important, yet extended limited-area runs can depart dynamically from the driving analysis. We use a two-tier controlled design that separates dynamical attribution from aerosol transport response: a continuous chemistry-free FREE-FDDA pair spanning 104 days (15 March–27 June 2024) isolates the meteorological response to spectral nudging of the horizontal wind, and paired event-scale WRF–Chem simulations of two Saharan outbreaks test whether that response is reflected in dust prediction skill. The meteorological response is variable-selective and strongly non-monotonic. Sea-level pressure improves most (mean daily RMSE 2.08 to 1.53 hPa) as an indirect response of the mass field, 10 m wind speed improves coherently but less (2.50 to 2.20 m s−1), and 2 m temperature does not improve (2.05 to 2.15 °C); the benefit recurs episodically; formal age-adjusted interaction tests identify regime modulation for T2 and WSPD10, but not SLP, rather than a universal simulation-age threshold. Aerosol transport, evaluated against AERONET Version 3 Level 2.0 AOD550 with Level 1.0 as a coverage-sensitivity check, is conditional. In the weakly forced June case all seven sites improve simultaneously in RMSE, correlation and variability amplitude (station-mean RMSE 0.457 to 0.235; correlation 0.778 to 0.881). In March, RMSE decreases at all eight sites but mean correlation is unchanged, indicating amplitude correction without uniform improvement of plume timing. Spectral nudging therefore acts as a process-targeted constraint on circulation and transport consistency. Improved transport-relevant winds coincide with lower AOD error in both events, but the daily meteorology–AOD associations are not statistically resolved and do not establish that transport error dominates the total aerosol error; constraints on dust emission, optical properties and removal remain independently necessary.
items.authors: Alessandra Chiappini, Umberto Rizza, Giorgio Passerini, Antonio Ricchi

items.title: Study on the Evolution and Driving Factors of Shallow Groundwater Depth in Zhengzhou City
items.abstract: Groundwater is one of the main water supplies for Zhengzhou City. Changes in groundwater depth negatively affect the water supply and geological stability of the city. Based on groundwater monitoring data from 1999 to 2024, this paper investigates the spatiotemporal changes in shallow groundwater depth in Zhengzhou and their driving factors. Trend analysis, ordinary Kriging interpolation, and Pearson correlation analysis were first employed to characterize the spatiotemporal evolution patterns of groundwater depth. A principal component regression (PCR) framework was then applied to reduce multicollinearity among hydro-climatic and water-use variables and to quantify their integrated relationships with groundwater depth at individual monitoring wells. The main findings are as follows: (1) Over the past 25 years, groundwater depth in Zhengzhou has gradually increased, with an average decline rate of 0.68 m per year. The most rapid increase occurred from 1999 to 2012. (2) Spatially, groundwater depth is greatest in the central urban area (average 35.2 m) and decreases with distance from the city center, forming a depression cone in the downtown area. (3) Anthropogenic factors dominate groundwater depth variation. Groundwater extraction shows a strong positive correlation with groundwater depth, and standardized regression coefficients indicate that domestic water consumption and groundwater supply are the key drivers of groundwater deepening and recovery, respectively. Rapid urbanization has led to water table decline, while changes in precipitation have had relatively minor effects. (4) Socioeconomic factors, such as expansion of construction land, population growth, and industrialization, have also contributed to the increase in groundwater depth by raising water demand and reducing infiltration recharge. The PCR-based analysis provides a parsimonious and spatially explicit basis for understanding groundwater-depth dynamics in a rapidly urbanizing plain city and offers practical guidance for targeted groundwater management, extraction control, and ecological water replenishment in Zhengzhou and similar regions.
items.authors: Wenhui Liu, Lantian Guo, Guizhang Zhao, Chunyan Zhang, Kui Suo, Zhenzhen Qi

items.title: Risk Assessment of Simultaneous Dual-Well Drilling Operations on the Same Shale Gas Well Pad Based on a BT-BN Model
items.abstract: Shale gas is an important unconventional energy resource in China with considerable development potential. However, the coupling of hazards during simultaneous dual-well drilling on multi-well pads has not been adequately quantified. This study examines a scenario in which two drilling rigs operate concurrently on the same shale gas well pad and develops an integrated Bowtie–Bayesian network (BT–BN) model to compare single-well drilling with simultaneous dual-well drilling. Bowtie analysis identified 63 risk factors, preventive barriers, and events for simultaneous dual-well drilling and 35 for single-well drilling across human, equipment, environmental, and management dimensions. An improved fuzzy evaluation method was used to quantify the prior probabilities of 15 root nodes, and the conditional probability tables of the remaining non-root nodes were calculated using the extended recursive noisy-OR (ERNOR) procedure with an independent background cause. Bayesian inference was used to calculate the relative composite risk value at the target node in each scenario. The target event was loss of well control in the single-well scenario and simultaneous loss of well control in both wells in the dual-well scenario. Ratio-of-variation analysis was used to identify influential factors. For comparable basic risk factors, the single-well and dual-well models used the same seven-level expert-evaluation scale and probability-calculation procedure; the dual-well model additionally included factors arising specifically from simultaneous cross-operations. Under the same evaluation conditions, the relative composite risk value for simultaneous dual-well drilling, calculated through the Bayesian network using expert-assessed risk values, was 47.85% higher than that for single-well drilling. The results provide expert-knowledge-based quantitative support for comparative risk assessment and safety-management decision-making for simultaneous dual-well drilling on shale gas well pads.
items.authors: Xueqiang Wang, Feng Xiong, Yu Zhang, Jue Wang, Chang Shu, Jiayin Zhang

items.title: Buddhist Healing: Methods and Mechanisms—A Madhyamaka-Oriented Investigation
items.abstract: In Buddhist discourse, the path of healing often begins with awareness. Its crucial element, however, lies not in awareness alone, but in the direction toward which awareness is oriented and in the transformative process that follows from it. Ultimately, this process concerns how reality is understood. Madhyamaka thought takes cognition as its point of departure and emphasizes cognitive transformation as a means of reshaping the relationship between individuals and phenomena. Such transformation is not merely an exercise of psychological imagination; rather, it may bring about substantive changes in the structure of lived experience. Contemporary scientific research on psychological change, by contrast, largely relies on quantitative data and instrumental measurement, with its primary emphasis placed on neuroscience and psychology, whereas religious studies more commonly approaches such questions through textual interpretation and philosophical analysis. Each approach offers a distinct level of understanding. Nevertheless, the question of how religious thought may be translated into concrete and practically applicable methods remains in need of further exploration. Against this background, the present study takes healing as its central concern and examines, from within Buddhist theoretical frameworks, whether Buddhism may be understood as a mechanism of cognitive and existential transformation. Focusing on Chapter One of the Mūlamadhyamakakārikā, it argues that Nāgārjuna’s critique of arising is not merely an analysis of causality, but also a deconstruction of the linguistic and conceptual assumptions through which causality and existence are reified. By exposing both the limitations of language and the tendency to mistake conceptual constructions for reality itself, Nāgārjuna opens a therapeutic pathway through which rigid patterns of attachment, conflict, and suffering may be transformed. Furthermore, as individuals gradually loosen their reified assumptions about the self, others, and conflict through insight into emptiness, rigid boundaries between self and other, as well as between friend and enemy, may likewise be reconsidered. Such cognitive transformation may, in turn, provide a possible foundation for equanimity, compassion, and more inclusive forms of ethical engagement.
items.authors: Su-an Lin

items.title: Fatigue Crack Growth in Rubber: Comparability of Test Results, Material Effects and Transfer to Component Life—A Critical Review
items.abstract: Fatigue crack growth (FCG) relations rank rubber compounds and predict component life, yet a reported rate–tearing-energy curve depends on how it was measured as well as on the compound. This critical review treats the test variables as criteria for deciding whether two results may be compared. Specimen geometry, energy accounting, load minimum, frequency, waveform, specimen temperature, crack preparation, imaging, rate extraction and data independence shape the measured response. A two-stage, seven-item checklist and an eight-domain minimum reporting set are proposed, and the evidence on backbone, filler, cure system, temperature, ageing and chemical environment, graded by strength, is read against them. Formulation rankings hold only within matched test conditions: when compounds differ in exponent, the power-law curves cross, and rankings can reverse within or beyond the tested energy range. Where exponents were reported for both, natural rubber mostly showed a lower exponent than styrene–butadiene rubber, but the backbone was not isolated and exponent values differ between programmes. Component transfer requires geometry-specific crack-driving histories, defect criteria, thermal and load histories, and independent validation. Quantitative comparison needs a shared endpoint and energy convention, with other items matched or bounded by measurement; a single-compound inter-laboratory round-robin would test the checklist.
items.authors: Jeong-Hwan Yoon, Kyoung-Ho Shin, Ye-Won Park, Yeon-Jee Cho

items.title: A Multiscale Thermal Environment Network Framework for Urban Agglomerations: Changes from 2000 to 2020 and Planning Insights from the Hangzhou Bay Region
items.abstract: Against the backdrop of climate change and rapid urbanization, the urban thermal environment (UTE) in urban agglomerations continues to deteriorate, posing a growing challenge to regional sustainability. Network-based approaches have increasingly been applied to UTE studies, but most studies have focused on a single spatial scale, with limited attention to thermal connectivity at different scales. Therefore, this study used land surface temperature (LST) data from 2000, 2010, and 2020 together with the Patch-generating Land Use Simulation (PLUS) model and circuit theory to construct a multiscale UTE network framework for the Hangzhou Bay urban agglomeration. A cooling network was constructed at the urban-agglomeration scale and a heat network within the national-level urbanized zone, and temporal changes in each scale-specific network were examined across the three study periods. The results showed that: (1) Low-temperature areas remained concentrated in the southwestern mountains and major water bodies but continued to shrink, whereas high-temperature areas expanded and gradually coalesced across areas surrounding Hangzhou Bay, with more pronounced clustering within the national-level urbanized zone. The total area of cold sources decreased from 3249.76 to 2411.50 km2, whereas that of heat sources increased from 1061.32 to 2896.28 km2. (2) At the urban-agglomeration scale, the mean corridor length of the cooling network increased from 12.23 to 17.41 km, while the α, β, and γ indices declined continuously; within the national-level urbanized zone, the mean corridor length of the heat network decreased from 17.85 to 10.30 km, with all three indices reaching their highest values in 2020. (3) Cooling-network barriers spread from cold-source clusters into transitional areas linking cold sources with urbanized areas, whereas heat-network pinch points shifted from established heat-source clusters to emerging ones. This study provides a multiscale network perspective on thermal connectivity in urban agglomerations and offers spatial evidence for cross-regional thermal-environment management and climate-adaptation planning.
items.authors: Ziqian Nie, Shouhang Zhao, Yuexin Xu, Yuqi Li, Yunyuan Li

items.title: Thymol in Different Parts of the Rabbit Intestinal Tract: Its Effect on Intestinal Microbiota, Morphometry and Immunoglobulin A
items.abstract: The positive effect of thymol on gut health largely depends on its absorption from the intestinal tract and its biotransformation processes in the intestinal wall. A total of 32 rabbits were randomly divided at 35 days of age into a control (CG) and an experimental group (EG) that received thymol at 250 mg/kg feed. Thymol concentration was significantly higher in the caecum than in the ileum (p 0.05), which is likely associated with caecotrophy and reduced enzymatic activity in the distal segments of the small intestine. Coliform bacteria (p = 0.0095) and lactic acid bacteria (LAB; p = 0.0002), Staphylococcus spp. (p = 0.0002), and Enterococcus spp. (p = 0.0002) in the duodenum; LAB (p = 0.0003) and Enterococcus spp. (p = 0.0002) in the ileum; and other Enterobacteriaceae (p = 0.0002) and LAB (p = 0.0068) in the caecum were significantly higher in the EG. Despite the significantly lower thymol concentration in the ileum compared to the caecum, the beneficial LAB was positively affected. A decrease in immunoglobulin A in all parts of the intestinal tract except the colon was a result of the modulation of mucosal immunity. Thymol at this concentration modulated the gut ecosystem without disrupting its beneficial components, thereby helping maintain intestinal homeostasis.
items.authors: Radoslava Kristofova, Karin Zitterl-Eglseer, Markus Wildner, Andreas Zitterl, Monika Pogany Simonova, Andrea Laukova

items.title: Gamified Augmented Sensorimotor Feedback During Balance Training Improves Postural Control and Nocturnal RMSSD
items.abstract: Background and Objectives: Augmented sensorimotor feedback may enhance motor learning during balance training, but whether these adaptations extend to cardiac autonomic regulation remains unclear. This study compared wobble-board training with gamified augmented feedback versus conventional wobble-board training on dynamic balance and nocturnal heart rate variability. Methods: Thirty adults were assigned to training with gamified-augmented feedback (GBT), conventional training (CBT), or control (CON). GBT and CBT completed three ~20-min sessions weekly for six weeks. Dynamic balance, measured via the modified Star Excursion Balance Test (mSEBT), and nocturnal Root Mean Square of Successive Differences (RMSSD) were assessed. Results: Group × time interactions occurred for RMSSD and mSEBT (both p 0.001). RMSSD increased 6.93 ± 1.86 ms in GBT, versus 1.01 ± 1.38 and 0.80 ± 1.61 ms in CBT and CON, respectively. GBT exceeded CBT (mean difference, 5.92 ms; 95% CI, 4.37–7.46; Hedges’ g = 3.46) and CON (6.12 ms; 95% CI, 4.49–7.76; g = 3.38; both adjusted p 0.001); CBT did not differ from CON (p = 0.761). mSEBT increased 7.54 ± 1.62 points in GBT, 3.65 ± 1.50 in CBT, and 0.47 ± 1.46 in CON. GBT exceeded CBT (mean difference, 3.89 points; 95% CI, 2.42–5.36; g = 2.39) and CON (7.07; 95% CI, 5.63–8.52; g = 4.40), while CBT exceeded CON (3.18; 95% CI, 1.79–4.57; g = 2.06; all adjusted p 0.001). Conclusions: Gamified augmented feedback and its associated features were associated with greater improvements in dynamic balance and RMSSD than conventional training. Mechanisms underlying RMSSD response require further investigation.
items.authors: Vishruth Shatagopam, Jake Pirnazar, Phillip Goldman, Trent Yamamoto, Joshua A. Kidwell, Brett A. Dolezal
items.category_raw: Journal of Functional Morphology and Kinesiology

items.title: Hypergraph-Augmented Reconstruction and Adaptive Metric Aggregation Network for Few-Shot Fine-Grained Image Classification
items.abstract: Few-shot fine-grained image classification aims to recognize unseen fine-grained categories from very few labeled examples. The task is difficult because visually similar classes may differ only in subtle details, while images from the same class can vary considerably. Useful evidence is therefore often localized. Reconstruction-based metric methods reduce local misalignment by reconstructing query features from class-wise support features, but a small support set may still provide an incomplete reconstruction basis. In addition, spatial reconstruction errors are usually combined with fixed or nearly uniform weights, and intermediate features receive no direct reconstruction-oriented supervision. We develop HARA, a Hypergraph-Augmented Reconstruction and Adaptive Metric Aggregation Network, to address these limitations. HARA forms learnable soft hyperedges over local support features and uses the resulting aggregated features to enrich the class-wise reconstruction basis. It then combines class-conditional reconstruction with query self-reconstruction to obtain position-wise joint errors, which are aggregated using query-dependent weights. A training-only auxiliary branch applies reconstruction-based supervision to intermediate backbone features. For 5-way evaluation, HARA obtains 84.09%/93.48% on CUB-200-2011, 76.91%/88.69% on Stanford Dogs and 88.53%/95.87% on Stanford Cars under the 1-shot/5-shot settings, respectively. Ablation and diagnostic analyses further characterize the contributions and behavior of the proposed framework. Overall, HARA provides an effective extension to reconstruction-based few-shot fine-grained classification.
items.authors: Zhen Zheng, Zhen Wang, Xinzhong Wang, Yang Liu, Mingzhe Yang, Yichen Yu

items.title: Causes of Azimuthal Air Temperature Biases on a 100 m Meteorological Gradient Tower
items.abstract: Azimuthal temperature biases in multi-level tower-mounted sensors have long been reported, yet their underlying physical causes remain unclear. In particular, three candidate mechanisms—flow blockage, structural-geometry effects, and instrument-to-instrument differences in radiative sensitivity—have rarely been disentangled within a single observational experiment. Here, we address this gap by using a 100 m lattice tower at the Shouxian National Climate Observatory (32.5° N, 116.8° E), which has base and top widths of 10.0 m and 2.0 m, respectively. East–west symmetric dual temperature sensors and independent bilateral anemometers were installed at 34, 50, 65, and 80 m, with an additional reference anemometer at 95 m. On 12 May 2025, the complete probe-and-shield assembly at 50 m was reversed east–west, whereas the other three levels remained unchanged as negative controls, thereby establishing a difference-in-differences (DID) framework. Using the top-mounted reference wind direction, the bilateral wind-speed difference shows no statistically significant shadow sector at any level, allowing us to reject the flow-blockage (tower-shadow) hypothesis. The structural baseline bias S(z) of the three un-swapped decreases monotonically in magnitude with height (from −0.92 °C at 34 m to −0.28 °C at 80 m) and tracks the height-dependent tower geometry, proxied by the face width W(z), linearly, with stable day–night behavior—pointing to a geometric/orientational origin. After the swap, the 50 m bias amplifies to 3–18 times the baseline and reverses seasonally; the inter-instrument difference in daytime shortwave response is significant (Δα = +46.27 × 10−3 °C/(MJ m−2 d−1), 95% CI [+5.71, +91.30]), whereas the nighttime net-longwave difference is directionally consistent but not significant (Δβ = +38.33 × 10−3 °C/(W m−2), 95% CI [−1.32, +70.78]). We conclude that instrument-swap-induced homogeneity breaks are more likely caused by inter-instrument differences in radiative-response sensitivity than by a constant offset. This finding has important implications for climate-network homogenization and for azimuthal quality control of tower-mounted sensors.
items.authors: Lei Chu, Xinfeng Ling, Chunfeng Duan, Kaidi Zhang, Houfu Zhou, Cong Zhu

items.title: Did Congress Trade Ahead of the 2026 Iran War? Disclosure Delays and the Value of Early Entry
items.abstract: Did Congress trade ahead of the 2026 Iran War? We examine 135 disclosed transactions made by members of Congress in ten geopolitically exposed industries during the escalation. Members traded heavily in industries that subsequently rose, and congressional trading volume peaked roughly two months before public attention, but they earned no first-mover advantage. We compare portfolios that track congressional transactions at trade dates against portfolios entering at public disclosure dates. Entering positions at transaction dates offers no tangible edge: Under member-clustered inference, the disclosure delay advantage, trade timing, and any committee premium are indistinguishable from zero. Members of the Armed Services and Intelligence committees show no return edge over other members. The Senate result reduces to four trades by three senators, of which three timely oil purchases supply the bulk of the advantage. The two exceptions are purchases in positively exposed industries, which earned a 7.28% abnormal return over the disclosure window across seven members, and marginally significant sales in the negatively exposed industries. Neither can be separated from informed reading of public escalation signals. Despite intense media scrutiny of congressional trading during the escalation, we find no evidence sufficient to attribute these returns to private information.
items.authors: Florian Richard
items.category_raw: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

items.title: Microplastics as Ecological Filters Across Food Systems: From Microbial Selection and Antimicrobial Resistance to Human Health Risks and Mechanisms
items.abstract: Microplastics are increasingly detected throughout food-production systems, from agricultural soils and irrigation waters to aquaculture environments, food-processing facilities, and final food products. Beyond their role as contaminants and microbial carriers, plastic particles provide persistent surfaces for biofilm development and may selectively shape the microorganisms and functional traits that persist during environmental transport. This review introduces an ecological-filter framework for understanding how microplastics restructure microbial communities across food systems and how these processes may ultimately influence human exposure and health. We examine how polymer properties, conditioning films, weathering, environmental gradients, ecological succession, and colonization history drive plastisphere assembly and microbial turnover, with particular attention to pathogen selection, antimicrobial-resistance determinants, and horizontal gene transfer. We further distinguish three partially overlapping mechanisms through which foodborne microplastics may acquire human-health relevance: particle-mediated effects, arising from gastrointestinal interactions and changes in intestinal conditions and microbiota; chemical-mediated effects, involving compounds associated with or released from particles; and plastisphere-mediated effects, involving environmentally selected microorganisms or functional genes transferred through the food chain. Current evidence strongly supports dietary exposure, selective microbial and resistome restructuring, and several intermediate steps of biological transfer, while direct causal links between environmental plastisphere selection and human disease remain limited. We therefore propose that microplastics in food systems should be considered dynamic ecological filters and relays whose biological significance depends on their ecological history, microbial composition, functional traits, processing history, and interactions with the gastrointestinal environment. Integrating microbial ecology, multi-omics, cultivation, food-chain tracking, and mechanistic health assessment will be essential to determine when microplastic-associated ecological selection translates into meaningful human-health risk.
items.authors: Christine Gaylarde, Estefan Monteiro da Fonseca

items.title: Formulation-Dependent Physical, Mechanical, and Water-Exposure Behavior of Hemp-Based Mycelium Composites with Polymeric Additives
items.abstract: Hemp-based mycelium composites are promising bio-based materials, but their heterogeneous structure may strongly affect mechanical performance and stability under water exposure. Six hot-pressed composites based on hemp hurds and chopped hemp straw, colonized with Pleurotus ostreatus or Ganoderma applanatum, were investigated. Depending on formulation, spent coffee grounds, thermoplastic or plasticized starch, and polymeric components introduced as granules, film flakes, or poly(ε-caprolactone) meshes were incorporated. Apparent density, water absorption, dimensional changes during immersion, compression, and three-point bending were evaluated. Mean apparent density ranged from 0.69 to 0.96 g × cm−3 and showed a positive specimen-level association with maximum compressive stress within the investigated plates (Spearman’s ρ = 0.845, n = 30). Because only one plate was manufactured per formulation, the observed formulation-specific property profiles represent exploratory observations within the investigated manufactured plates rather than population-level estimates of formulation effects or manufacturing reproducibility. The highest mean maximum compressive stress was 5.7 ± 1.2 MPa, whereas the highest mean maximum flexural stress and flexural modulus were 4.6 ± 2.1 MPa and 627 ± 285 MPa, respectively. Water uptake, dimensional swelling, and retention of measurable integrity followed different formulation-dependent trends; the greatest through-thickness swelling did not necessarily correspond to the fastest loss of cohesion. Overall, density, mechanical response, water uptake, dimensional deformation, and wet-state integrity were related but distinct descriptors of material performance, highlighting the need for multi-property optimization.
items.authors: Ewa Borucinska-Parfieniuk, Małgorzata Kowalska, Madhavi H. Dalsaniya, Adrian Dubicki, Magdalena Pantol, Wojciech Grodzki

items.title: Distribution and Source of Metals in the Horizontal and Vertical Profiles, and Their Ecological Risk in the Red Sea Coast, Western Saudi Arabia
items.abstract: Metal pollution is a critical environmental challenge that endangers marine life and ecosystems worldwide. This study evaluated the metal distribution in horizontal and vertical profiles, as well as their sources in the Red Sea coast, Western Saudi Arabia, using the contamination factor (CF), ecological risk (Er) index, potential ecological risk index (RI), and multivariate statistical analysis (MSA). Seawater samples were collected from three zones (north (N = 90), middle (N = 60), and south (N = 90); total = 240) and were analyzed for 18 metals (Ag, As, Ba, Cr, Cd, Cs, Cu, Co, Ga, Mn, Ni, Pb, Rb, Se, Tl, U, V, and Zn), EC and pH. The results reveal that metals enrichments differ across zones, namely north (Cr, Zn, Ag, and U), middle (V, Mn, Co, Ga, Ba, and Pb), and south (EC, Cu, Se, and Rb) zones. In the north zone, most metals exhibited higher concentrations in the bottom layer. Horizontal distribution reveals metals’ enrichment in 30 m (Ni, Cu, and Pb) and 60 m (Cr, Zn, and Rb). In the middle zone, higher metal concentrations were observed in the bottom (Cr, Zn, Ni, Cu, Rb, and Ag) and top layers (Mn and Pb). Conversely, most metals in the south zone accumulated in the top layer (Ni, Zn, Rb, and Ba). Seawater in nearshore areas is more polluted than that 30 and 60 m offshore. The CF indicates very high to moderate contaminations in the north and middle zones. In the south zone, Se and Cu show very high contamination, while V exhibits considerable contamination. Er implies a low ecological risk for most metals, except for Cu (in the north and south zones) and Mn (in the middle zones), meaning that it poses a predictably low risk with isolated hotspots of high ecological risk. The RI results suggested that approximately 90% of the samples fell within the low ecological risk category. MSA suggested that the observed metal concentrations were potentially associated with both natural and anthropogenic sources in the study site.
items.authors: Riyadh F. Halawani, Natarajan Rajmohan, Najeeb M. Almasoudi, Ahmed Alanazi, Fahed A. Aloufi

items.title: Passive Thermal Management of Cylindrical Lithium-Ion Cells Using Additively Manufactured Polymer Housings
items.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are widely used in modern energy storage systems; however, increasing power demand makes thermal management a critical challenge, particularly for cylindrical cells operating under high discharge conditions. This study investigates the thermal behavior of cylindrical lithium-ion cells equipped with additively manufactured polymer housings produced by fused filament fabrication (FFF). PLA, PCTG, flame-retardant PLA (FG_PLA), and ASA housings were evaluated using Samsung 50S, Molicel P42A, and Reliance RS50 cells under 1C–5C discharge rates. Surface temperatures were measured at multiple locations to assess heat transfer through the housing structures. All investigated housings reduced the measured maximum cell surface temperature compared with the housing-free configuration, particularly at high discharge rates. PLA exhibited the greatest thermal buffering effect, while PCTG showed the highest estimated conductive heat-transfer rate and a more uniform temperature evolution across the housing. ASA demonstrated stable thermal behavior, with thin housings generally showing a greater measured temperature reduction than thick configurations. In contrast, flame-retardant PLA provided the smallest temperature reduction. Wall thickness influenced the transient thermal response but did not consistently result in a greater measured temperature reduction. At elevated temperatures, partial deformation of some polymer housings was observed. The results demonstrate that FFF-manufactured polymer housings can substantially modify the transient thermal response of cylindrical lithium-ion cells, while material selection and housing geometry remain key design parameters for passive thermal management applications.
items.authors: Szabolcs Kocsis Szürke, Brigitta Fruzsina Szívós, Kornél László, Illés Lőricz, Levente Eördögh

items.title: Sickle Cell Disease-Related Dating Challenges, Intimacy, and Family Planning Decisions
items.abstract: Individuals living with sickle cell disease (SCD) experience reproductive health challenges related to unpredictable pain crises and hospitalizations. However, little research has examined how SCD-related pain influences dating and reproductive decisions. This qualitative phenomenological study explored dating, reproductive health, and family-planning experiences of young adults with SCD.
