Pretrained model parameters are then transferred to edge hardware for deep feature extraction. A kernel extreme learning machine (KELM) is further adopted for fast on-site tool wear regression prediction. When validated on full-lifecycle milling vibration data collected under real machining conditions, the proposed approach achieves nearly identical prediction performance on edge devices compared with cloud-side inference while also reducing edge inference latency to 0.01–0.021 s. These results demonstrate that the presented framework can deliver accurate prediction of milling tool RUL and provide rapid response under limited edge computational resources.
items.authors: Jianliang He, Yinhao Zhang, Caihong Han, Chen Yin
items.category_raw: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing

items.title: Isolation, Identification and Genomic Characterization of Carbamazepine-Tolerant Bacteria from Contaminated Aquatic Environments
items.abstract: Pharmaceutical contamination in aquatic environments has increased interest in microorganisms able to tolerating these compounds and the mechanisms underlying their tolerance. This study isolated and characterized carbamazepine (CBZ)-tolerant bacteria from contaminated waters of the Machángara River, Quito, Ecuador, and investigated the genome of the most tolerant isolate. Isolates were characterized by morphological and biochemical analyses, and 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Tolerance to CBZ (1–50 mg L−1) was evaluated by culture-based growth measurements. CBZ1, CBZ3, CBZ6, and CBZ7 were taxonomically assigned to Enterobacter hormaechei, Paenibacillus lactis, Aeromonas hydrophila and Raoultella ornithinolytica, respectively. Among the four isolates evaluated, CBZ7 exhibited significantly higher relative growth at elevated CBZ concentrations (30–50 mg L−1) and was therefore selected for whole-genome sequencing. The CBZ7 draft genome comprised 5,671,759 bp distributed across 181 contigs, with a G+C content of 55.65%, an N50 of 79,780 bp, 98.2% BUSCO completeness, and CheckM2 estimates 0.87% contamination. Genome annotation revealed genes associated with membrane transport and efflux, oxidative metabolism, glutathione metabolism, environmental sensing, and aromatic compound metabolism. Although no complete CBZ-specific catabolic pathway was identified, the results support strong tolerance of CBZ7 to elevated CBZ concentrations and identity candidate functions potentially involved in xenobiotic adaptation.
items.authors: Gabriela Méndez, Diana Carrera, Lizbeth Olivo Silva, Elena Coyago-Cruz, Melisa Ortiz, Ivonne Vega

items.title: Science Education Research for Global Citizenship
items.abstract: Research in science education—the study of the ways in which teachers teach and students learn scientific skills and concepts across nations, disciplines, and levels of education—has a key role in supporting the preparation of the next generation of scientists who will expand our human understanding of the natural world (Sung et al [...]
items.authors: David R. Geelan

items.title: Relative Contributions of Quinolone Resistance-Determining Region Mutations and Efflux Pump-Associated Mechanisms to Fluoroquinolone Resistance in Staphylococcus aureus Clinical Isolates and Their Associations with Virulence Gene Profiles
items.abstract: Background: Fluoroquinolone resistance in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) involves multiple mechanisms, including quinolone resistance-determining region (QRDR) mutations and efflux pump activity. However, the relationship between these resistance mechanisms and virulence factors (VFs) remains unclear. This study investigated the relative contributions of QRDR mutations and carbonyl cyanide 3-chlorophenylhydrazone (CCCP)-responsive mechanisms to fluoroquinolone resistance in MRSA and their associations with VF profiles. Methods: Sixty ciprofloxacin-resistant MRSA bloodstream isolates were analyzed. The minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of ciprofloxacin (CIP) and levofloxacin (LEV) were determined before and after treatment with the efflux pump inhibitor CCCP. The isolates were classified as CCCP responsive or non-responsive based on a ≥4-fold reduction in CIP MICs. The associations of QRDR mutations in gyrA, gyrB, parC, and parE and virulence-associated genes with CCCP responsiveness were evaluated. Results: CCCP significantly reduced both CIP and LEV MICs, although changes in LEV MICs were limited to a subset of isolates. Of the 60 isolates, 15 were CCCP responsive, whereas 45 were non-responsive. The non-responsive isolates had significantly more QRDR mutations, particularly gyrA nucleotide mutations and GyrA amino acid substitutions. fnbA-positive isolates showed greater CCCP-mediated CIP MIC reductions and fewer QRDR nucleotide mutations, whereas seg-, sei-, and tst-positive isolates showed lower CCCP-mediated CIP MIC reductions and greater QRDR nucleotide mutation numbers. Conclusions: QRDR mutations and CCCP-responsive mechanisms were differentially associated with fluoroquinolone resistance phenotypes in MRSA. Their associations with distinct VF profiles suggest a potential relationship between CCCP responsiveness, QRDR mutation profiles, and the virulence genetic background of MRSA.
items.authors: Sohyeong Kim, Heechul Park, Minju Jung, Soyun Kim, Jieun Lim, Choseung Kim

items.title: Top-Hat Beam Shaping via Asymmetric Hollow-Core Anti-Resonant Fibers
items.abstract: Conventional low-loss Hollow-Core Anti-Resonant Fibers (ARFs) deliver a near-Gaussian fundamental mode profile that is suboptimal for applications favoring uniform irradiance. We show here that deliberately breaking the cladding symmetry can allow for delivering a low-loss fundamental mode with a top-hat intensity profile, with no need for mode mixing or external beam-shaping optics. By enlarging one pair of nested cladding capillaries relative to the orthogonal pair, the core is elongated and the y-polarized fundamental mode reshapes from a near-Gaussian distribution into a flat-top profile whose 90%-intensity plateau width is 104.8% wider than that of a symmetric reference fiber at λ=1μm. Full-vectorial simulations show that this plateau varies by less than 2.1% across the 900–1600 nm near-infrared guidance band, where the confinement loss falls below 1 dB/km, and that the shaping mechanism persists essentially unchanged from the visible to the mid-infrared, where the overall attenuation remains below 0.1 dB/m within the 2700–3200 nm wavelength range. These results establish a purely geometric route to broadband top-hat beam delivery in anti-resonant hollow-core fibers.
items.authors: Ahmed Adel Elsayed Saleh, Davide Riccardo Preite, Walter Belardi

items.title: Exploring Caregivers Lived Experiences in Accessing Comprehensive Cleft Care at Jimma University Medical Center: A Phenomenological Study in Southwest Ethiopia
items.abstract: Background: Orofacial clefts are one of the most common congenital anomalies worldwide. Comprehensive cleft care interventions aim to address the complex surgical, nutritional, dental, speech, audiology, and psychosocial needs of patients with clefts. While studies from other countries have identified various implementation barriers and facilitators, evidence from Ethiopia remains limited, particularly regarding caregivers’ experiences accessing comprehensive cleft care. This study explored caregivers’ lived experiences of accessing comprehensive cleft care at Jimma University Medical Center in southwestern Ethiopia. Methods: We conducted a phenomenological study at the Comprehensive Cleft Care Center of Jimma University Medical Center. Participants were purposively selected from caregivers of children with orofacial clefts who had received at least two components of comprehensive cleft care. Data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews. Data collection continued until thematic saturation was achieved. Audio recordings were transcribed verbatim, translated into English, and managed in ATLAS.ti version 7.5.18. Data were analyzed inductively using Colaizzi’s seven-step descriptive phenomenological method. Trustworthiness was enhanced through member checking, reflexive bracketing, and systematic procedures. Results: Twelve caregivers of children with orofacial clefts participated in the study. The analysis generated eight overarching themes. Participants reported limited initial awareness of cleft conditions, cultural misconceptions, stigma, emotional distress, and delayed care-seeking. Key barriers included poor referral linkages, transportation difficulties, financial constraints, and geographic inaccessibility. Participants reported that engagement with comprehensive cleft care was associated with increased knowledge, caregiving confidence and skills, and trust in healthcare providers. They also described perceived improvements in feeding, nutritional status, speech development, physical appearance, and social integration, alongside reduced stigma and increased caregiver advocacy and community awareness of cleft conditions. Conclusions: Caregivers described a transition from limited awareness of orofacial clefts, emotional distress, stigma, and challenges accessing care toward greater knowledge, confidence, trust in healthcare providers, and perceived improvements in their children’s health, functional abilities, and social participation. Persistent barriers related to poverty, transportation difficulties, referral delays, and limited community awareness remained. These findings can inform policy and program planning to strengthen comprehensive cleft care and address inequities in access to care for children with orofacial clefts and their families in similar settings in Ethiopia.
items.authors: Abiy Semunigus Dejene, Allyn Auslander, Abraham Tamirat Gizaw, Fira Abamecha Ababulgu, Elias Ali Yesuf

items.title: Effects of Nut Consumption on Body Composition: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials with Subgroup Analyses by Nut Fatty-Acid Profile
items.abstract: Background: Despite their high fat content, nut consumption is suggested to benefit body composition. However, it remains unclear whether nuts with different fatty-acid compositions affect body composition differently. This study aimed to assess the effects of monounsaturated fatty acid (MUFA)-rich and polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA)-rich nut consumption on body composition. Methods: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane, and additional sources identified 3118 articles, with 154 meeting the inclusion criteria. Subgroup analyses were conducted by nut fatty-acid composition and control diet type. Nuts were classified as MUFA-rich (MUFA:PUFA ratio ≥ 1.3) or PUFA-rich ( 1.3) based on the percentages of total fat content. Results: Although there were no effects on body mass, BMI, or waist circumference, nut consumption significantly reduced % fat mass (WMD: −0.28%, 95% CI: −0.53 to −0.02) and fat mass (WMD: −0.41 kg, 95% CI: −0.58 to −0.27) and increased % lean mass (WMD: 0.71%, 95% CI: 0.32 to 1.10). However, absolute lean mass did not change significantly. Benefits were observed only in the MUFA-rich subgroup, although subgroup differences were not significant. Both MUFA- and PUFA-rich nut consumption showed reduced total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels, while MUFA-rich nut consumption further reduced triglyceride levels. Conclusion: Nut consumption, particularly MUFA-rich nuts, can improve body composition by percentage fat mass and absolute fat mass. Consuming either MUFA-rich and PUFA-rich nuts can further improve lipid–lipoprotein profiles.
items.authors: Weili Hu, Meihan Chen, Zixi Wang, Sunhye Shin, Jung Eun Kim

items.title: β-PruNet: An Explainable, PSO-Optimized Degree-Centrality-Pruned Regularized Extreme Learning Machine for Lightweight Household Appliance Recognition
items.abstract: Accurate recognition of individual appliances from their own power consumption profiles underpins non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM), yet deep learning models often incur high computational overhead and lack operational interpretability. This study proposes a new explainable and lightweight model named β-PruNet to recognize household appliances using daily power consumption signals. The task addressed here is appliance classification from submetered profiles rather than disaggregation of an aggregate household signal, so the model is positioned as the recognition stage of a NILM pipeline. Each 24 h signal (86,400 samples) is transformed into a 720-bin ordinal pattern (OP) distribution, and the distribution is summarized by 27 statistical and spectral descriptors over 48 sliding windows. A compact class-weighted convolutional neural network extracts 128 embedding features. Drawing inspiration from collective swarm intelligence and biological synaptic pruning, a particle swarm optimization (PSO)-tuned regularized extreme learning machine (R-ELM) classifier with beta-weight centrality pruning conducts classification via a diverse softmax ensemble. On an imbalanced 18-class benchmark containing 916 daily appliance profiles, β-PruNet achieved 98.9% classification accuracy and a 97.6% macro F1-score while pruning 87.3% of hidden neurons (from 1500 to 191) without accuracy loss. Post hoc explainability analyses using SHAP, LIME, and Grad-CAM confirmed that the pruning criterion strongly correlates with Shapley feature attribution (r = 0.974). These findings indicate that integrating symbolic dynamics with bio-inspired pruning delivers a computationally efficient, highly accurate, and transparent solution suitable for edge-oriented energy management systems. The theoretical contribution is that the magnitude of a hidden unit’s learned output weights provides a usable ranking signal at no additional computational cost beyond the closed-form solution already obtained. The practical contribution is that this signal allows the classifier head to be compressed by 87.3% without a measurable loss in accuracy.
items.authors: Ömer Faruk Alçin, Muhammed Buğracan Özküçük, Muzaffer Aslan, İlhami Sel

items.title: Selective Nickel Leaching from Cu-Ni Sulfide Ores Using Deep Eutectic Solvents
items.abstract: Traditional hydrometallurgical lixiviants such as sulfuric and hydrochloric acid pose environmental and safety risks due to their corrosive and toxic nature. To advance greener extraction technologies, this study evaluated deep eutectic solvents (DESs) as potential sustainable alternatives for the selective extraction of nickel (Ni) from polymetallic sulfide ore concentrates. Three choline chloride (ChCl)-based DESs, ethaline, reline, and maline, were compared using a factorial experimental design approach. All of the DESs demonstrated selectivity for Ni, indicating their potential for targeted metal extraction with minimal co-dissolution of copper (Cu) and cobalt (Co). Ethaline achieved the highest Ni recovery of 56.3%, while maline achieved moderate Cu recovery (19.6%). The Co recoveries were low (~16%) across all solvents. Factor screening identified the pulp density as the dominant parameter influencing Ni recovery, with lower solid loading enhancing the leaching efficiency. Under optimized conditions (0.5% w/v, 600 rpm, 25 °C, 1 h), a peak Ni recovery of 59.1% was achieved, consistent with the response surface methodology (RSM) model prediction of 58.1%. The recovery ceilings below industrial benchmarks were attributed primarily to the locked nature of pentlandite ( 30% liberation), which likely restricted the reactive surface area accessible to the DES lixiviant. The study highlights the potential of ChCl-based DESs as selective, energy-efficient, and environmentally benign lixiviants for nickel extraction.
items.authors: Biki T. Kalake, Sehliselo Ndlovu, Mmilili M. Mapolelo

items.title: Rapid Consolidation and Mechanical Characterization of High-Entropy Particle-Reinforced Al-Cu-Mg Composites Through High-Frequency Induction Hot Sintering
items.abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) and refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) have received considerable attention as innovative reinforcements to replace traditional ceramics in lightweight matrices. However, understanding how different high-entropy systems interact under ultra-fast consolidation pathways remains an open challenge. This study compares conventional sintering (CS) and high-frequency induction hot sintering (HFIHS) in an Al-4.5Cu-1.5Mg matrix reinforced with AlCoCrFeNiTi (HEA) and WMoTaNbV (RHEA) particles at various concentrations, enabling a direct comparison of both reinforcement types under identical processing conditions. Results show that HFIHS achieves near-theoretical densification within minutes while restricting atomic mobility and precipitate coarsening through sustained pressure and short thermal exposure. Furthermore, the study observes a clear strengthening dependence on reinforcement content, with the HEA system exhibiting unexpectedly superior mechanical performance and load-bearing capacity compared to the RHEA. Finally, the correlations between ultra-fast sintering, phase evolution, and strengthening mechanisms are discussed, highlighting HFIHS as a promising route for developing high-strength lightweight composites.
items.authors: Sebastián Adame-Pérez, Jair Marcelo Lugo-Cuevas, Raúl Pérez-Bustamante, Xóchitl Atanacio-Sánchez, Roberto Bernal-González, José Manuel Mendoza-Duarte

items.title: Silk Web Removal Enhances the Efficacy of Beauveria bassiana Treatment Against Hyphantria cunea: Insights from Immune and Physiological Parameters
items.abstract: The construction of physical shelters represents a widespread survival strategy among insects. This study evaluated the effect of silk web removal on the efficacy of Beauveria bassiana treatment against Hyphantria cunea larvae. Results indicated that the removal of silk webs significantly increased larval mortality and enhanced conidia attachment to the larval body during B. bassiana infection. Removal of the silk web increased larval mortality from 23.06 ± 3.14% to 46.94 ± 3.20%, with the presence of the silk web thus corresponding to a 50.88% relative reduction in B. bassiana-induced mortality. Scanning electron microscopy showed that conidial deposition on the larval cuticle was 2.8-fold higher, and markedly more aggregated within cuticular folds, in web-removed larvae, indicating that the silk web substantially lowers the conidial exposure actually experienced by the larvae. This difference in conidial exposure between silk web-bearing and silk-web-removed larvae was accompanied by multi-level physiological responses in the host. Silk web removal decreased the cellular immune response of H. cunea larvae to B. bassiana, as evidenced by reduced hemocyte counts, lower encapsulation and melanization activity, and altered expression of cellular immune-related genes (e.g., Galectin-1 and PPO2). Silk web removal intensified the oxidative damage manifested by MDA and H2O2 and the cell apoptosis manifested by apoptosis regulatory genes (e.g., AIFM3 and Metacaspase-1-like), accompanied by a significant decrease in the antioxidant enzyme activity and total antioxidant capacity in B. bassiana-infected larvae. The depletion of nutrient reserves (e.g., glucose) by B. bassiana from the H. cunea larvae was exacerbated upon silk web removal. Moreover, larvae exhibited a heightened response to B. bassiana infection upon silk web removal, including upregulated expression of cuticular protein genes and humoral immunity regulators (e.g., Lebocin and Attacin), antioxidant genes, and key enzymes in the glycolytic and tricarboxylic acid cycles. Collectively, the silk web reduces the efficacy of B. bassiana treatment against H. cunea larvae; this reduction is accompanied by a markedly lower conidial load on the cuticle, together with changes in the host’s immune defense, oxidative stress, and energy metabolism.
items.authors: Hong Jiang, Peng Li, Ying Wang, Ming-Tao Tan, Ao-Ying Zhang, Shan-Chun Yan

items.title: Distinct Modes of Quantum Information Transfer in Power–Law Long-Range Spin Networks
items.abstract: We identify different regimes of quantum state transfer in long-range coupled spin-12 systems, where naturally occurring power–law interactions enable rapid, high-fidelity transfer with minimal engineering. Across a broad range of interaction profiles, from effectively nearest-neighbour coupling to Coulomb interactions, we show how long-range connectivity fundamentally reshapes the mechanisms underlying information propagation within such systems. For effectively short-range interactions, transfer follows familiar ballistic transfer dynamics: an initially localised excitation spreads across many eigenmodes concentrated within the approximately linear region of the spectrum, enabling robust wavepacket motion. In contrast, increasing long-distance interactions via lowering the power–law exponent α (α=1−2) drives a striking transformation, where the initial state becomes confined to progressively fewer eigenmodes, ultimately reducing the dynamics to the coherent participation of only a few states corresponding to the highest eigenenergies. This spectral localisation gives rise to emergent long-range oscillations between distant sites, revealing a distinct—and faster—transfer mechanism arising from the intrinsic structure of long-range quantum interactions rather than from full-system engineering pathways.
items.authors: Ellis E. Marshall, Chad C. Nelmes, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Timothy P. Spiller, Irene D’Amico

items.title: Quantum Computing in Space: Engineering Challenges, Fundamental Limits, and Perspectives
items.abstract: Quantum computer deployment in space remains constrained by demanding hardware, environmental, and communications requirements. This paper reviews the opportunities and challenges of using quantum computing in space systems. It focuses on payload integration, radiation protection, quantum-memory stability, autonomous hybrid classical–quantum control, and quantum-network performance. The work is integrative, not novel in algorithms, architecture, optimization, or experiments. It organizes reviewed literature around system-level deployment barriers and highlights open research gaps. Compared with existing reviews, this paper adds a category taxonomy, a system-level constraint framing, updated coverage, and an integration of rate–loss fundamentals. The analysis highlights the need for standardized interfaces, autonomous classical–quantum control, and evolutionary qualification of subsystems in orbit. Modular, radiation-adaptive payloads and calibration-aware classical processing are identified as important strategies for improving reliability and mission resilience. The industrial outlook indicates a gradual transition from subsystem demonstrations toward standardized, interoperable, and vertically integrated quantum-communication services, including LEO QKD constellations, space-qualified protocol stacks, and CubeSat-scale photonic devices. Readiness claims are classified using a multi-stage ladder: launch, power-on, communication, calibration, quantum operation, and peer-reviewed useful computational performance. Fully fault-tolerant quantum computing in orbit remains a longer-term objective requiring advances in logical-qubit overhead, radiation tolerance, low-power control, memory performance, and repeater architectures.

items.title: CYBA Gene Polymorphisms, Lipid Parameters and Atherogenic Indices: A Cohort Study of Healthy Individuals Without Prior Lipid-Lowering Therapy
items.abstract: Single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the CYBA gene, encoding the p22phox subunit of vascular NADPH oxidases, have been associated with atherosclerosis-related disorders. This association may partly reflect their involvement in lipid metabolism. We investigated the effects of seven CYBA SNPs (rs7195830, rs1049255, rs4673, rs13306296, rs72811418, rs16966671, and rs9932581) on systemic lipid profiles (total cholesterol, HDL-C, LDL-C, and triglycerides) and six lipid-derived atherogenic indices in 220 blood donors who had never received lipid-lowering therapy. Genotyping was performed using PCR-RFLP and TaqMan PCR. Serum lipid concentrations were determined by enzymatic colorimetric methods. For all SNPs, in silico analyses assessed allele-specific binding (ASB) of transcription factors (TFs) and gene expression in cardiovascular tissues. Statistically significant differences in lipid parameters were observed among the rs7195830, rs1049255, and rs13306296 variants. In silico analyses indicated ASB of TFs for rs1049255 and rs13306296 and genotype-dependent effects of rs13306296 and rs4673 on CYBA expression. Notably, the G allele/GG genotype of rs13306296 was associated with the least favorable lipid profile across multiple parameters, preferential binding of thirteen TFs, and increased CYBA expression in aorta and heart tissues. In conclusion, CYBA variants influence the systemic lipid profile and lipid-derived atherogenic markers in individuals untreated with lipid-lowering drugs, potentially through modulation of CYBA expression.
items.authors: Paweł Niemiec, Tomasz Nowak, Justyna Wrona, Joanna Iwanicka, Tomasz Iwanicki, Alicja Jarosz

items.title: AI-Mediated Work as Occupation: An Occupational Science Perspective on Meaning, Identity, and Justice
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming part of everyday work. Workers use it to prepare documents and evaluate information, while some may encounter it through systems that assign or assess their work. Research has examined productivity, organizational adoption, collaboration, and algorithmic management. These studies offer important evidence but tell us less about how workers experience AI as part of their daily work. In this conceptual paper, I apply occupational science to AI-mediated work. I argue that patterned and situated AI-related activity can be examined as occupation: it takes shape within workplace routines, can carry meaning for workers, and can affect their opportunities to participate. Drawing on occupational science and selected AI-at-work scholarship, I propose an analytic map with seven elements: human–AI actions, work integration, interpretive work, responsibility work, relational work, identity work, and boundary work. I consider how workplace conditions shape these elements and their consequences for workers. This perspective connects questions about AI at work with workers’ experience of what they do and what their contribution means.
items.authors: Amanda C. Jozkowski

items.title: Synthetic Cannabinoids: Metabolism, Biomarkers of Exposure and Advanced Analytical Strategies in Forensic and Clinical Toxicology
items.abstract: In the last twenty years, synthetic cannabinoid receptor agonists (SCRAs), also frequently known as synthetic cannabinoids, have grown into one of the leading and structurally diverse types of new psychoactive substances. This has brought about major trouble for clinical and forensic work. Even though there have been significant advances in the field, there remain important gaps in the understanding of the mechanism of action, biotransformation pathways, etc. Numerous studies indicate that optimized chromatographic–mass spectrometric technologies are vital for the sensitive and specific detection of SCRAs and their metabolites from complex biological matrices. Studies that employ rigorous accreditation-level protocols highlight the need for a method validation process for the reliable detection of compounds. Meanwhile, scientifically controlled studies involving humans provide information on the connection between a compound and its metabolites with the clinical effects. In parallel, metabolomic investigations suggest that SCRA metabolism is closely tied to cellular dysregulation and adverse toxicological outcomes, indicating that biotransformation can generate reactive intermediates and contribute directly to toxicity. Overall, by combining metabolite profiling, emerging biomarkers and structure-informed toxicological interpretation, the literature points toward a more integrated and predictive framework to guide future analytical strategies and support evidence-based harm reduction measures.
items.authors: Telma M. Gomes, Paula Guedes de Pinho, Ivone Nunes, José S. Câmara

items.title: More than Beauty—Edible Flowers of New Rosa × hybrida Genotypes Grown in Vojvodina (Serbia) as a Novel Source of Bioactive Compounds
items.abstract: Flowers have a long tradition of use beyond ornamental purposes, including incorporation into numerous food products. Roses stand out for their attractive colors and pleasant floral aromas, yet their nutraceutical potential remains largely underestimated. In this study, rose flowers from five new garden cultivars were evaluated for their potential use as food ingredients. Total phenolic, total flavonoid, total monomeric anthocyanin and vitamin C contents were quantified, along with quantitative analysis of 45 selected compounds by LC-MS-MS. Additionally, in vitro antioxidant, neuroprotective and hypoglycemic activities were assessed. They proved to be rich sources of polyphenols (TPC in the range of 122–240 mg GAE/g de, TFC in the range of 18.1–42.7 mg QE/g de) and vitamin C (0.24–0.31 mg/g fw), exhibiting strong antioxidant and moderate neuroprotective effects. They are weak inhibitors of α-amylase and strong inhibitors of α-glucosidase (23.7–81.6% inhibition at 2.50 μg/mL), suggesting potential benefits for managing blood sugar levels and metabolic health. Cultivar ‘Magic Aroma’ demonstrated the greatest potential for further research and incorporation into food products. Given modern consumers’ growing interest in natural and functional food ingredients, these findings highlight the untapped potential of rose flowers for innovative, health-promoting culinary uses.
items.authors: Nemanja Živanovic, Marija Lesjak, Dejan Orčić, Biljana Božanic Tanjga, Mirjana Ljubojević, Jelena Čukanović

items.title: SF-SRGAN: Shift-Free Transformer GAN with High-Frequency Enhancement for Image Super-Resolution
items.abstract: Image super-resolution refers to the process of recovering high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs. However, existing methods face three critical challenges: GAN-based approaches suffer from training instability and artifacts; shifted-window Transformers have issues of computational cost and fixed receptive fields; and high-frequency detail modeling along with multi-source feature fusion remains insufficient. To address these issues, this paper proposes SF-SRGAN, a high-frequency enhanced shift-free Transformer generative adversarial network. The generator introduces a shift-free variable-window Transformer architecture that progressively increases window sizes across layers (4 × 4 → 8 × 8 → 16 × 16), achieving natural receptive field expansion without shift operations or masking overhead. A High-Frequency Positional Encoding module is designed to extract multi-directional high-frequency responses via Laplacian kernels and adaptively inject them through a content-aware gating mechanism. An adaptive dual-path fusion mechanism dynamically integrates global Transformer features with local CNN features. The discriminator adopts a multi-scale architecture combined with R1 gradient penalty and an auxiliary edge prediction loss to stabilize adversarial training and preserve high-frequency structures. Extensive experiments on SR-CelebA and Flickr2K datasets demonstrate that SF-SRGAN achieves superior performance in PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS, and ablation studies validate the effectiveness of each component.
items.authors: Qingyu Liu, Kai Guo, Xuetao Meng, Yinyin Li

items.title: Management and Prognosis of Sustained Ventricular Tachycardia in the Emergency Department: A Retrospective, Observational, Single-Centre Study
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sustained ventricular tachycardia (VT) is a potentially life-threatening arrhythmia requiring prompt Emergency Department (ED) assessment and management. However, data on its frequency, real-world treatment, and prognosis in the ED remain limited. We aimed to describe the clinical characteristics, acute management, and short- and long-term outcomes of patients presenting with VT. Methods: We retrospectively included consecutive patients presenting to the ED between January 2018 and December 2024 with a primary diagnosis of sustained VT with a pulse. We collected baseline characteristics, hemodynamic status, underlying cardiac disease, and acute treatment. In-hospital events and 30-day and 1-year outcomes were assessed. Results: A total of 103 patients were identified, accounting for approximately 0.025% of all ED visits during the study period; 84.5% were male. Chest pain (31.1%) and palpitations (25.2%) were the most common presenting symptoms. Structural heart disease was present in 90% of the cases, predominantly of ischemic origin (61%). Nearly half of the patients (49.5%) had a prior history of VT. Electrical cardioversion was performed in 28.2% of the cases. The majority of the patients (95/103; 92%) required hospitalization. Mortality was 4.9% at 30 days and 17% at 1 year. After adjustment for age, a left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 30% and in-hospital arrhythmic recurrence were independently associated with 1-year mortality. Conclusions: Sustained VT is an uncommon but high-risk ED presentation, mainly affecting patients with ischemic structural heart disease. A discrepancy was observed between real-world clinical practice and guideline recommendations. The substantial mortality observed, particularly among patients with impaired left ventricular function or in-hospital arrhythmic recurrence, highlights the need for prompt risk stratification and optimized, guideline-concordant acute management.
items.authors: Francesco Salinaro, Pietro Begnini, Roberto Rordorf, Santi Di Pietro, Benedetta Traversi, Debora Monti

items.title: Anticholinergic Burden and Falls in Older Adults: The Role of Functional Status
items.abstract: Background: Falls are a major geriatric problem associated with functional decline, loss of independence, and increased healthcare utilization. Although anticholinergic burden and impaired functional status are recognized risk factors, their combined association with recurrent falls remains unclear. This study evaluated how anticholinergic burden and functional status relate to recurrent falls in older adults. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 347 patients aged ≥65 years who underwent comprehensive geriatric assessment. Anticholinergic burden was assessed with the Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB) score, functional status with the Barthel Index and Lawton Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL) Scale, and comorbidity with the Charlson Comorbidity Index. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed; the interaction between ACB ≥ 2 and functional impairment was also tested. Results: Recurrent falls were reported by 108 patients (31.1%). Patients with recurrent falls were older, had higher medication use, ACB scores, and comorbidity burden, and lower Barthel Index and Lawton IADL scores (all p 0.05). In univariable analyses, ACB scores of 2 and 3 were associated with increased odds of recurrent falls. In multivariable analyses, both the Barthel Index (aOR = 0.96, 95% CI: 0.94–0.98; p 0.05) and Lawton IADL score (aOR = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.87–0.96; p 0.05) remained independently associated with recurrent falls. The Barthel Index and Lawton IADL Scale showed the highest discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.75 and 0.74, respectively). Patients with Lawton IADL ≤ 19 and ACB ≥ 2 had the strongest combined association with recurrent falls (OR = 12.04, 95% CI: 5.88–24.66; p 0.05). This association remained significant after multivariable adjustment for age, sex, number of medications, and comorbidity burden (aOR = 7.93, 95% CI: 3.51–17.90; p 0.001). The interaction between ACB ≥ 2 and functional impairment was not statistically significant (p for interaction = 0.271 for the Barthel Index and 0.285 for the Lawton IADL Scale); therefore, the findings are described as joint (combined) associations rather than effect modification. Conclusions: Functional status remained independently associated with recurrent falls after adjustment for age, sex, anticholinergic burden, medication count, and comorbidity burden. In this cross-sectional study, functional impairment and higher anticholinergic burden showed a joint association with recurrent falls, without evidence of statistical interaction; longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporal and causal relationships.
items.authors: Feyza Mutlay, Murat Das

items.title: Safety and Outcomes of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Therapy in Systemic Sclerosis: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: With their success in the treatment of various malignancies, immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are quickly being established as a critical component of treatment plans in oncology. However, due to concerns regarding autoimmune flares and immune-related adverse events, patients with autoimmune disease have historically been excluded from clinical trials. While research has been slowly incorporating those with autoimmune disease, research focusing on some autoimmune diseases such as systemic sclerosis is still lacking. This scoping review aimed to characterize the safety and outcomes of immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy in patients with systemic sclerosis. A literature search conducted through PubMed, Semantic Scholar, and OpenAlex was performed through June 2026 in accordance with the PRISMA-Scoping Review guidelines. Available evidence regarding the safety of ICI therapy in patients with pre-existing systemic sclerosis remains limited and heterogeneous. Autoimmune flares and immune-related adverse events, including severe complications, have been reported, and the available data are insufficient to establish the safety or tolerability of ICIs in this population. Further prospective studies are needed to better characterize outcomes and identify factors associated with increased risk.
items.authors: Jennifer George, Michalah O’Connell, Jonathan Kruger, Hanna K. Jensen

items.title: Beyond the Parasite Metaphor: A Morphological Typology of Architectural Intervention
items.abstract: Parasitic Architecture represents a radical strategy for urban densification, yet the literature lacks a systematic morphological framework to analyze its physical relationship with the host beyond metaphorical descriptions. Addressing this theoretical gap, this study proposes an action-based analytical typology to classify these interventions. Adopting a purposive, case-based qualitative content analysis, the research examines fifteen documented cases in order to trace how each intervention physically engages its host. The findings identify five distinct morphological attachment strategies: Wedging, Perching, Clinging, Piercing, and Wrapping. These actions are synthesized into a matrix that relates the host interface to the specific spatial strategy of the parasite. Consequently, the findings indicate that these forms can be organized according to their primary morphological action in relation to the host. This study ultimately repositions the concept of the parasite from a critical metaphor into an operational grammar of architectural intervention, offering an analytical tool with potential applications in adaptive reuse and urban design.
items.authors: Anday Türkmen, Selva Başçı

items.title: Investigating Electro-Thermal Distribution in High-Capacity Large-Format Blade Batteries for Energy Storage
items.abstract: Batteries are regarded as a uniform heat source in traditional thermal management system design. Inconsistencies in electrochemical reactions across time and space are often ignored, which leads to an unreasonable battery thermal management system. This paper establishes a 2D electro-thermal fully coupled model based on the Kim model and NTGK model for a high-capacity blade battery. Based on the experimental results, the accuracy of the model was verified by examining terminal voltage, average battery temperature, and temperature distribution. The distribution characteristics of physical fields within the battery were analyzed using the electro-thermal model. The results indicated that the distribution of electrochemical reaction rates inside the battery shows a clear boundary between the near-tab area and the middle positions. In the initial stage of discharge, the electrochemical reaction rates were higher around the tabs. However, the electrochemical reaction rates were higher around the middle positions at the end stage of discharge. Thus, we proposed two schemes, a three-zone model and a five-zone model for 3D thermal analysis, according to the distribution characteristics of the physical fields. We found that the difference in the prediction accuracy of temperature distribution between the two schemes was small. Therefore, we recommended the three-zone scheme for 3D thermal analysis, considering the complexity of the operation. These conclusions could provide a reference for a refined thermal management system design of large-sized blade batteries.
items.authors: Jun Wang, Xueqin Yin, Hu Cao, Shusheng Deng, Xinyan Zhou

items.title: Microbiome-Related Amino-Acid Profiles of Liver and Muscle Tissues in Arbor Acres Broiler Chickens
items.abstract: The study, designed as a group-level integrative data analysis, included homogeneous datasets obtained from 24 Arbor Acres chicken groups. Quantitative amino-acid analysis in chicken tissues was carried out using the capillary electrophoresis method. Gut microbial community analysis was performed using 16S rRNA gene-sequencing technology on the Illumina MiSeq platform. Amino-acid analysis of liver samples revealed 10 Arg-high and 14 Arg-low chicken groups, while for thigh samples, the ratio of Arg-high and Arg-low groups was 18/6, respectively. The gut microbiomes of chickens with an Arg-high amino-acid profile showed increased Chao1 and Shannon diversity index values, defined by a significant abundance of several members of the phylum Bacillota (formerly Firmicutes), including the genera Christensenella, Eisenbergiella, Dysosmobacter, Anaerotignum, Oscillibacter, unclassified Oscillospiraceae, and Lachnospiraceae. In contrast, the gut microbial communities of chickens with low Arg content showed decreased Chao1 and an increased Shannon dominance index, which was explained by the significant abundance of the genus Alistipes belonging to the phylum Bacteroidota (formerly Bacteroidetes). Prediction of amino-acid biosynthetic pathways in chicken-gut microbiomes revealed a general trend toward increased relative abundance of most KEGG orthologs in Arg-high groups, as well as a number of positive links with Arg and Val/Leu + Ile content in liver and thigh samples.
items.authors: Dmitry Deryabin, Lyudmila Vlasenko, Ilshat Karimov, Dianna Kosyan, Shamil Rakhmatullin, Galimzhan Duskaev

items.title: Fungal Communities and Their Environmental Correlates in BSCs Under Sand-Fixing Plantations in Alpine Sandy Land
items.abstract: The fungal communities within biological soil crusts (BSCs) of alpine sandy lands remain poorly understood, particularly regarding their associations with long-term plantation restoration. Four types of sand-fixing plantations (Salix psammophila, Salix cheilophila, Caragana korshinskii, and Populus simonii) in the Gonghe Basin were chosen as study sites, and bare sand, algae crust, and moss crust samples were obtained from each plot. Soil physicochemical properties and extracellular enzyme activities were measured, and the fungal community was characterized by Illumina high-throughput sequencing of the ITS1 region. We systematically examined how key predicted guilds of fungal communities and their environmental factors changed across crust types, and characterized the differentiation of predicted guilds. Our main results are summarized below: (1) Ascomycota and Basidiomycota dominated at the phylum level, while Preussia, Alternaria, Paraphoma, and Endocarpon dominated at the genus level. (2) Moss crust had the highest fungal richness and evenness, followed by algae crust, whereas bare sand had the lowest values. Furthermore, PCoA-ANOSIM further revealed marked differences in BSC fungal community structure among the plantations. (3) Spearman’s correlation analysis, CCA, and the Mantel test indicated that the plantations were associated with fungal community differentiation through variation in edaphic physicochemical properties and extracellular enzymatic activity. Furthermore, pH, AK, and AP were associated with fungal community composition in both crust types, with ALP and SUC additionally important in algae and moss crusts, respectively. (4) FUNGuild predictions indicated that Undefined Saprotroph was the dominant predicted guild and that saprotrophy was the dominant trophic mode in the BSC fungal communities of the study area. This study revealed the fungal community composition and organization of BSCs across various crust types, and identified the factors associated with these communities in different artificial sand-fixing plantations in alpine sandy land. These findings may offer a microbiological foundation for restoring alpine sandy land ecosystems in the future.
items.authors: Xionglian Jin, Yinhua Ma, Huichun Xie, Xiaoping Kong, Jiawei Yan, Zhe Chen

items.title: Integrating Life Cycle Assessment and Techno-Economic Considerations for Sustainable Perovskite Photovoltaics: A Digital Decision-Support Framework
items.abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) represent a promising alternative to conventional crystalline silicon photovoltaics (Si PV), but their commercialization requires simultaneous consideration of environmental performance, operational lifetime, end-of-life (EoL) management, and technology-development priorities. This study develops an integrated life-cycle and decision-support assessment of PSC and Si PV systems. Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) models were developed in openLCA on a functional basis of 1 m2 of PV system, considering production, use, and EoL stages and applying ReCiPe 2016 Endpoint (H) and CML-IA Baseline. The environmental results were further integrated into a multi-criteria decision-support framework using cost-criterion normalization, Simple Additive Weighting, and scenario-based sensitivity analysis. Literature-derived techno-economic parameters provided contextual information rather than a harmonized quantitative techno-economic assessment; the Decision-Support Scores (DSS) were based exclusively on environmental indicators. In the area-based assessment, PSC exhibited substantially lower climate-related impacts than Si PV, with reductions of 57.04% for global warming–human health (ReCiPe) and 57.35% for GWP100a (CML-IA), together with 48.53–53.41% lower fossil-resource-related impacts. However, pronounced trade-offs were identified, including higher stratospheric ozone depletion (+132.50%), mineral resource scarcity (+22.06%), land use (+754.03%), photochemical oxidation (+5747.52%), and terrestrial ecotoxicity (+731.95%). Under equal weighting in the area-based assessment, Si PV achieved higher DSS for both ReCiPe (78.88 vs. 67.33) and CML-IA (67.05 vs. 62.75). The area-based sensitivity analysis showed stable ordering under all ReCiPe scenarios, whereas the CML-IA ordering reversed under climate- and resource-priority scenarios. A parallel electricity-based assessment reduced the PSC climate-related advantages to approximately 18% and yielded higher DSS values for Si PV under all scenarios and both LCIA methods. Although PSCs offer important opportunities associated with lower-energy manufacturing, their sustainable commercialization depends on extending operational lifetime, reducing material- and toxicity-related hotspots, implementing scalable and resource-efficient manufacturing, and developing effective recycling and material-recovery systems. The proposed framework demonstrates how LCA combined with multi-criteria decision support can provide a transparent basis for evaluating environmental trade-offs and guiding the sustainable development of emerging photovoltaic technologies.
items.authors: Kyriaki Kiskira, Ioannis Klinakis, Michael Papoutsidakis, Nikitas Gerolimos, Christos Drosos, Nikolaos Laskaris

items.title: Digital and AI-Supported Game-Based Interventions for Executive Function Development in Early Childhood: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Executive function (EF)—working memory, inhibitory control, and cognitive flexibility—underpins school readiness, academic achievement, and socio-emotional competence in early childhood (ages 3–8). Digital and AI-supported game-based interventions are a promising but underexamined modality for EF training. This review aimed to synthesize the reported effects of digital and AI-supported game-based interventions on executive function in children aged 3–8 years and the technological features linked to reported gains. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this systematic review synthesized 19 studies from six databases (PubMed, PsycINFO, ERIC, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore) covering January 2012–March 2026, involving 1890 children aged 4–8 years across 11 countries. Narrative synthesis indicated predominantly positive findings across all three EF components; this was observed most consistently for working memory. Adaptive difficulty calibration, immediate corrective feedback, and motivational scaffolding were the features most often linked to gains; positive findings were somewhat more frequent in school-based settings and in longer interventions, though these descriptive patterns rest on small, unbalanced subgroups and cannot establish setting or duration as moderators. Critically, the corpus was overwhelmingly conventional and rule-based: only three studies (15.8%) contained machine-learning components, with none driving pedagogical personalization (confined to gesture recognition or post hoc analysis); none employed conversational agents or affect-sensing, and no eligible study sampled 3-year-olds. Findings should therefore be read as evidence about adaptive digital game-based interventions rather than AI-driven ones. This near-absence of machine-learning personalization for typically developing children aged 3–8 years is itself a principal finding, alongside gaps in long-term retention, cross-cultural generalizability, and ethical AI data governance.
items.authors: Khawlah Alhejii

items.title: Combined Use of Sodium Bentonite and Recycled Aggregates in Concrete: Microstructural Characterization and Mechanical Performance
items.abstract: The reuse of construction and demolition waste (CDW) and supplementary aluminosilicate materials can reduce the environmental impact of concrete. This study evaluated two formulations produced with fine and coarse recycled CDW aggregates: a control with 0 wt% sodium bentonite and an experimental mixture with 5 wt% sodium bentonite as a partial Portland cement replacement (ACI 211.1-91, target 19.61 MPa at 28 days). Two independent control batches achieved 19.833 MPa (202.24 kg/cm2) and 19.788 MPa (201.78 kg/cm2) (mean 19.810 MPa, 101.01% of target). The 5 wt% bentonite mixture achieved a mean of 15.353 MPa (156.55 kg/cm2, SD 0.060 MPa, CV 0.391%, 95% CI, 15.290–15.416 MPa, n = 6), equivalent to 78.29% of the target strength and 22.50% lower than the control mean. The six specimens containing 5 wt% bentonite were technical replicates obtained from a single batch, whereas control values correspond to two independent batches (one specimen each); therefore, confidence intervals are presented descriptively. Characterization of the 5 wt% formulation at 28 days was performed by XDR, SEM, and EDS. XRD identified calcite, ettringite, quartz, and signals compatible with calcium silicate hydrate (C-S-H) products and tobermorite. SEM reveals a heterogeneous matrix with acicular morphologies compatible with C-S-H and densified regions. EDS showed O 54.8 wt%, Ca 27.8 wt%, Si 10.2 wt%, and Al 2.8 wt% with heterogeneous distribution of Ca, Si, and Al without marked segregation at the observation scale. Characterization was limited to the 5 wt% formulation at 28 days; therefore, observed phases and morphologies cannot be attributed exclusively to bentonite.
items.authors: Hugo Morales-Beltrán, Edelmira Gálvez, Eleazar Salinas-Rodríguez, Manuel Saldana, Norman Toro, María del Pilar Gutiérrez-Amador

items.title: An Integrated Processing–Performance Modeling Framework for Predicting the Effect of Curing on the Transverse Strength of Thermoset Composites
items.abstract: The mechanical properties of fiber-reinforced polymer matrix composites are strongly influenced by manufacturing processes. In particular, curing of thermoset polymer matrices introduces residual stresses that can significantly affect microscale damage initiation and the transverse strength of composite materials. This study presents an integrated processing–performance modeling framework to predict the transverse tensile strength of thermoset composites by explicitly accounting for the microstructure and curing-induced residual stress. A discrete microscale Finite Element Analysis (FEA) model based on Representative Volume Elements (RVEs) with a random fiber distribution is developed to predict curing-induced residual stress development and damage evolution under subsequent mechanical loading. The composite curing behavior is modeled using the Cure Hardening Instantaneous Linear Elastic (CHILE) model in which the resin modulus evolves monotonically with the degree of cure (DOC). Progressive damage is captured through a fracture-energy-based Smeared Crack Approach (SCA). To enable coupled curing–damage simulations, an incremental formulation of the SCA is implemented within the FEA framework to accommodate the non-zero stress state resulting from curing. To account for the inherent variability and stochastic nature of composite microstructures, a random fiber packing algorithm is employed to generate multiple fiber distribution realizations. The influences of RVE size and matrix fracture properties on the predicted transverse tensile response are systematically investigated. This work provides a fundamental building block toward understanding how manufacturing-induced effects propagate across length scales and ultimately govern the mechanical performance of composite materials.
items.authors: Sai Krishna Meka, Haotian Sun, Ryan Enos, Dianyun Zhang
items.category_raw: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing

items.title: Genome-Informed Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Assays for Detection and Differentiation of Ralstonia pseudosolanacearum Phylotypes I and III
items.abstract: The Ralstonia solanacearum species complex (RSSC) causes bacterial wilt in a broad range of economically important hosts. The RSSC has been reclassified into three species, of which R. solanacearum sequevars 1 and 2 in phylotype IIB are designated as Select Agents in the U.S. Many rapid tests for “R. solanacearum” target the RSSC and thus cross-react with R. pseudosolanacearum, which is endemic to the U.S. To avoid false positive identifications and unnecessary triggering of Select Agent measures, four portable LAMP-based screening assay variations were developed and validated for specific detection of R. pseudosolanacearum: real-time LAMP assays for detection of R. pseudosolanacearum (1) and differentiation of R. pseudosolanacearum phylotypes I and III in the AmpliFire® Isothermal Fluorometer (2) or Genie® III (3), and a colorimetric LAMP for detection of R. pseudosolanacearum (4). All assays demonstrated high sensitivity (10–50 colony-forming units (CFU)/reaction) and specificity; 100% analytical specificity and selectivity based on 177 RSSC isolates (81 phylotype I, 70 phylotype II, 15 phylotype III and 11 phylotype IV) and 53 non-RSSC bacterial pathogens on relevant hosts and soil, and 100% diagnostic specificity and sensitivity based on testing inoculated plants and a Euphresco sample panel. The assays presented here represent useful diagnostic tools that can be deployed on-site to aid domestic survey and detection efforts.
items.authors: Brijesh B. Karakkat, Qi Huang, Schyler O. Nunziata, Jarred Yasuhara-Bell

items.title: Reconfiguration of Urban Leisure Space Use During Hot Periods: Evidence from Nanjing, China
items.abstract: Overall leisure activity can conceal substantial changes in how urban leisure use is distributed across functions, time, and space during hot periods. We analysed 917,186 user–venue–day leisure visits recorded on Weibo in central Nanjing during 2023–2025. Warm-season models compared representative daily maximum temperatures of 28 °C and 37 °C, while full-year records supported within-user comparisons of destination environments. Baseline estimated daily recorded visits were 8.54% higher under sustained 37 °C conditions. This association persisted with seasonal adjustment. The share of nature-based recreation fell from 22.37% to 18.88%, while heritage and tourism gained 1.18 percentage points. Nature-based recreation shifted relatively towards morning hours, and its effective density area decreased by 5.12%. Public cultural facilities showed an 8.20% reduction in effective density area. The cluster with the lowest median relative land surface temperature was a loss cluster, showing that a cooler surface thermal background did not translate into greater relative use. Full-year within-user comparisons showed 2.75 percentage points more surrounding water and 1.60 points less tree cover at destinations recorded on days at or above 30 °C; warm-season differences were smaller, with all 95% confidence intervals including zero. Heat-adaptation planning should consider function-specific use and conditions at heavily used destinations.
items.authors: Sijie Zhu

items.title: Diagnosis of Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis at the Interface of Pathogen Detection and Host Response: Molecular, Microbiological, and Histopathological Advances
items.abstract: Extrapulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB) accounts for approximately 16% of notified tuberculosis (TB) cases worldwide and disproportionately affects children and immunocompromised populations. Paucibacillary disease, anatomically diverse sites, and nonspecific presentations make EPTB one of the most persistent diagnostic challenges in TB control. This review integrates microbiological, molecular, sequencing-based, and histopathological approaches to EPTB diagnosis within the context of site-specific immunopathology, including granuloma biology and the microenvironment of caseous necrosis. Comparative evidence is synthesized across osteoarticular, lymph node, pleural, central nervous system, and disseminated EPTB, focusing on Xpert MTB/RIF and Ultra, targeted and metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS), and emerging host-response biomarkers and AI-assisted histopathology. Pragmatic, tiered diagnostic algorithms are proposed for resource-limited settings, where most EPTB occurs, and unresolved gaps in current international guidance are identified. Aligning diagnostic modality choice with anatomical site, specimen quality, pathological subtype, and laboratory capacity can shorten the time to EPTB diagnosis and inform host-directed diagnostic strategies.
items.authors: Qibin Liu, Yuhui Jiang

items.title: Systemic Complementarities in Sustainability Transitions: Energy Governance, Transportation Efficiency, and Sustainable Competitiveness
items.abstract: Sustainability transitions are increasingly shaped by the interaction between infrastructure systems and institutional frameworks, yet empirical evidence on how these complementarities influence outcomes remains limited. This study examines the relationship between energy governance and transportation efficiency, focusing on whether their interaction generates non-linear effects on sustainability performance. Using panel data from 110 countries for 2019–2024, we employ fixed-effects models with interaction terms to evaluate both competitiveness and distributional outcomes. The results reveal three main findings. (1) We find no statistically significant evidence, at conventional levels, of a “Green Multiplier” interaction between energy governance and transportation efficiency (β = 0.0057, p = 0.102), although the available governance and infrastructure indicators are reported at a lower frequency than the annual panel employed in this study, limiting statistical power for detecting interaction effects. (2) Contrary to the hypothesized compensatory logic, ground transportation efficiency and air connectivity show a significant positive interaction (β = 0.026, p = 0.039), indicating complementarity rather than substitution between transport modes. (3) Once income is correctly controlled for, infrastructure development shows no significant direct association with access to clean energy, in either direction. These findings advance sustainability transition research by providing rigorously specified evidence on infrastructure–governance interactions, showing that some previously hypothesized complementarities do not hold at conventional significance levels. In contrast, others (ground–air transport complementarity) emerge in directions contrary to prior theoretical expectations. The results caution against inferring the governance-contingent effectiveness of green investments from associational panel evidence alone and instead point to the value of transparent, fully reproducible specification reporting in this literature.
items.authors: Wendy Anzules-Falcones, Juan Ignacio Martín-Castilla, Ana Belén Tulcanaza-Prieto, Cristina Vargas-Urresta

items.title: Unraveling Spatial Associations of Surface Subsidence in Typical Oil Production Areas of Songyuan City by Integrating Time-Series InSAR and Deep Learning
items.abstract: Oilfield subsidence threatens infrastructure and sustainable development. Although facility detection, factor-association analysis, and deformation forecasting have each advanced considerably, their systematic integration remains insufficiently explored for oilfields in agricultural plains, where C-band SAR decorrelation over cropland and wetland yields sparse and uneven deformation observations. This constraint complicates facility extraction, quantitative analysis of associations among interacting factors, and robust temporal prediction. To address these challenges, this study develops and applies an integrated modular workflow for the monitoring, analysis and prediction of surface subsidence in a typical oil production area of Songyuan City, China. We first used PS-InSAR for high-precision deformation monitoring and validated the results with leveling survey data. Subsequently, the YOLOv12 model was utilized for automated oil well identification, and the Geodetector model was applied to quantify the spatial associations between subsidence and the examined natural and anthropogenic factors. Finally, a hybrid LSTM–Transformer model was developed for time-series prediction and applied to forecast deformation through November 2025, twelve months beyond the final SAR acquisition. Results indicate significant spatial differentiation in deformation, with a maximum subsidence rate of −26.0 mm/y. Analysis identifies oil well density and surface elevation as the leading spatial factors among those examined, and the buffer zone analysis indicates a distance-related association of approximately 700 m between oil wells and subsidence rates. The hybrid model demonstrated superior overall accuracy compared to standalone LSTM and Transformer models. The findings provide concrete scientific support for risk mitigation in oil cities.
items.authors: Liyang Yin, Xinran Xu, Xinlei Huang, Fengyan Wang, Mingchang Wang, Qing Ding
