items.title: Comparative Structural Behavior of Sustainable Fibrous Voided Ferrocement Slabs Incorporating Waste Glass Powder and Different Void Formers
items.abstract: Ferrocement slabs, being lightweight and sustainable, can help in achieving resource-efficient construction by reducing material consumption while maintaining satisfactory structural performance. The flexural behavior of environmentally friendly ferrocement slabs with recycled materials and internal void-slab systems was investigated in this work. Glass powder (GP) was used to replace 15% of the cement, and the effect of polypropylene fibers (PPFs) on the mechanical and structural behavior was investigated. Eight one-way ferrocement slabs, including two solid reference slabs and six voided slabs with two longitudinal void paths formed using PVC tubes, waste plastic bottles and recycled aluminum beverage cans, were tested. Each configuration was made with and without 1% PPF. The experimental work included tests of the flow diameter, compressive and flexural strengths, load–deflection behavior, cracking pattern, failure load and displacement, and toughness. The results showed that the addition of PPFs reduced the diameter of the mortar flow from 22.0 to 17.8 mm and increased the compressive strength from 54.0 to 55.45 MPa and the flexural strength from 4.15 to 6.80 MPa. Voided slabs without PPFs showed a decrease in the ultimate load of 6.3–13.1% when compared to the solid reference slab. The ultimate load was increased by 14.8–33.6% by adding 1% PPF, and the toughness and failure displacement were increased by 51.9–89.8% and 20.9–59.7%, respectively. The recycled aluminum-can void slab showed a comparable structural response to the other void-forming materials, demonstrating its waste valorization potential and responsible material use.
items.authors: Mohammed Hmood Mohana, Sheelan Mahmoud Hama, Ziadoon Mohsin Ali, Taher A. Tawfik

items.title: Hydration-Mediated Multiscale Structural Evolution in Polyurethane Hydrogels: From Water States to Microphase Reconstruction and Dynamic Networks
items.abstract: Polyurethane (PU) hydrogels combine high water content with the intrinsic structural heterogeneity of segmented polyurethane, giving rise to strong coupling among hydration, intermolecular interactions, microphase organization, and network dynamics. This review treats hydration as an active structural variable rather than solely as a swelling medium. The effects of soft- and hard-segment chemistry and network topology on the pre-hydration state are first summarized, followed by analysis of the multiscale sequence from water uptake and water state to competitive hydrogen bonding, segmental mobility, microphase reconstruction, and dynamic-network evolution. Particular attention is paid to distinguishing hydration-induced reconstruction of pre-existing domains from water-induced microphase separation, in which hydration generates new compositional segregation or phase connectivity. Direct evidence from PU hydrogels is also distinguished from mechanistic evidence derived from related hydrated PU, polyurethane–urea, and thermoplastic PU systems. The consequences of these processes for strengthening, toughening, cyclic recovery, stimuli responsiveness, wet interfaces, and representative applications are discussed. A system-dependent hydration window is further introduced to define the conditions under which sufficient molecular mobility for reversible reorganization coexists with persistent load-bearing structures. Remaining challenges include synchronized wet-state characterization, long-term fatigue and aging, and the establishment of predictive composition–hydration–structure–property relationships.
items.authors: Li Zhang, Rongrong Zhang, Xinliang Wang, Honghong Zhang, Zhaosheng Hou

items.title: Serving Through a Crisis: Mental Health Outcomes and Their Predictors Among Filipino Civil Servants During COVID-19
items.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic precipitated a global health crisis, entailing profound disruptions to daily life that substantially affected mental health, particularly among essential workers. However, despite facing similar challenges and limited mental health resources across different occupational groups, civil servants, particularly in Southeast Asia, remain underrepresented in existing research. This study addresses that gap by exploring mental health outcomes and their associated factors among Filipino civil servants. In a sample of 572 Filipino civil servants, findings revealed elevated prevalence rates of mental health problems, with 25.9% likely exhibiting generalized anxiety disorder, 30.6% major depression, and 56.5% high psychological distress. Moreover, several sociodemographic variables and pandemic-related experiences were found to be significant risk factors of generalized anxiety, depression, and distress. These findings provide important information for developing targeted interventions to mitigate the psychological burden on this critical population during public health emergencies.
items.authors: Imelu G. Mordeno, Alex Cassandra A. Adamat, Kimberly Joy P. Daguisonan, Christine O. Mantuhac, Laira Dee A. Baroquillo, Rosnani R. Pamaybay

items.title: Visual Perception and Autonomous Navigation Control for Orchard Robots: From Scene Understanding to Closed-Loop Motion Execution
items.abstract: Autonomous navigation is essential for orchard robots performing spraying, weeding, inspection, harvesting, and transport, yet semi-structured orchards combine repeatable tree-row geometry with canopy occlusion, uneven illumination, weak road boundaries, terrain variation, and intermittent global positioning. This review examines orchard visual navigation through a control-oriented chain of scene information, perception and localization, navigation-reference construction, motion execution, and closed-loop evaluation. Particular emphasis is placed on orchard-specific interfaces: repeated row geometry can stabilize reference extraction but can also create perceptual ambiguity; canopy occlusion can simultaneously degrade visual features and GNSS availability; and headland turning requires explicit switching among row following, turning, relocalization, and task resumption. Passable areas, tree-row/canopy structure, and obstacle/end-of-row semantics are compared according to the control variables they generate, including drivable corridors, lateral and heading errors, curvature, safety clearance, event states, and tracking targets. Traditional vision, deep-learning detection and segmentation, depth vision, visual SLAM, multi-sensor fusion, and path-tracking control are synthesized in terms of operating conditions, failure modes, and downstream control effects. The review further analyzes perception-to-control error propagation, end-to-end latency, cross-season generalization, and the mismatch between image metrics and field navigation performance. A unified perception–representation–localization–planning–control–evaluation framework and full-chain benchmark protocol are presented.
items.authors: Yunfei Wang, Xiang Dong, Zhenlei Zhang, Zhihao Zhang, Weidong Jia

items.title: Real-Time Physical-to-Virtual Scene Reconstruction for Dynamic Manufacturing Systems via Semantic—Spatial Mapping
items.abstract: Real-time reconstruction of virtual scenes in response to changing physical conditions remains a challenge in manufacturing digital-twin systems. During manufacturing operations, changes in object positions, orientations, and spatial arrangements require the virtual scene to be updated to reflect the evolving physical environment. Here, we present a physical-scene-driven semantic–spatial mapping framework to support real-time scene reconstruction in dynamic manufacturing systems. The framework integrates visual object detection, point-cloud-based spatial estimation, digital asset retrieval, and virtual scene updating. A lightweight detector identifies physical objects and provides semantic information for spatial processing, while object-level point clouds are used to estimate their positions and orientations. The resulting semantic and spatial information is associated with predefined computer-aided design (CAD) models and used to update corresponding virtual objects in a Unity environment. To improve the efficiency of semantic perception, we develop SF-Lite-YOLOv8n by integrating C2f_Star, Spectral-SPPF, and Detect_Efficient. On the MVTec ITODD dataset, the detector achieves an mAP@0.5 of 0.940 with 1.98 million parameters and 6.2 GFLOPs, at a measured inference speed of 83 frames per second. In experiments involving 20 self-collected manufacturing scenes, the integrated perception and mapping pipeline achieves mean position and orientation errors of 2.7 mm and 1.9°, respectively, with a processing latency of 146 ms, excluding Unity rendering. These results demonstrate the potential of combining lightweight semantic perception and point-cloud-based spatial estimation to support the reconstruction and updating of virtual manufacturing scenes.
items.authors: Songling Tian, Jianwen Gu, Lei Pan, Xiaoqian Qi, Peng Wang, Junjun Han

items.title: MTFNet: A Lightweight Multi-Scale Time–Frequency Neural Network for Multi-Class Event Recognition in DAS-Based Perimeter Security
items.abstract: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) has emerged as a pivotal technology for perimeter security. However, existing DAS event recognition methods have inherent limitations. Single-domain modeling has limited feature representation, while conventional multi-domain fusion methods require converting one-dimensional signals into two-dimensional images. This conversion adds computational overhead and may discard part of the original phase and amplitude information. In addition, the robustness of lightweight recognizers under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions remains insufficiently examined. This paper proposes a lightweight multi-scale time–frequency network (MTFNet) for direct processing of one-dimensional DAS signals. The model adopts a parallel time–frequency dual-branch architecture. The time-domain branch utilizes a lightweight 1D Inception-ResNet variant to capture short-term impulse features and long-range temporal dependencies via multi-scale parallel convolutions and residual connections. The frequency-domain branch performs multi-scale segmented spectral analysis to extract complementary discriminative information at diverse time and frequency resolutions, followed by a lightweight attention-free fusion module for effective time–frequency feature fusion. Experimental results on a self-built dataset covering Wind, Facility Noise, Hammering, Sawing, and Walking events show that MTFNet achieves a recognition accuracy of 99.55% with 0.12 M parameters, outperforming SVM, 1D-CNN, TCN, MS 1D-CNN, CNN-BiLSTM, and attention-based multimodal fusion methods. It maintains an accuracy of 94.06% at an SNR of 0 dB, demonstrating its robustness against additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and practical engineering application potential.
items.authors: Qiankun Zhang, Yangyang Sun, Zhilong Chen, Linjian Ma, Xiaoyu Zhao, Kai Cheng

items.title: A Blind Architecture for Signal Combining in Distributed Satellite Communications
items.abstract: To meet the increasing demand for high data rates in satellite communications (SATCOM), the requirements in terms of link quality and reliability are also increasing. Reception of SATCOM signals with multiple ground stations and combining them to increase the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) provides a flexible and robust alternative to larger antenna dish sizes and higher transmit powers. In practical scenarios, the signals received at different ground stations may exhibit different time delays, phase/frequency offsets and noise powers. This might be due to movement of the satellite in low-earth orbit (LEO) and ground stations as well as temperature differences on the ground causing different thermal noise levels. When the transmitting satellite does not cooperate with the ground stations, the central signal processor, e.g., the combiner, has to blindly estimate and compensate for these impairments to achieve optimal combining gain. This paper proposes a blind combiner architecture that integrates time-delay synchronization, frequency synchronization, as well as blind diversity combining to work under practical conditions independently of the signal modulation. The architecture is evaluated in a LEO satellite overflight simulation and validated with real measurements from geostationary satellites. We further derive the theoretical requirements for the accuracy under the different impairments and how these impairments degrade the SNR at the combiner output. The proposed architecture shows a near-optimal SNR performance in both the simulation and measurement results.
items.authors: Constantin Wimmer, Marco Krondorf, Andreas Knopp, Steffen Bittner

items.title: Blue–Green Landscape Structure and Development–Terrain Coupling in Metropolitan Flood-Susceptibility Contexts: Shanghai, Tokyo, and Istanbul
items.abstract: Metropolitan flood-resilience planning requires understanding how development and blue–green landscapes intersect with low-lying terrain. This study compared flood-susceptibility contexts in Shanghai, mainland Tokyo, and Istanbul using a harmonized geospatial framework integrating 2021 land-cover and impervious-surface baselines with elevation, hydrography, surface water, 2020–2025 satellite rainfall, and administrative population data. The analysis distinguished landscape coverage, vegetation configuration, proximity to development, and development–terrain overlap. Of the impervious surface mapped for 2021, 96.31% occurred below the elevation product’s 10 m threshold in Shanghai, compared with 23.24% in Tokyo and 4.12% in Istanbul. In Tokyo, this share exceeded the metropolitan low-elevation share of 15.76%, revealing a concentration of development in lowlands obscured by citywide terrain summaries. Shanghai had less non-agricultural vegetation than Istanbul (25.15% versus 64.50%), yet greater built-up proximity to vegetation (94.27% versus 89.10% within 100 m). Despite this proximity, only 23.04% of Shanghai’s vegetation qualified as interior vegetation, compared with 79.60% in Tokyo and 82.06% in Istanbul. Within-city analysis at 2 km showed strong vegetation coverage–adjacency associations (r = 0.803–0.936), alongside substantial variation in adjacency and built-up proximity within comparable coverage bands; association directions persisted at 5 km. Shanghai’s widespread low-elevation development calls for finer differentiation of drainage and storage conditions, whereas Tokyo’s terrain contrast supports distinguishing lowland development from upland areas. Joint assessment of blue–green structure and development–terrain overlap thus provides a basis for targeting detailed drainage assessment and sustainable metropolitan landscape planning.
items.authors: Mertkan Fahrettin Tekinalp, Gülbin Çetinkale Demirkan

items.title: Air Quality and Emission Trends Following the 2021 Environmental Code Reform in Kazakhstan Across Regions and Industrial Sectors
items.abstract: The 2021 revision of the Environmental Code of the Republic of Kazakhstan was introduced to align with the World Health Organization (WHO) air quality guidelines and the national carbon neutrality strategy for 2060. The revised Code reflects a transformation of environmental governance, including the transition towards a low-carbon and climate-oriented policy framework, the tightening of air quality standards, the strengthening of environmental monitoring, the expansion of region-specific regulatory mechanisms, and increased emphasis on the implementation of Best Available Techniques (BAT). This study presents a comparative analysis of atmospheric pollutant emissions across regions and industrial sectors, including major pollutants such as PM2.5, SO2, CO, NO2, and others. The analysis considers ambient air quality indicators, pollutant composition, the chemical composition of atmospheric precipitation, regional industrial profiles, and changes observed during the reform period. The findings demonstrate substantial regional and pollutant-specific heterogeneity in air-quality dynamics. Although stationary-source emissions decreased by approximately 5–6% between 2021 and 2024, no statistically significant improvement in the assessed ambient-air indicators was identified between 2021 and 2025. Persistent high pollution levels and episodic particulate matter exceedances remained evident in several cities. These findings provide an empirical basis for further assessment of the environmental outcomes of the revised Environmental Code.
items.authors: Nurlan Mukhamediyarov, Vladimir Kolbin, Zhanat Baigazinov, Medet Aktaev, Almagul Mukhamediyarova, Azhar Tashekova
