items.title: SARS-CoV-2-Specific IgG Levels Are Inversely Associated with ACPA-Reactive Pathological and Natural Autoantibody Profiles in Residual Diagnostic Samples
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: SARS-CoV-2-specific antibody levels vary among patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs). In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), the most prevalent SARD, this is further shaped by rheumatoid factors (RFs). Attenuated post-vaccination antibody levels in RA are documented, but links to broader autoreactivity remain underexplored. We therefore examined pathological (pAAbs) and natural autoantibodies (nAAbs) in relation to SARS-CoV-2-specific IgG. Methods: A decade-long dataset (2014–2024; 73,747 patients) gave descriptive context, not the substudy population. SARS-CoV-2 IgG and nAAbs were evaluated in 200 residual specimens collected between November 2023 and February 2024. SARS-CoV-2-specific IgG was interpreted as an antiviral readout, not a protection correlate (clinical/exposure data unavailable). QuantiVac (wild-type) and Omicron BA.1 IgG were compared across ACPA-reactive (n = 44/38), anti-SSA/SSB-dominant (n = 24/22), anti-dsDNA-reactive (n = 33/32), aPL AAb-dominant (n = 15/14), and autoantibody-negative groups (n = 70/68). Results: ACPA-reactive samples showed lower antiviral IgG across both assays. After age/sex adjustment, comparator groups had 2.58–3.30-fold higher QuantiVac and 2.70–4.87-fold higher Omicron BA.1 IgG. Antiviral IgG correlated inversely with ACPA IgG (ρ to −0.474) and RF isotypes (ρ = −0.299 to −0.400). ACPA-reactive samples showed increased CS-IgM and HSP60/HSP70 IgG/IgM reactivity, which correlated positively with ACPA IgG and RF isotypes. Conclusions: In this exploratory analysis, an ACPA-reactive serological profile was associated with lower SARS-CoV-2 IgG and higher, positively correlated CS- and HSP-directed autoantibody levels, suggesting a shared rather than independent basis for these autoreactive compartments. These cross-sectional associations persisted after age/sex adjustment but cannot be separated from unmeasured clinical, treatment, or exposure factors.
items.authors: Alain Le Roux, Nancy Zeineddine, Katalin Böröcz, Dávid Szinger, Diana Simon, Ferenc Boldizsár

items.title: Kidney Outcomes in Offspring Exposed to Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: Background: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) may impair placental function and disrupt foetal nephrogenesis, increasing kidney vulnerability in offspring. However, the magnitude and phenotype-specific pattern of offspring kidney risk remain uncertain. We aimed to systematically assess the association between maternal HDP and offspring kidney outcomes. Methods: PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, Wanfang Data, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched from inception to October 2025. Cohort and case–control studies evaluating maternal HDP and offspring kidney outcomes were included. Outcomes were grouped into three final categories, including chronic kidney disease (CKD), acute kidney injury (AKI), and congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT). Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. Pooled effect estimates were derived from random-effects meta-analysis using the generic inverse variance method, prioritising the adjusted estimates. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251175714). Results: Thirty studies (20 cohort and 10 case–control studies), including 10,954,573 participants, were included. Maternal preeclampsia was associated with an increased risk of offspring CKD (pooled adjusted relative effect 1.26, 95% CI 1.16, 1.37; I2 = 0%). Although crude analysis suggested a significant association between maternal HDP and offspring CAKUT (odds ratio [OR] 1.18, 95% CI 1.07, 1.31; I2 = 18%), the pooled adjusted estimate was not significant (adjusted OR 1.07, 95% CI 0.87, 1.31; I2 = 0%). A pooled adjusted estimate for offspring AKI was not derived, as this was reported in only 2 studies with considerable population heterogeneity. The overall crude risk ratio (RR) showed no statistically significant association but substantial heterogeneity (pooled crude RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.61, 1.10; I2 = 78%). Crude AKI RRs varied by criteria: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes 0.71 (95% CI 0.55, 0.91; I2 = 51%) versus Acute Kidney Injury Network 1.09 (95% CI 0.60, 1.96; I2 = 83%). Conclusions: Maternal HDP, particularly preeclampsia, was associated with elevated risks of offspring CKD; however, the pooled adjusted estimate for CAKUT was not statistically significant. Evidence for offspring AKI remains inconclusive, providing no reliable evidence for either an increased or decreased risk. Prospective studies using harmonised definitions and robust confounding control are needed to assess these associations and determine their clinical relevance.
items.authors: Limei Xiong, Yong Zhang, Yuanxi Liao, Yao Zhang, Yanxia Mao, Tao Xiong

items.title: The E80 Microworld: A Gate-Transparent VHDL CPU and One-Click Toolchain
items.abstract: The E80 is an open-source, 8-bit, single-cycle soft processor written in VHSIC Hardware Description Language (VHDL) from gates, multiplexers, and flip-flops, without an arithmetic package. Its 39 instructions were derived from a survey of eight sources of introductory computer architecture material. A toolchain takes an assembly program to a simulation waveform with one keystroke. It includes presets for three field-programmable gate array (FPGA) boards, one of which is supported by a fully open-source flow. This extended version removes a false combinational loop from the datapath, so the design passes timing analysis on all three flows without workarounds. A serial light-emitting diode (LED) matrix mirrors the simulation signals on the board. Execution can be slowed or stepped one instruction at a time. A self-checking suite was added to test the instruction set. Two recursive programs were run on the E80 and checked against analytical predictions: a Fibonacci computation that follows Dijkstra’s method of recursive programming, and the largest program in the surveyed material, namely a maze search written for a 16-bit machine and ported in full into the E80’s memory. The effect on learning remains unmeasured.
items.authors: Panos Stokas, Vasileios Fotopoulos, Konstantinos Giannakopoulos, Anastasios Fanariotis, Minas Dasygenis

items.title: Distributed Adaptive Sliding Innovation Fixed-Lag Smoother for Maneuvering Target Tracking with Impulsive Measurement Outliers
items.abstract: Target maneuvers and impulsive measurement outliers can both produce large innovations, posing a challenge to accurate space target tracking. To address their simultaneous occurrence, this study proposes a distributed adaptive sliding innovation fixed-lag smoother based on the consensus-based cubature sliding innovation filter (CCSIF). The proposed method retains cubature-based moment propagation and consensus fusion while replacing saturation-based gain modulation with Gaussian-kernel innovation weighting. Spatial synchrony across observation satellites and temporal persistence within a reference-innovation window are constructed to characterize innovation anomalies. These complementary features drive a fuzzy inference system (FIS) that adaptively adjusts the kernel width to balance outlier suppression and maneuver responsiveness. Subsequent measurements within the window guide the update of a past state, yielding a fixed-lag smoothing scheme. Simulations involving four low-Earth-orbit satellites tracking a maneuvering high-altitude space target under impulsive measurement contamination demonstrate substantially improved position estimation. With a fixed lag of 10 steps, the proposed smoother achieves time-averaged position and velocity root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of 13.14 m and 0.1165 m/s over the final 200 s, respectively.
items.authors: Junhang Zhao, Yidi Wang, Wei Zheng, Chao Ma

items.title: Evolution of Phenolic Compounds and Antioxidant Capacity of Olive Leaf (Olea europaea L.) Remaining on Branches After Pruning
items.abstract: Olive leaves (Olea europaea L.) are an important by-product of olive pruning and oil production and a rich source of phenolic compounds with antioxidant properties. However, their post-pruning biochemical evolution when leaves remain attached to branches is poorly understood. This study evaluated the changes in phenolic composition and antioxidant capacity of Cornicabra olive leaves attached to the branches during five months after pruning under intensive and super-intensive cultivation systems. Phenolic compounds were analyzed by HPLC-DAD and antioxidant capacity was assessed using DPPH and ORAC assays. Oleuropein was the main compound, followed by verbascoside and hydroxytyrosol derivatives. Both phenolic content and antioxidant capacity showed a clear temporal decline after pruning, with maximum values occurring within the first 6–24 days. The super-intensive system consistently showed higher levels than the intensive one. Antioxidant capacity closely followed phenolic behavior, with strong positive correlations, particularly for oleuropein and hydroxytyrosol compounds. Overall, olive leaves maintain high biochemical activity shortly after pruning, and the first 2–3 weeks represent the optimal period for their valorization. These results support improved management strategies and the use of olive leaves as a sustainable source of bioactive compounds.
items.authors: Manuel Piqueras-García, Rosario Sánchez-Gómez, Nayara Iniesta-Aroca, Maria Rosario Salinas, Gonzalo L. Alonso, Cristina Cebrián-Tarancón

items.title: Dose- and Time-Dependent Effects of a Ferula communis Extract on Bone Remodelling in a Human Osteosarcoma Cell Line
items.abstract: Ferula communis is a herbaceous plant in the family Apiaceae and order Apiales. It has two chemotypes that cannot be distinguished botanically, although one is highly toxic while the other is not. The non-poisonous chemotype has many beneficial activities for human health, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, cytotoxic, antimycobacterial, antiproliferative, neuroprotective, and estrogenic properties, thanks to its numerous secondary metabolites. This manuscript evaluates the effects of a Ferula communis extract on bone remodelling in a human osteosarcoma cell line. The extract from Ferula communis (FER-E) comes from the roots of the plant and, after chemically removing toxic ferulenol, further chromatographic analysis allowed us to estimate the ferutinin content, titrated at 25%. Saos-2 cells were treated with FER-E for both short times (24, 48, and 72 h) and longer times (up to 20 days) and, at each time, three aspects were evaluated: (a) cell viability; (b) cytosolic calcium concentration; and (c) the expression of specific proteins (OPG-RANKL) related to bone remodelling. The results were encouraging, suggesting that FER-E effects were dose- and time-dependent. Furthermore, both short and prolonged treatments positively modulated bone structure maintenance. For example, treatment with FER-E for 72 h preserves osteoblastic activity, presumably at the expense of osteoclastic activity. Treatment for 12 days seems to turn off this activity. Still, surprisingly, in a time window between the thirteenth and twentieth day, the cells produce one or more late compounds, capable of returning to the extract the ability to activate osteoblastic activity again. If these findings are properly confirmed, both in vitro and in vivo, Ferula communis could be associated with the delicate mechanism of bone remodelling.
items.authors: Jessica Maiuolo, Miriam Scicchitano, Lorenza Guarnieri, Stefano Ruga, Francesca Bosco, Francesca Oppedisano

items.title: Belonging, Visibility, and Voice: Perceptions and Practices Promoting Social–Emotional Support in Online Learning in Teacher Education
items.abstract: The consolidation of online learning in higher education raises a question teacher education can no longer defer: How is social–emotional –support created when teaching and learning are mediated by screens? This study explored how preservice teachers experienced social-emotional learning (SEL) in an online course, focusing on three dimensions: belonging, visibility, and voice. Using reflexive thematic analysis within a constructivist orientation, the study analyzed the summative written reflections, composed as letters to the lecturer, of preservice teachers (N = 27) in a year-long synchronous online course at a teacher education institution. The cohort, aged 19 to 35, was heterogeneous in life circumstances, professional experience, and learning profiles. The analysis constructed four themes: belonging built through structured relational rituals; visibility as pedagogical noticing across the screen; voice as graduated, chosen participation; and the intended translation of experienced online SEL (O-SEL) into a professional toolbox for inclusive teaching. The findings indicate that the online space is double-edged: it heightens the risks of invisibility and disconnection, yet its affordances, written channels, structured formats, and learner control over self-presentation, can deepen inclusion when deliberately designed. Because the letters were addressed to the lecturer–researcher, the findings are read as situated accounts of perceived support and intended practice rather than as evidence of effectiveness or of classroom implementation. The discussion links the findings to systemic and transformative SEL and online disinhibition theory, and proposes a practice architecture for preparing teachers for inclusive classrooms.
items.authors: Noam Lapidot-Lefler

items.title: 4-(5-((1E,3E)-4-(benzo[d][1,3]dioxol-5-yl)buta-1,3-dien-1-yl)-1,3,4-oxadiazol-2-yl)aniline
items.abstract: This research aimed to develop a new semisynthetic piperine compound derived from black pepper (Piper nigrum, Piperaceae), commonly known as “King of Spices”. Piperine was isolated from the ethanolic extract of Piper nigrum by the Soxhlet extraction method. In this, 5(2E,4E)-5-(benzo[d][1,3]dioxol-5-yl)-1-(piperidin-1-yl)penta-2,4-dien-1-one (Piperine) is used as a starting material to form (2E,4E)-5-(benzo[d][1,3]dioxol-5-yl)penta-2,4-dienoic acid (2). After that, ethyl (2E,4E)-5-(benzo[d][1,3]dioxol-5-yl)penta-2,4-dienoate (3) will be formed by the esterification process. The (2E,4E)-5-(benzo[d][1,3]dioxol-5-yl)penta-2,4-dienehydrazide (4) was formed by using hydrazine and ethanol. In the final step, the hydrazide was reacted with p-aminobenzoic acid to form 4-(5-((1E,3E)-4-(benzo[d][1,3]dioxol-5-yl)buta-1,3-dien-1-yl)-1,3,4-oxadiazol-2-yl)aniline (5). The novel synthesized compound was characterized by IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and mass spectroscopy.
items.authors: Salahuddin, Vimal Datt, Rajnish Kumar, Avijit Mazumder, Kavita Rana, Mohamed Jawed Ahsan

items.title: Lose the Hardware: The Rise of Leadless Modular Cardiac Pacing
items.abstract: Leadless pacemakers have reshaped the approach to cardiac pacing by eliminating transvenous leads and subcutaneous pockets. Since the introduction of the first leadless pacemakers, leadless pacing has advanced from single-chamber ventricular systems to atrioventricular synchronous pacing, standalone atrial pacing, and fully leadless dual-chamber platforms, enabling patient-tailored pacing therapy. The modular leadless pacing concept allows a standalone leadless pacing device to be implanted initially, with additional leadless devices added sequentially as pacing requirements evolve, minimizing unnecessary hardware while preserving the option for future pacing upgrades. This modular approach has expanded to include integration with subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillators and leadless cardiac resynchronization therapy, moving towards a fully leadless cardiac rhythm management ecosystem. This review summarizes the evolution of leadless pacing, compares currently available devices and their clinical applications, explains leadless pacemaker implantation and end-of-life management, and explores the modular leadless pacing concept as the foundation for future fully leadless cardiac rhythm management.
items.authors: Mohamad Al-Mir, Mikhael F. El-Chami

items.title: Hydrogel-Based Delivery Systems for Targeted Probiotic Release and Colonization: From Design Principles to Health Outcomes
items.abstract: Probiotics exert profound health benefits via the modulation of the intestinal microbiota. However, the efficacy of orally administered probiotics is severely constrained by a cascade of physiological barriers, including gastric acid inactivation, suboptimal intestinal release, and inadequate mucosal colonization. In response to these challenges, hydrogel-based delivery platforms have garnered considerable interest as versatile carriers capable of providing protective encapsulation, enabling spatiotemporally controlled release, and augmenting intestinal retention. This narrative review presents recent progress in the design and application of hydrogel-based oral delivery systems tailored for targeted probiotic release and effective colonization. First, the key gastrointestinal obstacles to successful probiotic delivery are delineated. Hydrogel design parameters are then critically appraised, with particular emphasis on material selection and network design. The underlying release mechanisms are subsequently examined. These encompass pH-responsive, enzyme-triggered, and inflammation-responsive modalities. Emerging colonization-enhancing strategies are discussed in detail. These include mucoadhesive hydrogel architectures and the nascent paradigm of “living hydrogels” functioning as dynamic bioreactors. The translational potential of these systems for health management is illustrated through applications in inflammatory bowel disease, colorectal cancer, and gut–brain axis modulation. Finally, key challenges in manufacturing, viability, and translational feasibility are evaluated. These include regulatory, safety, and encapsulation-related constraints. To address these, multi-responsive platforms, machine learning-assisted design, and synbiotic hydrogels are proposed. These hydrogels synergize with probiotics to target dysbiosis and repair mucosal damage for improved gastrointestinal health management.
items.authors: Wenjia Yan, Haichuan Shi, Hao Wang, Shanshan Xu, Zhuochen Wang

items.title: Expansion of the Field Practice Experience Scales (FPE-DK) to a Long Form to Improve Targeting to the Student Teacher Population
items.abstract: Targeting measurement scales to the intended population is important to maximize the information gained. The Field Practice Experience scales (FPE-DK) measure student teachers’ opportunities to learn through the observation of other teachers, own practice, and receiving feedback on 12 key teaching activities while in field practice placements during teacher education. While the three scales have previously been shown to fit pure Rasch models, they were not well targeted to the population. The present study aimed to improve the targeting of the three scales of the FPE-DK by adding more difficult items. The study used Rasch and graphical log-linear Rasch models for item analysis of field practice experience data of 307 Danish student teachers collected with the FPE-DK-long immediately after having completed a field practice placement. The three expanded scales did not fit pure Rasch models, as had been the case in previous research. Instead, each of the three proposed long scales had to be divided into two subscales: one set of seventeen items measuring opportunities to learn through observation and own practice, respectively, receiving feedback with regard to instruction-related practices; and one set of eight items measuring opportunities to learn through observation and own practice, respectively, receiving feedback with regard to collaboration-related practices. The six subscales fitted graphical log-linear Rasch models with some locally dependent items and some items functioning differentially, and targeting was improved compared with the FPE-DK short form. The findings provided an improved measurement instrument and advanced our knowledge of differences in opportunities to learn through observation, own practice, and receiving feedback over the course of teacher education.
items.authors: Tine Nielsen, Beate Headley, Gitte Larsen

items.title: Genome-Wide Identification and Characterization of the Rboh Gene Family in Populus trichocarpa Reveals PtrRbohB Positively Regulates Adventitious Root Development
items.abstract: Adventitious roots (ARs) are essential for clonal vegetative propagation of woody tree species. Extensive studies have focused on phytohormone and transcription factor regulatory networks during AR development in poplar, yet the regulatory roles of reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling during AR development remain poorly understood. In this study, we performed a genome-wide identification and systematic characterization of the Respiratory Burst Oxidase Homolog (Rboh) gene family in Populus trichocarpa. A total of 10 PtrRbohs were identified and phylogenetically classified into five subfamilies. Expression profiling revealed distinct tissue-specific and stress-responsive expression patterns among PtrRbohs. Functional validation via CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout showed that disruption of PtrRbohB significantly reduced AR length, diameter, and lateral root density in poplar. Heterologous overexpression of PtrRbohB in Arabidopsis thaliana enhanced ROS accumulation, confirming its conserved function in ROS generation. Furthermore, knockout of PtrRohB down-regulated the expression of several AR-positive regulators and up-regulated that of AR-negative regulators in poplar. Collectively, this study provides the direct genetic evidence that Rboh regulates AR formation in poplar, and identifies PtrRbohB as a key positive regulator of AR development. These findings enrich our understanding of woody plant AR formation and provide candidate genes for molecular breeding of poplar rooting traits.
items.authors: Run Shi, Yanping Ding, Peng Guo, Fude Shang, Shenquan Cao

items.title: Wine at the Table: Food Pairing, Occasion, and Sensory Discourse in an Online Enthusiast Community
items.abstract: Wine is a food-cultural product: it is chosen for meals, paired with dishes, opened for special occasions, and discussed in a shared language of taste. Yet most research on how consumers experience wine relies on controlled tastings or product-centred rating platforms that abstract wine away from the table. We use the Reddit community r/wine as a longitudinal corpus of spontaneous, unprompted wine conversation (66,081 submissions, 2012–2025) and read it as a record of wine’s place in food culture. Using a curated lexicon of ten thematic categories, we quantify the prevalence of culinary, social and sensory themes, reconstruct food–wine and occasion–wine associations from co-mention, trace their evolution over fourteen years, and map the structure of the discourse with a co-occurrence network, community detection and PageRank centrality. Culinary and social themes are among the most prevalent in the corpus; the food–wine associations that emerge from consumer discussion closely reproduce established pairing conventions; occasion-specific choices reflect shared cultural scripts; and food, style and occasion form a single structural community. Sensory description did not increase steadily across the period; instead it rose sharply and significantly in the most recent years (2023–2025), in both prevalence and network centrality. Reddit thus allows wine talk to be observed at scale, as it occurs unprompted, within an Anglophone online enthusiast community.
items.authors: Efstathios Kaloudis, Eleni Naziri

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Approaches for Insurance Claim Analytics in Synthetic Environments
items.abstract: Insurance claim analytics is often constrained by limited access to real-world data, which restricts the evaluation of advanced artificial intelligence approaches in practical insurance settings. Leveraging the SynthETIC framework, this study systematically evaluates classical actuarial models, neural-network-based methods, generative adversarial networks, and reinforcement learning for three core components of insurance claim processes: claim severity, incremental payments, and settlement delays. GAN-based data augmentation is implemented using task-specific architectures, including a tabular GAN for claim severity, an LSTM-based sequence GAN for incremental payments, and a conditional Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty for settlement delays, while Proximal Policy Optimization provides a sequential decision-learning framework for claim processes. Experimental results show that the performance of data-driven approaches is task-dependent, with GAN-based data augmentation improving some predictive measures but not consistently across all tasks and evaluation metrics. PPO-based reinforcement learning is more sensitive to task formulation and model design, reflecting the importance of action-space specification and reward structures. Additional experiments and mathematical analysis further examine the role of task-specific constraints in sequential payment allocation and delay prediction, highlighting the importance of admissible actions, state representation, and reward design. Overall, the findings illustrate how synthetic insurance environments can support the systematic evaluation of emerging AI paradigms and provide methodological insights into the task-dependent roles of GAN-based data augmentation and reinforcement learning in insurance claim analytics.
items.authors: Zeyuan Li, Qingdao Huang

items.title: An Efficient Error-Controlled POD Reduced-Order Collocation Spectral Method for Unsteady Incompressible Navier–Stokes Equations
items.abstract: The efficient numerical solution of the unsteady incompressible Navier–Stokes equations requires a balance between computational accuracy and efficiency. Although spectral methods provide high-order spatial approximation, the dense algebraic systems generated by their global discretization lead to relatively high computational costs. To address this issue, a POD-based reduced-order collocation spectral method is developed in this paper. First, a nonlinear collocation spectral method (NCSM) is constructed using the projection method and Chebyshev collocation discretization. An SVD-based linearization is then introduced to obtain a linearized collocation spectral method (LCSM) compatible with POD reduction. Based on snapshots generated by the LCSM, a reduced-order collocation spectral method (ROCSM) is further established. Error estimates are derived for the full-order discretization, linearization, and POD reduction, and a residual-based criterion is introduced to guide the selection and updating of the POD basis. Numerical experiments on a body-force-driven multimode vortex flow and an unsteady lid-driven cavity flow verify the theoretical error estimates and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The ROCSM accurately reproduces the principal flow structures while substantially reducing the computational cost. Moreover, the results show that the POD-basis updating strategy guided by the POD reduction error effectively prevents error accumulation in long-time simulations. These results confirm that the proposed method provides an accurate and efficient approach for unsteady incompressible Navier–Stokes flows.
items.authors: Yige Xu, Shiju Jin, Mingzhou Yu, Mei Huang

items.title: Associations Between Types of Physical Activity and Mental Health Among Korean Adolescents: A Cross-Sectional Study Using Data from the 21st Korea Youth Risk Behavior Survey (2025)
items.abstract: Adolescence is critical for developing physical activity habits and maintaining mental health. Using data from the 21st Korea Youth Risk Behavior Survey (2025), this cross-sectional study examined the associations between physical activity and mental health in Korean adolescents. The sample included 52,618 middle and high school students. Physical activity included ≥60 min/day of physical activity, vigorous physical activity, muscle-strengthening exercise, active transportation, and physical education class participation. Mental health indicators included stress perception, depressive symptoms, suicidal ideation, suicide plans, and suicide attempts; stress perception was examined descriptively, whereas depressive symptoms and suicide-related indicators were evaluated as outcomes in the multivariable analyses. Analyses accounted for the complex survey design, including sampling weights, stratification, and clustering. Survey-adjusted tests and complex-sample multivariable logistic regression were performed, adjusting for sex, grade, academic achievement, household economic status, living arrangement, and weight status. Vigorous physical activity and physical education participation were significantly associated with all four mental health outcomes. Compared with no vigorous physical activity, participation on 1–2 days was associated with lower odds of suicidal ideation (aOR = 0.875, 95% CI: 0.811–0.944), suicide plans (aOR = 0.810, 95% CI: 0.720–0.912), and suicide attempts (aOR = 0.803, 95% CI: 0.688–0.937). Physical education twice per week was associated with lower odds of all four outcomes (aORs = 0.737–0.927). In contrast, several frequency categories of ≥60 min/day of physical activity and muscle-strengthening exercise were associated with higher odds of depressive symptoms. These findings suggest that associations between physical activity and mental health vary by activity type and mental health outcomes.
items.authors: Sung-Ho Hwang, Su-Yeon Roh, Geun-Kook Kim

items.title: The Nuances of Cost-Related Medication Non-Adherence in Patients Receiving Immunosuppression Compared to Patients with Chronic Disease: A Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Background: Medication adherence rates across diseases that require immunosuppression, including autoimmune diseases, are low. While cost barriers affect medication adherence, it is unknown whether adherence rates related to cost barriers differ between medically immunosuppressed patients and similar patients with other chronic diseases. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the influence of immunosuppression on cost-related medication non-adherence (CRMNA). Methods: We performed a cross-sectional study utilizing the National Health Interview Survey (NHIS). Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between immunosuppression and CRMNA, accounting for sex, age, education, race, income, life satisfaction, insurance status and marital status. Predicted probabilities of CRMNA were estimated by age group, and a subgroup analysis was performed among people who described as having poor health. Results: In our unweighted sample of 17,394 adults, 54.3% were female, 12.8% self-identified as Black, 35.2% were publicly insured (Medicare and/or Medicaid), and 11.1% were below the federal poverty level. The prevalence of reporting CRMNA was 11% for patients with chronic diseases and no immunosuppression, 12.5% for patients with immunosuppression but no chronic disease, and 19.1% for patients with chronic disease and immunosuppression. In the multivariable model, participants with medical immunosuppression and chronic diseases were more likely to report CRMNA than participants with chronic diseases but no immunosuppression (OR 1.55, 95% CI [1.24, 1.94], p = 0.001). Participants with medical immunosuppression but no chronic disease did not differ significantly from the group with chronic diseases and no immunosuppression (OR 0.87, 95% CI [0.60, 1.29], p = 0.49). The predicted probability of CRMNA was highest for 30–49-year-old immunosuppressed individuals with one or more chronic diseases at 23%. CRMNA was similarly associated with immunosuppression status in patients with poor health. Conclusions: Medically immunosuppressed individuals with chronic disease experience greater CRMNA than individuals with chronic disease who are not immunosuppressed, particularly among individuals 30–49 years of age. Future studies aimed at reducing CRMNA in immunosuppressed individuals may consider interventions that target the role of chronic health conditions in non-adherence.
items.authors: Samuel D. Good, Bryant R. England, Elizabeth R. Volkmann

items.title: Brazilian Red Propolis Extract-Loaded Colloidal Systems Derived from Microemulsion Compositions: Physicochemical, Antioxidant, and Antileishmanial Properties
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Brazilian red propolis is a rich source of isoflavonoids with promising antioxidant and antileishmanial activities. However, its poor aqueous solubility and chemical instability limit its pharmaceutical application. This study aimed to develop microemulsion-based systems containing high concentrations of Brazilian red propolis extract (RPE) and evaluate their physicochemical properties, phytochemical composition, antioxidant capacity, and antileishmanial activity. Methods: Pseudoternary phase diagrams were constructed by water titration to select suitable microemulsion compositions. RPE was subsequently incorporated into the selected compositions to obtain RPE-loaded colloidal systems. The three selected RPE-free microemulsions and their corresponding RPE-loaded systems were characterized by pH, electrical conductivity, dynamic light scattering, rheological measurements, and polarized light microscopy (PLM). The RPE-loaded systems were further evaluated for phenolic marker content, antioxidant activity, and in vitro activity against Leishmania infantum. Results: Three RPE-loaded colloidal systems (F2-RPE12, F3-RPE30, and F4-RPE50) were developed. F2-RPE12 exhibited characteristics consistent with an oil-in-water microemulsion. Conductivity and PLM indicated physicochemical changes after RPE incorporation in F3-RPE30 and F4-RPE50, with localized birefringent features at higher RPE concentrations. Among the RPE-loaded systems, F4-RPE50 showed the highest phenolic and flavonoid contents and antioxidant activity. The RPE-loaded systems exhibited lower IC50 values than RPE alone, with IC50 values of 3.14, 2.28, and 0.56 µg·mL−1 for F2-RPE12, F3-RPE30, and F4-RPE50, respectively, compared with 5.90 µg·mL−1 for RPE. Conclusions: Overall, F4-RPE50 showed the most favorable phytochemical and biological performance, and the physicochemical and optical changes observed in the RPE-loaded systems open new avenues for investigating the relationship between structural organization and formulation performance.
items.authors: Salvana P. M. Costa, Ighor C. Barreto, Kathylen V. F. dos Santos, Nataly C. S. Gama, Monique A. Vila Nova, Victor Hugo V. Sarmento

items.title: BASG: A Behavior-Augmented Semantic Generalization Framework for Zero-Shot Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation
items.abstract: Training sequential recommenders for interaction-disjoint target domains is challenging: no target interaction data are available for training, model selection, or calibration. Semantic item representations support transfer across non-overlapping catalogs but do not encode query-local temporal signals or interaction-derived properties such as popularity and co-occurrence. We propose BASG (Behavior-Augmented Semantic Generalization), a backbone-compatible framework combining a source-trained semantic scorer with a separately trained Behavior Expert via a common candidate-score interface. The expert integrates query-local temporal features with popularity- and co-occurrence-related proxies predicted from frozen item-text embeddings by source-fitted mappers. Static Fusion standardizes and combines the two score vectors using a source-selected coefficient fixed during target evaluation. Catalog-level text representations and transferred property proxies are precomputed offline and reused at inference, without target-side calibration or aggregate target-domain statistics. Across three semantic backbones and three target domains including the cross-platform Steam dataset, BASG improves mean NDCG@10 by 0.43–1.68 percentage points in all nine backbone–target settings. In SAGERec-based analyses on the two Amazon targets, the interaction-property channel shows the larger removal effect, while source-calibrated Static Fusion transfers more reliably than the tested source-trained routers. These results support BASG as a strategy for integrating transferable behavioral evidence under a strict zero-shot protocol.
items.authors: Zihao Pan, Peilun Li, Yue Li

items.title: Recent Advances in Cold-Sprayed Aluminum Alloy 7075 Metal Matrix Composite Coatings: Surface Engineering, Feedstock Design, Post-Processing Strategies, and Emerging Applications
items.abstract: Cold spray technology has emerged as a transformative solid-state processing route for fabricating high-performance metal matrix composite (MMC) coatings, particularly for lightweight, high-strength aluminum alloy 7075 (AA7075). This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in cold-sprayed AA7075-based MMC coatings, focusing on critical aspects such as surface engineering, powder feedstock design, post-deposition treatments, and reinforcement strategies. The integration of hard ceramic and nanostructured reinforcements, including B4C, SiC, boron nitride nanoplatelets or tubes (BNNPs/BNNTs), and graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs), has improved the mechanical strength, wear resistance, and corrosion behavior of these coatings. Special emphasis is placed on functionally graded architectures, hybrid reinforcement systems, and densification methods such as heat treatment and hot isostatic pressing. The review also highlights emerging applications in aerospace, defense, and space technologies, including radiation shielding, structural repair, and metallization of polymer substrates. Remaining challenges, such as reinforcement dispersion, interface integrity, and process optimization, are discussed, along with future research directions involving machine learning, real-time diagnostics, and environmental validation. Overall, this review provides an integrated understanding of the processing, microstructure, properties, and applications of cold-sprayed AA7075-based MMC coatings and identifies key research gaps and future directions.
items.authors: Achyuth Kulkarni, Troy Y. Ansell
items.category_raw: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing

items.title: ClaimArena-LLM: Auditing Adversarial Propagation of False Causal Attributions in Multi-Agent LLM Debates
items.abstract: Background: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems increasingly rely on structured interaction, debate, and final model-based evaluation, yet an unsupported causal attribution introduced by one participant may propagate through the interaction and influence subsequent decisions. This study introduces ClaimArena-LLM, a controlled framework for auditing adversarial propagation, evidentiary provenance, and final-stage evaluator vulnerability in multi-agent causal reasoning. Methods: ClaimArena-LLM uses 100 synthetic causal incident cases with predefined evidence-supported and false causal propositions. Each case was evaluated under matched adversarial and all-honest debate conditions using four functional roles: investigator, honest analyst, adversarial analyst, and auditor. The experimental program comprised 1460 validated runs, including the 200-run main experiment, claim-source lineage visibility and debate-round ablations, an 800-run balanced model–role rotation, and a 60-run proposition-identifier and presentation-order sensitivity control. Outcomes were scored deterministically from structured causal propositions, evidence references, claim lineage, reports, and auditor verdicts. Results: The adversarial analyst maintained the predefined false causal target with 97.6% mean fidelity. Adversarial exposure increased investigator shifts toward the false target by 16.0 percentage points (Holm-adjusted p = 0.035). At the auditor stage, false-target attribution increased by 11.0 percentage points (adjusted p = 0.043), verdict contamination by 20.0 percentage points (adjusted p = 0.002), and semantic provenance validity decreased by 20.0 percentage points (adjusted p = 0.002). Neither the manipulation nor the false target was explicitly detected. The ablations showed no robust adjusted differences, model–role rotation revealed substantial configuration dependence, and no benchmark-characteristic interaction remained significant after Holm correction. The proposition-identifier and presentation-order sensitivity control showed no statistically robust evidence that fixed proposition encoding explained the observed condition contrasts. Conclusions: Adversarial causal influence in multi-agent LLM systems is selective rather than uniformly propagative and depends strongly on functional role and model–role configuration. Within the tested architecture, a final LLM auditor cannot be assumed to provide an independent safeguard against upstream contamination. Reliable evaluation therefore requires separate assessment of causal correctness, propagation, semantic provenance, and final-stage adversarial awareness rather than reliance on final answer accuracy alone.
items.authors: Catalin Anghel, Andreea Alexandra Anghel, Antonio Stefan Balau, Marian Viorel Craciun, Adina Cocu, Simona Moldovanu

items.title: Dual-Indicator Imaging Characterization of Luster in Chinese Freshwater Nucleated Pearls: Surface Luminance and Interference Color
items.abstract: Pearl luster is commonly assessed by expert visual grading, which is subjective and may show limited interlaboratory reproducibility. We developed a dual-indicator imaging method for Chinese freshwater nucleated pearls using surface luminance and interference color. Ninety pearls visually classified as weak-, medium-, or strong-luster were measured by multi-view luminance imaging and interference-color imaging. A background-corrected brightness index (GL) was derived from peak luminance, background luminance, and full width at half maximum, while an interference color index (IGI) was calculated from standardized hue and chroma dispersion in the upper interference-color region. GL showed a strong association with expert luster grade, whereas IGI also exhibited a significant positive relationship and provided complementary information for samples that were difficult to classify from GL alone. In leave-one-out cross-validation, combining GL and IGI improved classification accuracy from 73.3% for GL alone to 78.9%, and inclusion of a GL×IGI interaction further increased accuracy to 80.0%. These results indicate that surface-reflection intensity is the primary determinant of perceived pearl luster, while interference-color variation provides secondary diagnostic information. The proposed dual-indicator framework may therefore serve as an objective complement to conventional expert grading.
items.authors: Mingzhu Liu, Zhonghua Song, Huacai Chen, Jing Bao, Peiquan Yuan

items.title: Factors Associated with Adults’ Decisions to Undergo Rhinoplasty in Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Background and objective: The growing global popularity of rhinoplasty underscores the need to better understand public opinions and choices about the procedure. This study examines how acceptance of cosmetic surgery, concerns about nose appearance, and peer influence are associated with the decision to consider rhinoplasty among Saudi adults. Methods: This cross-sectional study of 1591 participants used a self-administered online questionnaire. Data on considering or undergoing rhinoplasty, sociodemographic characteristics, and whether friends or family members had undergone the surgery were collected. The Acceptance of Cosmetic Surgery Scale (ACSS) and nose-related appearance concern scale were used. Perceived reasons for and against considering rhinoplasty, as well as perceived seriousness of postoperative complications, were examined. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS v27. Results: The mean age was 35.7 ± 13.2 years, with a majority being females (70%). Of the 1591 participants, 74% were not considering rhinoplasty, while 26% were considering the procedure or had already undergone it. The most common perceived reason for undergoing rhinoplasty was to enhance appearance, while religious concerns were the most common perceived reason for refusing it. Participants identified the mismatch between the nose and the face (20.1%) as the most serious complication. The ACSS was a key factor associated with higher odds of considering rhinoplasty at all stages, from exploring options to undergoing surgery. During the exploration stage, those with financial constraints were more likely to explore rhinoplasty options, whereas wealthier participants were 67% less likely to do so (OR = 0.33, 95% CI: 0.16–0.71). Greater nose concerns and having a peer who had undergone surgery increased the odds of exploration and preparation. Older age was associated with higher odds of not considering rhinoplasty (OR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.03–1.19). Being female was linked to higher odds of undergoing rhinoplasty (OR = 7.76, 95% CI: 1.73–34.75). Conclusions: More than a quarter of the sample was willing to or had already undergone rhinoplasty. Factors associated with higher odds of considering rhinoplasty included female gender, young age, limited financial resources, having a friend or family member who had the surgery, concerns about nose appearance, and the acceptance of cosmetic surgery in general.
items.authors: Rasha Doumi, Abdulrahman Alhumaizi, Reem Abdullah Alfulayj, Lujain Rafa Alamri, Haifa Ali Alamro, Rahaf Saleh Alshahrani

items.title: Physics-Guided Graph Safe Reinforcement Learning for High-Fidelity and Scalable Alternating Current Optimal Power Flow
items.abstract: The alternating current (AC) optimal power flow (AC-OPF) problem is crucial for efficient power system operation, yet it remains challenging due to its nonlinear, nonconvex structure and numerous operational constraints. This paper introduces a Physics-guided Graph Safe Reinforcement Learning (PGSRL) framework that provides accurate, scalable, and physically consistent solutions to AC-OPF. The proposed PGSRL framework first models the power system as a weighted graph, encoding voltage magnitudes, load demands, and transmission line impedances to capture existing spatiotemporal correlations among power system buses. A Graph Mamba encoder with selective State Space Modeling extracts spatiotemporal correlations, which are used to define the system states within a constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP). To solve this CMDP, we design a physics-guided safe Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) architecture containing twin critics and deterministic actors, guided by physics-informed reward functions that promote feasibility through penalty-based soft constraints. By interacting with a simulated power system environment, the introduced PGSRL learns optimal generator dispatch strategies in continuous action spaces while honoring AC-OPF constraints. Experimental results on six test benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of PGSRL compared with traditional numerical solution and supervised data-driven baselines, rather than RL methods, in terms of estimation accuracy of AC-OPF setpoints.
items.authors: Yash Pratap Singh, Mohsen Saffari, Arash Asrari

items.title: Comparing Temporal Averaging and Transformer Encoders for Video-Based Cattle Behavior Classification Under Severe Class Imbalance
items.abstract: Automated cattle behavior monitoring from video is challenging due to severe class imbalance and the need for efficient temporal modeling. We compared four architectures on 542 videos containing standing, lying down, and rumination; rumination appeared only six times, while two dataset classes were absent. ResNet-50 and EfficientNet-B3 backbones were paired with either a Transformer encoder or temporal averaging and trained with three-fold stratified cross-validation and weighted cross-entropy. EfficientNet-B3 with temporal averaging (Eff-B3 + Avg) achieved the highest out-of-fold accuracy (85.61%) and best calibration (ECE = 0.074), while requiring 41 MB and 28 ms per video. Its Transformer counterpart scored 84.13% despite four times more parameters. ResNet-50 + Transformer reached 84.69% but was poorly calibrated and storage-intensive. Frame ablation identified 16 frames per video as the best accuracy-speed trade-off. No model correctly classified any rumination example, underscoring that rumination was not learnable under the specific weighted-cross-entropy and stratified-sampling strategies evaluated here; this finding does not establish a general impossibility of learning extremely underrepresented behaviors under alternative training strategies such as focal loss, oversampling, anomaly detection, or self-supervised pre-training. Rare-class analysis, treating support ≤106 as rare, showed high-confidence rumination errors: mean confidence was 0.891, but only 1.01% of probability mass was assigned to the true class, yielding a class-wise expected calibration error of 0.891. These findings indicate that calibration post-processing cannot rescue a class with zero true positives.
items.authors: Daniyar Pirlepesov Maratovich, Dae-Yeong Kang, Mohammad Ismail, Usama Hanif, Seong-hun Kim, Dasanayaka Lekamalage Vindya Sathsarani Dasanayaka

items.title: DEPGEMAN: A Conceptual Framework Integrating Energy Management and Physical-Asset Maintenance for the Life-Cycle Governance of Positive Energy Districts
items.abstract: Positive Energy Districts (PEDs) are increasingly promoted as the operational unit of urban decarbonisation, yet the literature rarely addresses how the equipment that generates, stores and distributes the district’s renewable surplus is kept reliable, available and maintainable over its lifespan. This paper addresses that gap with DEPGEMAN, a qualitative–quantitative conceptual model that aligns energy management with physical-asset maintenance across the life cycle of the PED infrastructure. The model is grounded in Toulmin’s argumentation scheme, a bibliometric analysis of Scopus and Web of Science, and three international standards, ISO 50001, ISO 55000:2024 and UNE-EN 17485:2023, and is operationalised through an Evaluate–Analyse–Correct–Verify (EACV) cycle. An explicit energy balance, four balanced phase indices and a new Integrated Energy Sustainability Index for Positive Energy Districts (IISE-PED) translate the model into measurable management practice. The framework is demonstrated on a parametrised archetype of the Zorrozaurre positive energy district (Bilbao, Spain). Moving from preventive and predictive maintenance to a reactive approach lowers system availability from 99.05% to 86.82%, raises grid purchases from 17 to 237 MWh/year for the same useful demand, and drives the IISE-PED from 0.98 to 0.33 without changing any social, tariff or behavioural input. It is worth noting that the district’s sustainability performance thereby becomes an auditable consequence of its asset-management regime.
items.authors: Víctor Martín Pérez Moreno, Tony Castillo-Calzadilla, Henry José Espinoza Bejarano, Carlos Quesada-Granja

items.title: Redesigned Electricity Institutions with Micro-Nodal Competitive Markets Reduce Electricity Costs Substantially and Induce Dynamic Energy Innovation
items.abstract: The electricity grid is a collective good that tends toward monopoly. It links private electricity generation to private electricity use. Its institutions converged near-globally at the end of the 20th century. Large-scale producers have separated ownership from transmission system operators. Quasi-markets link them. New challenges and opportunities render that design obsolete. Solar and wind energy are low-cost but intermittent. Decentralized secondary electricity is also becoming low-cost. Fast switches enable real-time adjustments in electricity production and use. Low-cost High-Voltage-Direct-Current lines centralize while also enabling decentralized frequency control. These centralizing and decentralizing options do not fit the currently fragmented markets-and-grids. Their integrated redesign is due, globally. Design elements include: a multi-layered meshed grid; multiple independent grid nodes; market rules that prohibit ownership of multiple linked nodes; real-time nodal pricing; equal prices for all purchasers at a node; and automatic equilibrium across nodes and the entire grid. The new driving mechanisms improve the electricity system’s efficiency and resilience, contributing to several SDGs. They include a single real-time integrated market, car batteries replacing in-grid batteries, and system expansion linked to low-cost renewables. Cost-reduction estimates are high in North America and Northeastern Asia, and are extremely high in Western Europe-Mediterranean, which is very fragmented.
items.authors: Gjalt Huppes

items.title: A Digital Twin Framework for Monitoring and Fault Identification of Marine Internal Combustion Engines
items.abstract: Monitoring the current technical condition of a marine internal combustion engine and diagnosing the causes of deviations of its operating parameters from reference values are important tasks for ensuring the efficient and safe operation of marine power plants and vessels in general. This study develops a digital twin framework for marine engine diagnostics and demonstrates its integration with the DEPAS 5.0W diagnostic system. The framework combines a calibrated 0D–1D engine-process model, sensor-based identification of the current operating mode, reference-state generation, and inverse identification of physical factors responsible for deviations from expected engine behavior. The mathematical model is adapted for digital twin operation through operating-mode-dependent parameterization, including a modified fuel-injection approximation. A four-factor constrained factorial numerical experiment with second-order response-surface models is used to investigate the inverse diagnostic problem. The approach is demonstrated first using virtual marine engines and subsequently using experimentally acquired data from a Weichai WP4 diesel generator with a controlled intake restriction introduced by a throttle valve. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework supports the identification of the most probable physical cause of the observed deviation when multiple potential fault factors are considered. At the same time, the results reveal the practical non-uniqueness of the inverse problem, as different factor combinations may produce similar observable engine responses. The Mahalanobis distance is shown to provide improved fault discrimination in the investigated case compared with individual pressure-based objective functions. The proposed architecture provides a basis for further development of automated digital twin-assisted diagnostics, including systematic uncertainty and identifiability analysis and validation under controlled faults.
items.authors: Dmytro Minchev, Roman Varbanets, Yurii Kucherenko, Pavlo Bratchenko

items.title: Testing Carbon-Input Feasibility in RothC Using Paired Soil Resampling over a 20-Year Interval in a Semi-Arid Steppe
items.abstract: Long-term soil organic carbon (SOC) monitoring provides a rare opportunity to test the performance of process-based models against real data. We evaluated RothC using 20 georeferenced soil profiles sampled in 2004 and 2024 in the semi-arid steppe of Central Kazakhstan. We used the 2004 SOC stocks for equilibrium initialization, whereas independently measured 2024 stocks were used for endpoint evaluation. A baseline-conditioned, endpoint-uncalibrated forward simulation (S1) was driven by profile-specific climate, NPP-scaled plant-C inputs, vegetation cover, and reconstructed management; a constrained inverse analysis (S2) estimated the non-negative effective C-input multiplier required to reproduce the observed endpoint, and a zero-input simulation (S3) defined the lower feasibility boundary. S1 preserved the broad between-profile variation in absolute 2024 SOC stocks (R2 = 0.692), but agreement for the observed 2004–2024 SOC change was negligible (R2 0.001; Lin’s CCC = 0.002). The direction of SOC change was reproduced at 9 of the 20 profiles, with an RMSE of 12.49 Mg C ha−1 and a mean bias of −4.41 Mg C ha−1. We obtained physically admissible inverse solutions for 17 profiles, with Mrequired ranging from 0.42 to 4.62 (mean = 2.04; median = 1.96). Profiles 295, 299, and 313 remained below the zero-input boundary under all management-timing scenarios. Together, these results show that adjusting plant-C input can reconcile modeled and observed SOC at most profiles. However, no non-negative adjustment of plant-C input could reproduce some observed endpoints. These cases indicate that other processes or sources of uncertainty should be considered.
items.authors: Azamat Yershibul, Zhassulan Smanov, Eleanor Milne, Guillermo Peralta, Konstantin Pachikin, Kanat Kulymbet

items.title: Dracocephalum moldavica and Nepeta racemosa Essential Oils: A Review of Chemical Composition, Biological Activities, and Anti-Helicobacter pylori Potential
items.abstract: Dracocephalum moldavica and Nepeta racemosa essential oils (DMEO and NREO) are under-studied Lamiaceae oils whose major constituents—citral-type monoterpenes and nepetalactones, respectively—have been independently associated with antibacterial and anti-Helicobacter pylori activity; however, the literature on both oils remains fragmented. This comprehensive narrative review, based on a structured search of Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed, and Google Scholar (2016–2026), integrates 78 publications on their chemical composition, antioxidant and antibacterial activities, mechanisms of action, applications, and toxicological profiles. DMEO is dominated by oxygenated monoterpenes, chiefly geranyl acetate, geranial, neral, and geraniol, and exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, generally stronger against Gram-positive bacteria, whereas its antioxidant activity is weaker than that of synthetic standards. NREO composition is markedly chemotype-dependent, ranging from nepetalactone-dominant to 1,8-cineole- or citral-rich profiles, and direct bioactivity and toxicity data remain scarce. Overall, DMEO has a considerably stronger evidence base than NREO, and safety conclusions for both oils rely largely on data for major constituents rather than on whole-oil testing. The main limitations, namely methodological heterogeneity and the absence of direct anti-H. pylori data, define the research priorities: MIC/MBC testing of chemically characterized oils against reference and clinical H. pylori strains, antibiotic synergy, gastric cytotoxicity, and in vivo validation.
items.authors: Oana M. Grigor, Carmen R. Pop, Alina L. Nistor, Rodica Vârban, Ileana C. Nicoară, Liana C. Salanţă

items.title: Rural Higher Education as Misrecognition: Reconstructing the Agrarian University from Latin America
items.abstract: This concept paper reconstructs the public agrarian university as an institutional configuration of recognition and reads the rural–urban gap at the threshold of higher education as one material expression of it. The reconstruction runs from Hegel’s assignment of the agricultural estate to immediate ethical life, through the developmentalist reception of classical sociology, to Honneth’s spheres of recognition, Fraser’s institutionalized status hierarchies, and a Latin American rural sociology in which the peasant appears as knowledge-producer; it is anchored by an abductive diagnosis of published indicators. Across six Latin American countries with heterogeneous redistributive regimes, the rural–urban gap in secondary completion narrowed between 2010 and 2022, while the residential attendance gap at ages 20–24, an imperfect proxy for tertiary participation, converged more slowly in five of the six and not at all in three; the difference between the two trends is significant in every country except Chile. In Colombia, rural secondary completion rose by 20.6 percentage points while rural attendance at these ages rose by less than one. The patterns do not identify a causal mechanism; they delimit resource-based, Bourdieusian, capabilities, selection-based, and compositional accounts rather than refute them, and the paper states what would disconfirm its diagnosis. Three contributions follow. First, the non-reporting of rural origin in the higher education information systems is argued to be institutional misrecognition rather than a resource constraint: the same state records peasant self-identification in four statistical operations, the enrolment file records forty-one attributes of the student, and none is territorial origin, and the omission forecloses accountability for inequalities in admission, persistence, and graduation. Second, epistemic reciprocity is offered as the criterion of curricular reform. Third, the framework identifies reform sites and observable success criteria that resource-based accounts do not reach.
items.authors: Mónica Yadira Dotor-Robayo, Carlos Mario Zuluaga-Domínguez, Alejandro Pérez y Soto Domínguez

items.title: Nighttime Light and Thermal Environment Jointly Affect Urban Vegetation Phenology
items.abstract: Rapid urbanization has significantly impacted plant growth rhythms through increased surface temperatures and enhanced artificial light at night (ALAN). However, the effects of thermal environments and ALAN on urban vegetation phenology (UVP) remain unclear, limiting our knowledge of how plant growth responds to urbanization and climate change. This study employed high-resolution multi-source data to assess the changing characteristics of the start of the growing season (SOS) and the end of the growing season (EOS) along the urban–rural gradient in Shenyang City. The structural equation model (SEM) and the accumulated local effect model were employed to determine the combined effects and thresholds of thermal environments and ALAN on UVP. We found that the nighttime light duration is associated with delayed autumn vegetation phenology in urban areas. In addition to land surface temperature (standardized path effect, β = 0.41, p 0.05), the nighttime light duration (β = 0.27, p 0.05) and intensity (β = 0.05) were key factors influencing EOS. The impact of nighttime light duration on phenology exhibited distinct seasonal variations, with a significantly greater impact on EOS (β = 0.27, p 0.05) than on SOS (β = 0.14, p 0.05). This might be related to vegetation’s carbon assimilation capacity and its reaction to climate change. These drivers exhibited complex nonlinear relationships with UVP, and the same driver also displayed distinct variation patterns with SOS and EOS. Our findings indicate that nighttime light duration is an important associated factor of plant growth, with great significance for predicting vegetation dynamics under rapid urbanization.
items.authors: Guangliang Jia, Yakai Lei, Jiayi Lin, Pingyang Han, Yuanman Hu, Chunlin Li

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Computer Vision for Food Inspection: From Validated Measurements to Process Control
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence-enabled computer vision can increase the frequency and spatial coverage of food inspection, but high predictive accuracy does not establish reliable production decisions. This critical narrative review examines the evidence connecting image measurements with grading, rejection, and process control. Representative studies across produce, grains and nuts, meat and seafood, microbiology, and packaging are compared by sensing modality, reference endpoint, validation unit, and operational action. The synthesis distinguishes visible quality from specific hazards, prepared defects from natural variation, and image-level performance from verified product outcomes. An author-proposed evidence map organizes analytical feasibility, independent-sample testing, operational challenges, external transfer, and prospective impact as partly independent dimensions. It is unvalidated and is not a readiness score or regulatory standard. Task-dependent reporting considerations address uncertainty, prevalence, false rejection, and abstention. Safety-related uses require separate hazard-specific validation, sampling, and acceptance criteria. Process integration additionally requires acquisition-to-actuation testing, accepted-product verification, and controlled updates. The purposive evidence base cannot establish field-wide effectiveness or rank modalities. Research priorities include traceable datasets, mechanistic challenges, and prospective intervention studies. Progress toward closed-loop control should be judged by stable measurements and demonstrated effects on defined product and process outcomes within a stated operating domain.
items.authors: Na Xu, Yi Lu

items.title: Tax Avoidance and Corporate Governance: Mapping the Intellectual Structure, Emerging Trends, and Future Research Frontiers
items.abstract: In spite of a considerable amount of attention being paid to the interaction between tax avoidance and corporate governance across the globe, this study aims to provide a detailed bibliometric evaluation concerning the productivity, performance, and intellectual structure of scientific production on tax avoidance and corporate governance. All data used in this study were gathered from the Scopus database using documents published from 2006 to 2025, which made the total number of documents reach 295. In this study, both VOSviewer and Biblioshiny were used to conduct a bibliometric analysis of this corpus. The findings of this research revealed a remarkable annual increase in publication rate equal to 25.77%, showing an increasing trend in academic research concerning the role of corporate governance in shaping corporate tax avoidance behavior. The most productive journals that have been identified as the main sources are Accounting and Finance, Journal of Corporate Finance, Journal of risk and financial management and Cogent Business and Management. Moreover, Richardson G. and Taylor G. have been found to be the most productive authors in terms of the number of documents published in this field, whereas China, Indonesia, and the USA are the leading countries in terms of the number of affiliated documents. There are seven major clusters discovered based on co-occurrence analysis, among which corporate governance and tax avoidance emerge as the most powerful driving forces. The trending-topics analysis further highlighted that board-gender diversity, CEO compensation and agency problems are the keywords emerging most recently in the field.
items.authors: Kaoutar Lahrari, Siham Sahbani
items.category_raw: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

items.title: 4-(3,5-Dimethoxyphenyl)-3,4-dihydrobenzo[4,5]imidazo[1,2-a][1,3,5]triazin-2-amine
items.abstract: A new fused triazinobenzimidazole derivative, 4-(3,5-dimethoxyphenyl)-3,4-dihydrobenzo[4,5]imidazo[1,2-a][1,3,5]triazin-2-amine, was synthesized via one-step cyclocondensation reaction. The target compound was obtained in good yield and characterized by 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and HRMS. This work expands the library of aryl-substituted 3,4-dihydrobenzo[4,5]imidazo[1,2-a][1,3,5]triazines, a class of fused nitrogen-containing heterocycles of interest in medicinal chemistry.
items.authors: Kameliya Anichina, Nikolai Georgiev

items.title: Initial Orbit Determination of Low-Earth-Orbiting Objects Using Multi-Site Space-Based Optical Observations
items.abstract: Space Situational Awareness (SSA) is a growing field of study which provides knowledge of Resident Space Objects (RSOs) to help maintain a safe and sustainable space environment around Earth. A primary component of SSA is obtaining Initial Orbit Determinations (IODs) of these objects via optical observations. The present way of obtaining optical observations is by using a single observation site. However, using only one observation site does not yield accurate range or IOD results. This research tests space-based single-site and multi-site observations of RSOs in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) to provide the necessary information to calculate IODs. Gooding’s algorithm is used to calculate IODs from the simulated data, since it is the most robust IOD algorithm discussed in the literature. The results from this research demonstrate that selected multi-site observations produce more accurate range and IOD results than single-site observations and, thus, provide advancement opportunities for various SSA efforts.
items.authors: Marianna Veltri, Vithurshan Suthakar, Regina S. K. Lee
